title: 5001: human race, the
content: Human beings are the high point of God's creation. They alone are created in his image. As a result of sin they are alienated from God and from one another, and are unable by themselves to alter this situation. The salvation of humanity rests totally upon the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ, received by grace through faith.

title: 5002: human race, and creation
content:
Although the human race is the pinnacle of God's creative work, it shares the inherent limitations of the physical realm. Human beings are nevertheless given responsibility to manage and steward the world.

The human race is an integral part of the physical creation

The human race was created from the ground

GEN 2:7 The Hebrew word for man, “adam” sounds like the Hebrew word for ground “adamah”. See also GEN 3:17–3:19; JOB 10:8–10:9; PSA 103:13–103:14

The human race was created on the same day as the animals

GEN 1:24–1:27

The human race was created from dust like the animals

GEN 2:7, GEN 2:19

The human race is set apart from the rest of creation

The human race is uniquely created in God's image

GEN 5:1–5:2 See also GEN 1:26–1:27, GEN 9:6; JAS 3:9

The human race is given authority to take care of creation

GEN 1:26–1:28 See also GEN 2:15, GEN 9:1–9:3; PSA 8:3–8:8; HEB 2:5–2:8

The human race is created with the power of choice

GEN 2:16–2:17 See also GEN 2:19

Human beings are created accountable to God for their actions

MAT 12:36 See also EZK 18:20; JHN 3:18–3:19; ROM 2:14–2:15; REV 2:23

title: 5008: conscience
content: An innate ability to discern the difference between right and wrong, which Scripture describes as having its origin in God himself.

title: 5009: conscience, nature of
content:
The faculty, given to every individual, that is capable of producing guilt, or reassurance in the case of innocence. Though never wholly reliable, the conscience is cleansed when the individual turns to God for forgiveness. It is possible for the conscience to become deadened through lack of use.

The natural conscience

ROM 2:14–2:15 Human beings have a built-in ability to know what is right and wrong.

Guilty consciences

title: 5010: conscience, matters of
content:
Scripture gives guidance on matters of conscience, particularly in cases where believers may reach different conclusions on certain matters of moral or spiritual choice.

Having a right attitude to Christians with different opinions

Consciences may differ

ROM 14:2

Different conscientious decisions must not be condemned

ROM 14:1 The gospel dispenses believers from all prohibitions concerning food. Those who are strong in faith realise this, and joyfully accept this liberty. Yet others are hindered from accepting this, on account of scruples about food inherited from their past life. Paul asks those with a clearer grasp of the gospel to respect anyone whose “faith is weak”, so that, in their own time, they may come to share the fulness of the liberty of the children of God. See also ROM 14:10, ROM 14:13; 1CO 10:29–10:30

God accepts and supports people who reach different conscientious decisions

ROM 14:3–14:4

God alone must judge whether decisions of the conscience are right or wrong

ROM 14:12–14:13 See also COL 2:16

Decision-making

Decisions should honour Jesus Christ

ROM 14:6 See also ROM 14:7–14:9, ROM 14:22; 1CO 10:31; COL 2:20–2:23

Decisions should arise from convictions

ROM 14:5 See also ROM 14:23

Decisions should be based on good doctrine

1CO 10:25–10:26

Consideration of others

Regard for another's position

1CO 10:23–10:24 See also ROM 14:14

Restraint of freedom for the sake of another

1CO 8:9 “The weak” are Christians who have yet to grasp the full implications of the gospel. At this stage, they are likely to be scandalised by the full public exercise of Christian freedom on the part of those who are more mature in their faith. Paul's advice is to respect the sensitivities of the weak, and wait for these fellow believers to become spiritually mature. Paul is not suggesting that Christians should cease to exercise the liberty of faith. Rather, he is asking for pastoral sensitivity. See also ROM 14:15, ROM 14:19–14:21, ROM 15:1–15:3; 1CO 8:10–8:13, 1CO 10:27–10:29

content: A vital bodily organ. The term is used in Scripture of the inner life of God or a person. The entire inner person, though fallen, may be changed by the Holy Spirit, in which case it should show evidence of renewal.

content: Scripture declares that human nature was created by God in his image and likeness, and set above all other creatures.

PSA 116:7 The Hebrew and Greek words for “soul” are translated in various ways by the NIV, including “breath” and “life”. It refers chiefly to the principle of life. See also MRK 8:35–8:37; LUK 1:46; 1PE 1:9, 1PE 2:11

The spirit

JAS 2:26 The Hebrew and Greek words for “spirit” are translated in various ways by the NIV, including “breath”, “heart” and “mind”. It often refers to the identity-giving aspect of human nature. See also JOB 34:14; PSA 77:3, PSA 142:3; MAT 26:41; LUK 8:55; ACT 7:59; ROM 8:16; HEB 4:12

The flesh

JER 17:5 The Hebrew and Greek words for “flesh” are translated in various ways by the NIV, including “body”, “flesh” and “human nature”. The term can refer specifically to the frailty of human nature or to human nature in opposition to God. See also GEN 6:3; JOB 10:4; PSA 78:39; MAT 26:41; PHP 3:3–3:5

Human nature became corrupted by sin

Sin has its origins in the disobedience of Adam and Eve

GEN 2:16, GEN 3:1–3:6; ; ROM 5:12–5:19; ; 2CO 11:3; ; 1TI 2:14; ; JAS 1:13–1:15

Sin affects human nature universally

ISA 64:6 See also JOB 25:4; JER 17:9; JHN 3:19; ROM 3:23

Human nature is trapped in its sinful condition

ROM 7:24 See also GEN 6:5; JHN 8:34–8:36; ROM 6:16–6:17, ROM 7:5; EPH 2:3; 2PE 2:18–2:19

Sin hardens human nature

1SA 6:6 See also EXO 8:15, EXO 8:32; PSA 95:8; PRO 28:14; HEB 3:8, HEB 3:15, HEB 4:7

Human nature is mortal on account of sin

ROM 5:12, ROM 8:10 See also GEN 6:5–6:7; JOB 14:1–14:5; 1CO 15:22; 2CO 5:1; 2TI 1:10

Human nature can be redeemed through Jesus Christ

Jesus Christ took human nature upon himself

JHN 1:14

Jesus Christ mediated between God and humanity in his human nature

1TI 2:3–2:6 See also HEB 8:6, HEB 9:15; 1JN 2:1

Jesus Christ makes possible the reversal of Adam's disobedience

ROM 5:19 See also ROM 5:12–5:17

Jesus Christ makes possible a sharing in God's nature

2PE 1:4

title: 5021: humanity, of Jesus Christ
content: See 2033: Jesus Christ, humanity of

title: 5023: image of God
content:
Humanity is created in the image or likeness of God. This image of God, given in creation, was damaged in the fall, but may be restored through Jesus Christ.

Humanity created in God's image

GEN 1:26–1:27 Image and likeness are probably synonymous terms in Hebrew parallelism. No physical likeness between God and humanity is intended. See also GEN 5:1–5:2

Paul implies that the divine image is associated in the first place with men

Although Paul at points seems to imply that the image of God is especially associated with males, he does not imply that this involves male supremacy: 1CO 11:7, 1CO 11:11–11:12

Respect for human life in God's image

GEN 9:6; JAS 3:9

The divine image implies partnership with God in the stewardship of creation

GEN 1:26 See also PSA 8:3–8:8

The divine image includes imitating God's love and justice

MAT 5:48 See also DEU 10:17–10:19

The image of God disfigured, though not totally destroyed, in the fall

ROM 3:23

Fallen humanity in contention with creation

See also GEN 3:17–3:19

Fallen humanity and the exploitation of nature

DEU 22:6–22:7; ; ISA 7:23–7:25

Jesus Christ the image of God

PHP 2:6; COL 1:15 See also 2CO 4:4

He is the exact representation of God

HEB 1:3

He reveals God

JHN 1:18

Jesus Christ is the perfect human being

JHN 1:4 See also JHN 1:9, JHN 1:14; PHP 2:7; HEB 2:17

Restoration of the divine image through Jesus Christ

The divine image is renewed in all who are united with him by faith

ROM 8:29 See also 2CO 3:18; EPH 1:13–1:14, EPH 4:22–4:24; COL 3:9–3:10

The promise of complete restoration in the future

1CO 15:49; 1JN 3:2 See also 1CO 15:42, 1CO 15:45–15:48; PHP 3:21

The Christian life as a process of transformation

2CO 3:18

title: 5024: inner being
content:
The deepest aspects of human nature, known completely by God, to be contrasted with the outward appearance or public image of a person.

The contrast of the inner being with the outward person

The desires of the inner being

ROM 7:14–7:25 See also PSA 51:3–51:6

The inner being is not subject to physical constraints

2CO 4:7–4:18

The inner being should take priority over the outward person

1PE 3:3–3:4 See also 1SA 16:7; EPH 3:16–3:19

title: 5025: killing
content:
Depriving another person or animal of life, usually by physical force. Scripture identifies various types of killing. While forbidding murder, killing of human beings is permitted in the form of execution and war. Animals may be killed for food or sacrifice, provided that the blood is ritually disposed of.

Murder

Murder prohibited by the sixth commandment

EXO 20:13 parallel DEU 5:17

Murder prohibited from the time of Noah

See also GEN 9:5–9:6; LEV 17:11

The life of the murderer is forfeit

GEN 9:6

Judicial killing

Judicial killing permitted for capital crimes

EXO 21:12 See also EXO 22:18–22:20; DEU 17:8–17:13, DEU 21:18–21:21, DEU 22:21–22:27

Executed criminals are under the curse of God

DEU 21:23

Unintentional killing (manslaughter)

The accidental killing of a fellow human being

EXO 21:13 See also DEU 4:41–4:42

The provision of cities of refuge to avoid blood revenge

DEU 19:2–19:13 Blood revenge, based on Ge 9:6, refers to the judicial revenge of a family or clan against a man who accidentally kills one of their members.

Killing in war

Killing in a holy war

JOS 6:17, JOS 6:21

Killing in other wars

DEU 20:10–20:15

The killing of animals

Regulations for disposal of blood

LEV 17:3–17:7, LEV 17:11

Animals may be killed at a distance from the sanctuary

DEU 12:15–12:16

Limitations on the killing of animals

DEU 22:6–22:7 This limitation appears to be an attempt to preserve the balance of nature.

title: 5026: knowledge
content: A state of awareness and understanding, resulting from information which has been obtained or revealed concerning people or objects. Scripture stresses God's total knowledge of his creation and also the importance of his people knowing his will and purposes for them.

resource.label: 5028: knowledge, God as source of human

title: 5027: knowledge, God's of humanity
content:
God knows all people comprehensively, their nature, their deeds and their thoughts. He understands every aspect of their lives, past, present and future.

God knows all people

1KI 8:39 parallel 2CH 6:30 See also JOB 34:21; PSA 7:9; JER 17:10, JER 23:24, JER 32:19; ACT 1:24

God knows his own people

2TI 2:19 See also 1CO 8:3; GAL 4:9

He knows them by name

ISA 43:1 See also EXO 33:17; ISA 45:3–45:4

He knows them individually and intimately

JER 1:5 See also PSA 119:168, PSA 139:1–139:16; 1CO 13:12

He knows their needs and troubles

MAT 6:31–6:32 See also PSA 34:15, PSA 142:3; JER 18:23; MAT 6:7–6:8

He knows their sin

HEB 4:13 See also ISA 48:8; JER 29:23; HOS 5:3; AMO 5:12

The knowledge of Jesus Christ

He knows all people

JHN 2:25 See also MAT 12:25 parallel LUK 11:17; MRK 2:8 parallels MAT 9:4, LUK 5:22

He knows them by name

JHN 10:3 See also JHN 10:14

He knows their needs and troubles

REV 2:9 See also REV 2:13

He knows their sins

REV 3:15–3:16 See also REV 3:1–3:2

He knows their past and future

JHN 4:16–4:18 See also JHN 1:47, JHN 4:39MAT 26:33–26:34 parallels MRK 14:29–14:30, JHN 13:37–13:38

title: 5028: knowledge, God as source of human
content:
All knowledge proceeds from God, although many do not acknowledge it. The pursuit of knowledge apart from God is futile and leads to pride.

God is the source of all knowledge

PRO 2:6 See also JOB 28:28; PRO 1:7, PRO 9:10

Pursuit of knowledge apart from God led to the fall

GEN 3:1–3:7 See also GEN 3:22–3:24

Pursuit of knowledge apart from God is futile

ECC 12:11–12:12 See also ECC 1:16–1:18; 1CO 8:1

Pursuit of the knowledge that proceeds from God merits divine approval

PRO 3:13–3:18 See also PRO 2:3–2:5, PRO 4:5, PRO 15:14; 2PE 1:5

God bestows knowledge on certain individuals

DAN 1:17 See also EXO 31:1–31:5, EXO 35:30–36:1; 1KI 3:10–3:12; 2CH 1:10–1:12; 1CO 12:8

title: 5029: knowledge, of God
content:
Human knowledge of God may be a purely intellectual phenomenon, as when one knows about God through observing the results of his actions, but God's people know him in a personal way because of their relationship with him.

Knowledge of God through his actions

God acts in creation

ROM 1:20 See also PSA 19:1–19:4; ACT 14:17

God acts in judgment

EZK 38:22–38:23 See also EXO 7:5, EXO 14:4; PSA 83:9–83:18; EZK 6:13, EZK 39:6, EZK 39:23

God acts in saving his people

ISA 52:9–52:10 See also 1SA 17:46–17:47; ISA 37:20, ISA 49:26

God's people know him through his dealings with them

God delivers his people

EXO 6:6–6:7 See also EXO 10:2, EXO 16:6; DEU 4:32–4:35; JOS 3:10, JOS 4:23–4:24; 1KI 20:13, 1KI 20:28

God provides and cares for his people

EXO 16:8 See also 1KI 8:56–8:60; ISA 41:17–41:20, ISA 45:4–45:6; EZK 37:26–37:28

In giving them his law

EZK 20:19–20:20 See also EXO 31:13; EZK 20:11–20:12

God judges and restores his people

EZK 11:10–11:12 See also NUM 14:34; JER 24:5–24:7, JER 31:33–31:34; EZK 6:2–6:10, EZK 7:4, EZK 12:15–12:16, EZK 20:38, EZK 36:11, EZK 37:14

Knowledge of God leads to confidence in him

PSA 9:10 See also GEN 22:7–22:8; JOB 19:25; PSA 18:2, PSA 37:25, PSA 71:5–71:6; ISA 12:1–12:2; DAN 11:32

title: 5030: knowledge, of Jesus Christ
content:
The believer's understanding and experience of Jesus Christ, which arises from a personal relationship established through faith.

Jesus Christ is the supreme revelation of God

JHN 14:6–14:10 See also MAT 11:27; JHN 1:1–1:2, JHN 8:19, JHN 17:26; COL 1:15–1:20; HEB 1:3

Knowledge of Jesus Christ acquired through a personal relationship with him

JHN 4:42 See also MAT 9:4–9:8 parallels MRK 2:8–2:12, LUK 5:22–5:26; JHN 10:38, JHN 14:11

Knowledge of Jesus Christ acquired through the work of the Holy Spirit

JHN 15:26 See also 1CO 12:3; 1JN 5:6–5:9

Knowledge of Jesus Christ is associated with knowing God

JHN 17:26 See also JHN 8:19, JHN 10:14–10:15, JHN 10:27–10:30, JHN 14:6–14:11, JHN 15:15

Knowledge of Jesus Christ should increase consistently

PHP 3:10; 2PE 3:18 See also 2PE 1:5–1:8

Consequences of knowing Jesus Christ

Reconciliation with God

2CO 5:19–5:20; ; EPH 2:16

Access to God

ROM 5:1–5:2; ; EPH 2:18

Becoming like Jesus Christ

PHP 3:10

Peace

See also JHN 14:1, JHN 16:33; ROM 5:1–5:2; EPH 2:14–2:18

Hope

EPH 1:17–1:18

Eternal life

JHN 17:3 See also JHN 10:27–10:28; 1JN 5:13, 1JN 5:20

Renewal

EPH 4:19–4:22

Unity among believers

JHN 17:21

Rejection by the world

JHN 15:18–15:21, JHN 16:2–16:3, JHN 17:14

Knowledge of Jesus Christ is to manifest itself in obedience

1JN 2:3–2:6 See also MAT 7:21–7:23, MAT 25:31–25:46; JHN 14:15, JHN 14:21, JHN 14:23, JHN 15:4–15:5

title: 5031: knowledge, of sin
content:
Originating with the fall, it is revealed by conscience, the law and the Holy Spirit.

Knowledge of sin as a result of the fall

GEN 3:1–3:13 See also GEN 2:16–2:17, GEN 3:22

Knowledge of sin through conscience

ROM 2:14–2:15 See also 1SA 24:5–24:6; 2SA 24:10; HEB 10:22

Knowledge of sin through the law

ROM 3:20 See also ROM 5:13, ROM 7:7

The law was taught to all in Israel

LEV 10:11 See also DEU 4:1, DEU 5:31, DEU 6:6–6:9

Knowledge of sin through the convicting power of the Holy Spirit

JHN 16:7–16:11 See also 1TH 1:5

title: 5033: knowledge of good and evil
content:
Every human being has some innate knowledge of good and evil. The full knowledge of good and evil derives from God and is revealed in Scripture. The human desire of Adam and Eve to know good and evil, and thus gain independence from God, brought about the fall.

The human quest for knowledge of good and evil

GEN 3:22 See also GEN 2:9, GEN 3:5–3:6; 2SA 14:17, 2SA 19:35; EZK 28:2–28:7

The consequences of the attempt to attain this knowledge

GEN 2:17 See also GEN 3:7–3:19; EZK 28:13–28:19; ROM 1:28–1:32

God as the source of full knowledge of good and evil

PSA 119:66 See also JOB 28:28; PSA 34:11–34:14, PSA 111:10; ROM 7:7

The natural knowledge of good and evil

Given in the human conscience

ROM 2:14–2:15 See also JOB 27:6; EZK 36:31; JHN 3:20; ACT 24:16; ROM 9:1; 2CO 1:12; 1TI 1:5, 1TI 1:18–1:19; 1PE 3:15–3:16

Conscience and moral decisions

1SA 25:30–25:34; ; 1CH 21:6–21:7; ; PSA 37:27; ; AMO 5:14–5:15; ; EPH 4:25–4:32

A natural knowledge of good and evil will not necessarily empower anyone to do good

ROM 7:15–7:25

title: 5034: likeness
content:
The similarity between objects or persons. Humanity is created in the likeness of God. Jesus Christ possesses a likeness to both God and humanity, which is expressed and safeguarded by the doctrine of the incarnation.

Human beings are created in the likeness of God

GEN 1:26–1:27 See also GEN 5:1, GEN 9:6; COL 3:9–3:10; JAS 3:9

Redemption includes being conformed to God's likeness

The likeness of God the Father

MAT 5:48 See also EPH 4:20–4:24

The likeness of God the Son

ROM 8:29 See also 1CO 2:16; 2CO 3:18; EPH 4:11–4:13

Jesus Christ was in the likeness of God and humanity

Jesus Christ is like God

COL 1:15 While stating that Jesus Christ is like God, Scripture also insists that this likeness is grounded in the fact that Jesus Christ is God. See also 2CO 4:4; PHP 2:6; HEB 1:3

Jesus Christ is like human beings

ROM 8:3 While stating that Jesus Christ is like humanity Scripture also insists that this likeness is grounded in the fact that Jesus Christ is human. Yet Christ did not share human sinfulness 2Co 5:21; Heb 4:15. See also PHP 2:6–2:7

title: 5035: mind
content: The seat of human consciousness, thought and desires. Scripture stresses that the minds of believers must be shaped by the knowledge and love of God, as their ways of thinking and acting become more like the pattern set out in Jesus Christ.

title: 5036: mind, of God
content:
God's pattern of thought and attitude of heart is holy, righteous and good. It is expressed in his law and his word, and also in the outworking of his mercy, but it is, ultimately, beyond human understanding.

God's mind is expressed in his law and his word

EXO 20:1–20:17 See also DEU 4:1–4:2, DEU 6:1, DEU 6:24–6:25; PSA 119:4, PSA 119:34, PSA 119:66, PSA 119:89, PSA 119:105, PSA 119:130

The mind of God is holy, righteous and good

ROM 7:7 See also DEU 4:8; NUM 23:19; 1SA 15:29; 2SA 22:31 parallel PSA 18:30; PRO 30:5; PSA 19:7–19:10, PSA 119:68, PSA 119:75, PSA 119:137–119:138, PSA 119:142; JHN 17:17; ROM 7:12

The mind of God is also expressed in his merciful acts

EPH 2:4–2:5 See also NEH 9:31; PSA 123:2; ISA 55:7; DAN 9:18; HOS 11:8; MIC 7:18; LUK 1:78; ROM 9:18, ROM 11:32, ROM 12:1; 1PE 1:3, 1PE 2:10

The constancy of the mind of God

NUM 23:19 See also 1SA 15:29; PSA 110:4; EZK 24:14

God changes his mind

Drawing back from threatened actions

JER 26:13 The idea of God “relenting” does not mean a capricious change of mind, but the considered decision on God's part not to proceed with a threatened course of action in response to repentance on the part of individuals or the people. See also EXO 32:12–32:14; JER 18:5–18:10, JER 26:3, JER 26:19; JOL 2:13–2:14; AMO 7:3, AMO 7:6; JON 3:9–3:10, JON 4:2

Grieving over past actions

1SA 15:11 See also GEN 6:6–6:7; 1SA 15:35

The mind of God is, ultimately, beyond human understanding

Because of God's greatness

ISA 55:8–55:9 See also ISA 40:13–40:14, ISA 40:28, ISA 44:6–44:7; ROM 11:33–11:36; 1CO 2:16

Because of human lowliness

ECC 5:1–5:2 See also ECC 7:23–7:25

title: 5037: mind, of Christ
content:
The mind of Christ reveals the essence of God's nature. Jesus Christ desires that his followers adopt his attitudes; this comes about through the work of the Holy Spirit.

The mind of Christ discloses the mind of God

In relation to righteousness, holiness and the law

JHN 14:9–14:11 See also MAT 5:17; JHN 15:10; 1CO 1:30

In mercy

1TI 1:15–1:16 See also MAT 9:12–9:13 parallels MRK 2:17, LUK 5:31–5:32; HOS 6:6; MAT 23:23; JUD 1:21

The mind of Christ is made known to believers by the Holy Spirit

JHN 14:26 See also JHN 16:12–16:15; ROM 8:9; 1CO 2:11–2:13

The plans and purposes of Jesus Christ are made known to the first Christians by the Spirit

ACT 16:6–16:7 See also ACT 8:29, ACT 10:19, ACT 11:12, ACT 11:28, ACT 13:2, ACT 15:28

Knowledge of the mind of Christ leads to holiness

1CO 2:14–2:16 See also PHP 2:5–2:11; 1PE 4:1–4:2

title: 5038: mind, the human
content:
On account of its inner orientation the fallen human mind is in conflict with the mind of God. It is nevertheless capable of knowing God, and of being changed and renewed by him.

The human mind is the seat of reason and decision-making

JOB 12:1–12:3 See also 1CH 17:2; 2CH 7:11; NEH 5:7; PSA 19:14, PSA 49:3; PRO 15:28, PRO 19:21; ECC 2:3, ECC 8:16; DAN 4:16, DAN 5:12, DAN 7:1; ROM 10:10, ROM 14:5; 1CO 14:14–14:15; 1PE 1:13; REV 17:9

The fallen human mind

The human mind is fatally flawed by sin

JER 17:9 See also GEN 6:5, GEN 8:21; 2CH 12:14; PSA 5:9, PSA 64:6, PSA 73:7; ISA 32:6; JER 17:1; ROM 8:5–8:8; EPH 4:17–4:18

Even the fallen mind can know something of God through creation

ROM 1:19–1:20

The fallen mind tends to confuse the Creator with his creation

ISA 44:16–44:18 See also ROM 1:21–1:25

Consequences of the human mind's sinfulness

Sinful attitudes lead to sinful words and actions

MAT 15:19 parallel MRK 7:21–7:22 See also ROM 1:28–1:32; EPH 4:17–4:19; COL 2:18; 1TI 6:5; 2TI 3:8

Sinfulness leads to death

ROM 2:5 See also ROM 6:23; COL 1:21

Doubt and instability

JAS 1:6–1:8

God can change the attitudes of the sinful human mind

The mind can be convicted of sin

PSA 51:3 See also 1KI 2:44; JHN 16:8–16:11

The mind can be changed

1TH 1:9 See also 2CH 32:26; JOB 42:6; PSA 119:36; ACT 2:37, ACT 26:17–26:18

It is God who enlightens the mind

2CO 4:6 See also DEU 29:4 God may withhold understanding; 1SA 10:9; JOB 38:36; ISA 32:4; JER 24:7, JER 31:33, JER 32:39; EZK 11:19, EZK 18:31, EZK 36:26–36:27; ROM 2:4; 2CO 3:14

It is God who renews the human mind

PSA 51:10 See also TIT 3:3–3:7

The renewed mind of the believer

ROM 12:1–12:2

Renewal brings knowledge of God

COL 1:9–1:10

Renewal brings peace

PHP 4:7 See also ISA 26:3

Renewal leads to obedience

ROM 8:5 See also ROM 7:25, ROM 12:1–12:2; COL 1:10, COL 3:1–3:2; 1PE 1:13; HEB 8:10, HEB 10:16; JER 31:33

The believer's mind needs growth and renewal

2CO 11:3 See also ROM 7:22–7:23; EPH 1:17; COL 1:9

title: 5040: murder
content:
The unlawful killing of individual human beings, forbidden by God and carrying the threat of severe punishment.

Murder forbidden by the law

EXO 20:13 parallel DEU 5:17 See also MAT 5:21, MAT 19:18 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20; ROM 13:9; 1TI 1:9; JAS 2:11–2:12

Murder is to be punished

Punishment by death

EXO 21:12 See also GEN 9:6; LEV 24:17, LEV 24:21; NUM 35:16–35:21, NUM 35:31; DEU 19:11–19:13

Punishment by banishing

GEN 4:13–4:14 See also PRO 28:17

Punishment by exclusion from the kingdom

REV 21:8, REV 22:15

Unintentional murderers are protected from avengers

NUM 35:11 See also NUM 35:22–35:29, NUM 35:32; JOS 21:13, JOS 21:21, JOS 21:27, JOS 21:32, JOS 21:38

Witnesses are required before murder is proven

NUM 35:30 See also DEU 17:6, DEU 19:15; HEB 10:28

Unpremeditated murder

NUM 35:22–35:24 See also EXO 21:13; DEU 4:41–4:44, DEU 19:4; JOS 20:1–20:3

Premeditated motives of murder

Jealousy

GEN 4:8 See also 1JN 3:12

Lust

2SA 12:9–12:10 Many motives contributed to David's plan to remove Uriah. It began with lust. See also 2SA 11:1–11:17

Rebellion and power

2KI 12:20 See also JDG 3:21; 2KI 9:14, 2KI 9:24, 2KI 19:36–19:37

To remove opponents

1KI 2:25 See also JDG 9:1–9:6; 2SA 20:9–20:10; 2CH 21:4

To take revenge

2SA 13:28–13:29 See also EXO 2:11–2:13; 2SA 3:27, 2SA 4:1–4:8

Robbery

PRO 1:11–1:13 See also LUK 10:30

Persecution

MAT 24:9 parallel LUK 21:12–21:17 See also 2CH 21:13; JOB 24:14; PRO 29:10; MAT 14:6–14:11, MAT 23:30–23:37; MRK 3:6; ACT 2:23, ACT 7:54–7:60; 2TI 4:6

Murder as an attitude as well as an action

MAT 5:21–5:22 See also MAT 15:19; JHN 8:44; 1JN 3:15

Murderers can be pardoned

Unjustly

LUK 23:25 parallels MAT 27:15–27:17, MRK 15:6–15:11, JHN 18:39–18:40 See also ACT 3:14

Justly--through God's grace

2SA 12:9–12:13; ACT 26:10; 1TI 1:13–1:15 See also EXO 2:12–3:12; ACT 7:58, ACT 8:3, ACT 9:1, ACT 9:13, ACT 22:4; 1CO 15:9; EPH 3:8

title: 5041: name
content: The title given to a person or object by one who is in a position of authority or ownership. Names often reflect the characteristics of a person or the aspirations or wishes for that person of the one bestowing the name.

title: 5042: name of God, significance of
content:
God's name is synonymous with his person, his presence and his power, and is therefore held in the highest honour.

God is referred to as the Name

ACT 5:41 See also LEV 24:10–24:16; 2SA 6:2 parallel 1CH 13:6; 3JN 1:7

God's person is revealed in his name

EXO 34:5–34:7 See also GEN 14:18–14:20, GEN 17:1, GEN 21:33, GEN 32:29–32:30; EXO 3:13–3:15, EXO 6:3, EXO 33:19; JDG 13:17–13:18; JER 16:21

God's name is synonymous with his presence

NUM 6:22–6:27 See also DEU 12:5–12:7; 1KI 8:15–8:21 parallel 2CH 6:4–6:11; NEH 1:9; PSA 20:1, PSA 54:1, PSA 74:7, PSA 75:1; ISA 30:27; JHN 17:11–17:12

The name of God identifies his people

DEU 28:10 See also 2CH 7:14; ISA 43:6–43:7; MIC 4:5, MIC 5:4

Dishonouring God's name is a serious offence

EXO 20:7 See also LEV 19:12, LEV 22:2, LEV 22:32; PSA 74:10, PSA 74:18, PSA 139:20; EZK 43:7–43:8; MAL 1:6

The righteous honour God's name

PSA 29:2 See also NEH 1:11; PSA 86:11–86:12; ISA 26:13; MAL 2:5, MAL 3:16–4:2

The name of Jesus Christ

Supplication is to be made in the name of Jesus Christ

JHN 14:13–14:14 See also MAT 18:19–18:20; JHN 15:16, JHN 16:23–16:24

Healing and other miracles performed in the name of Jesus Christ

ACT 3:6–3:8 See also ACT 3:16, ACT 4:30

Baptism is in Jesus Christ's name

ACT 2:38 See also MAT 28:19; ACT 8:12, ACT 8:15–8:16, ACT 10:48, ACT 19:5

Salvation is in the name of Jesus Christ

ACT 4:12 See also JHN 14:6, JHN 20:31; ACT 2:21; JOL 2:32; 1CO 6:11; 1JN 2:12; PHP 2:9–2:11

resource.label: 2203: Jesus Christ, titles and names of
3110: Holy Spirit, titles and names of

title: 5043: names, significance of
content:
Labels that idenitfy individuals. They may also denote aspects of character or reputation.

A name may reflect an individual's nature

1SA 25:25 See also GEN 17:5 “Abraham” means “father of many”; GEN 32:27–32:29 “Israel” means “he struggles with God”; EXO 34:14; MRK 5:9 parallel LUK 8:30

Additional names or nicknames

MRK 3:17 In NT times an additional name or surname reflecting someone's character was sometimes appended to the given name. See also LUK 6:15; JHN 1:42 “Cephas” and “Peter” mean “rock” in Aramaic and Greek respectively; ACT 4:36

A name may indicate an individual's reputation and standing in the community

A good name indicates a good reputation

PRO 22:1 See also PRO 3:4, PRO 10:7; ECC 7:1; SNG 1:3

A bad name indicates a bad reputation

NEH 6:13 See also DEU 22:13–22:19; PRO 25:9–25:10

Survival of one's name is important

RUT 4:9–4:10 See also GEN 48:15–48:16; NUM 27:1–27:4; DEU 25:7–25:9; 2SA 18:18; JOB 18:17–18:19

Preservation of a name indicates divine blessing

ISA 56:4–56:5 See also GEN 12:1–12:3; 2SA 7:9 parallel 1CH 17:8; 1KI 1:47; ISA 66:22

Obliteration of a name is associated with death

JER 11:19 See also DEU 7:24, DEU 9:14; 2SA 14:7; 2KI 14:27

Obliteration of a name is often linked with divine judgment

PSA 9:5–9:6 See also DEU 29:20; PSA 109:13; ISA 14:22–14:23, ISA 48:18–48:19; NAM 1:14

Bearing someone's name indicates ownership or identification

REV 22:3–22:4 See also EXO 23:21; 2CH 7:14; DEU 28:10; ISA 43:6–43:7; JER 14:9; DAN 9:18–9:19; REV 3:12, REV 14:1, REV 22:4

God knows his people by name

ISA 43:1 See also EXO 33:12, EXO 33:17; ISA 45:3, ISA 49:1; JHN 10:3

title: 5044: names, giving of
content:
Scripture contains many examples of the naming of people and places. Personal names, usually given at birth by parents, were sometimes changed at a later date.

Names may reflect personal experiences

GEN 41:51–41:52 See also GEN 29:31–29:35, GEN 30:6–30:8, GEN 30:18–30:20, GEN 30:23–30:24, GEN 35:18; EXO 2:10, EXO 2:21–2:22, EXO 18:3–18:4; 1SA 1:20; 1CH 4:9

Names may reflect national experiences

1SA 4:21 See also GEN 10:25 parallel 1CH 1:19; ISA 8:3–8:4; HOS 1:2–1:11

Names may indicate future destiny

MAT 1:21 See also LUK 1:31–1:33

The giving of a name reflects the authority of the giver

GEN 1:5–1:10, GEN 2:19–2:20 See also GEN 2:23, GEN 35:18; 2KI 23:34 parallel 2CH 36:4; 2KI 24:17; LUK 1:62–1:63

The changing of names

On divine instruction

GEN 17:3–17:8 See also GEN 17:15–17:16, GEN 35:9–35:10; JHN 1:42

In relation to salvation

ISA 62:2 See also ISA 65:15; REV 2:17

In the light of past experience

JDG 6:32 See also RUT 1:20

In the future

ZEC 8:3 See also ISA 1:26, ISA 44:5, ISA 58:12, ISA 62:4, ISA 62:12; JER 7:32, JER 20:3–20:6; MAL 1:4

In a new culture

GEN 41:45 See also DAN 1:7

The instance of Paul

ACT 13:9 The occasion of and reason for the change from “Saul” to “Paul” are not clear.

Place-names may reflect events or experiences

GEN 11:8–11:9, GEN 16:13–16:14, GEN 19:21–19:22, GEN 21:31, GEN 26:32–26:33, GEN 28:18–28:19, GEN 31:45–31:50, GEN 32:1–32:2, GEN 32:30, GEN 33:17, GEN 35:7–35:8

title: 5046: opportunities
content: Events or moments at which actions of importance or significance can be achieved. God provides opportune moments both for his people to serve him and to proclaim the gospel and for those outside the church to respond to the gospel.

title: 5047: opportunities, in life
content:
Scripture views life as divinely ordained to include occasions when certain forms of behaviour are appropriate.

The need to discern opportune moments

ECC 3:1

Every possible opportunity should be taken to do good

GAL 6:10 See also LUK 10:33; JHN 9:4; EPH 5:16; COL 4:5; 2TI 4:2

Examples of individuals who seized opportunities to serve God

Rahab saved the spies and her household: JOS 2:8–2:14, JOS 6:23; 2KI 5:1–5:3 Naaman's wife's maid helped Naaman by telling her mistress about Elisha; ; NEH 2:2–2:5 Nehemiah gained permission to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.; EST 4:14, EST 7:3–7:6; DAN 2:14–2:16 Daniel offered to interpret Nebuchadnezzar's dream; ; ACT 18:24–18:26 Priscilla and Aquila taught Apollos.

Some opportunities should be rejected

1SA 24:3–24:4, 1SA 24:10, 1SA 26:6–26:11

Opportunities to do evil may have appalling consequences

GEN 4:8 Cain made an opportunity to murder Abel; ; GEN 25:29–25:31 Jacob took the opportunity to “buy” Esau's birthright.; GEN 37:18–37:20, GEN 37:27; DAN 6:4–6:5 Daniel's enemies sought and found an opportunity to lay a charge against him.; MAT 26:16 parallels MRK 14:11, LUK 22:6

Giving others an opportunity to do wrong must be avoided

1TI 5:14

title: 5048: opportunities, and salvation
content:
God chooses the right moment in his work to save humanity. It is important to seize the opportunities he offers, both in receiving salvation and in working with him to offer it to others.

Israel had opportunities of salvation

At Sinai

EXO 19:4–19:8 God had saved Israel from slavery in Egypt. Now they accepted the opportunity to become his covenant people.

At Shechem

JOS 24:14–24:15 After Israel entered Canaan, Joshua challenged them to forsake idolatry and renew the covenant with the LORD.

The coming of Jesus Christ offers a new and urgent opportunity to respond to God

MAT 3:1–3:2; GAL 4:4 See also MAT 10:7; MRK 1:15; ROM 5:6

The message of opportunity continues after the resurrection of Jesus Christ

For Israel

ACT 3:24–3:26

For the Gentiles

ACT 17:30 See also ACT 17:23, ACT 17:31

God in his mercy gives opportunity to repent and believe

ROM 2:4; ; 2PE 3:8–3:9

The urgency of the need to respond to God's opportunity of salvation

2CO 6:2; HEB 4:7 See also PSA 95:7–95:8; ISA 49:8, ISA 55:6–55:7

God will judge evil at an opportune time

REV 14:18 See also REV 14:7

It is possible to refuse the opportunity of salvation, with sad consequences

The lesson of Israel

NUM 14:8–14:10; ; PSA 95:7–95:11; ; 2CO 6:1–6:2; ; HEB 4:3, HEB 4:7 Hebrews warns Christians not to miss their chance of blessing.

The seriousness of rejecting the good news

MAT 10:14 parallels MRK 6:11, LUK 9:5; ; LUK 19:41–19:42 Jesus Christ wept over Jerusalem because the city didn't recognise its opportunity; ; ACT 13:46–13:51, ACT 28:25–28:28

Christians should take every opportunity to tell others the good news

JHN 4:35 See also LUK 10:2; 1CO 16:9; COL 4:5; 1PE 3:15

title: 5050: reason
content:
The human capacity to think logically and intelligently, thereby discovering truth or persuading others. But human reason is limited and cannot arrive at a true and full knowledge of God without divine assistance and revelation.

The human power of reason

1CO 13:11

Human reason is limited

JOB 32:11–32:12 See also JOB 32:3

Human reason is far inferior to divine reason

1CO 1:18–1:31 See also JOB 12:20, JOB 12:24–12:25; ISA 29:14, ISA 55:8–55:9

Human reason may point people towards God

ROM 2:14–2:15 See also ISA 1:18–1:20; ACT 17:22–17:23, ACT 17:27–17:28; ROM 1:19–1:20; HEB 11:17–11:19

Paul reasons with unbelievers

ACT 17:2–17:4 See also ACT 17:17, ACT 18:4, ACT 18:19

Believers are to give reasons for their faith

1PE 3:15

God reasons with his rebellious people

ISA 1:18–1:19

title: 5051: responsibility
content: An obligation, especially to give account of one's actions. Scripture stresses that the responsibilities which believers and the church have arise from their special and privileged relationship to God.

title: 5052: responsibility, to God
content:
Even though God is sovereign, all people everywhere are accountable to him for everything they do, say or think.

People are responsible for their own sins

God is not responsible for human sin

DEU 24:16; EZK 18:4 See also JOB 19:4; PSA 51:4–51:5; JER 31:30; EZK 18:20, EZK 33:1–33:20; ROM 6:23

Death is the result of sin

ROM 5:12, ROM 6:23 See also GEN 3:1–3:7; ISA 43:27; EZK 18:4; 1CO 15:21–15:22

The law heightens human responsibility for sin

It brings knowledge of sin

ROM 5:20 Because the law brings knowledge of sin, it prevents people from claiming ignorance of the nature and seriousness of that sin. See also ROM 7:7–7:9; GAL 3:19

It applies not only to actions but also to words and thoughts

MAT 5:22, MAT 5:28 See also JER 17:9–17:10; MAT 15:18–15:19

It brings judgment

ECC 12:14; MAT 12:36–12:37; 1CO 4:5 See also JOB 15:5–15:6; ROM 2:16, ROM 14:12; 2CO 5:10; 1PE 4:5; JUD 1:15

Ignorance does not remove responsibility

LEV 5:17 See also LUK 12:48; ACT 3:17–3:19; ROM 1:20

The responsibility of humanity to repent and believe

It is commanded by God

ACT 17:30 See also EZK 18:30; MAT 4:17; MRK 1:15, MRK 6:12; LUK 24:46–24:47

Jesus Christ's life and ministry heightens the responsibility to repent

JHN 3:18, JHN 15:22 See also MAT 11:20–11:24, MAT 12:41–12:42 parallel LUK 11:31–11:32; JHN 12:48

title: 5053: responsibility, for God's world
content:
All humanity has a moral obligation under God to one another, whether as national leaders, ministers, spouses, parents, children, believers or simply as human beings. This moral obligation is shown in the Scriptures to also include the animal kingdom and the environment.

The responsibility of national leaders

To reward good and punish evil

ROM 13:3–13:4 See also PRO 16:12

To administer justice

PRO 31:4–31:5, PRO 31:8–31:9 See also DEU 27:19; PRO 14:31, PRO 17:5, PRO 29:4, PRO 29:14

The responsibility of Christian leaders

To care for believers

1PE 5:2 See also JHN 21:15–21:17; ACT 20:28

To preach, teach and handle the Scriptures properly

2TI 2:15, 2TI 4:2 See also EZK 33:6

The responsibility of those who are married

To love each other

EPH 5:25; TIT 2:4

To mutually honour each other

EPH 5:22; 1PE 3:7 See also 1PE 3:1

The responsibility of parents to their children

EPH 6:4 See also DEU 6:7; PRO 13:24, PRO 22:6; 1TI 3:4; TIT 2:4

The responsibility of children to honour their parents

EPH 6:1–6:3 See also DEU 5:16

The responsibility of every believer to represent Jesus Christ in the world

MAT 5:13, MAT 5:14, MAT 28:19–28:20 See also MRK 16:15; ACT 1:8

The responsibility of every human being to love God and others

LUK 10:27 parallels MAT 22:37–22:39, MRK 12:29–12:31 See also DEU 6:5; LEV 19:18; 1SA 20:17; PRO 14:31; MAT 5:43–5:45; LUK 10:28–10:37

The responsibility to exercise dominion over the animal kingdom and creation

GEN 1:26; PRO 12:10 See also GEN 9:2; EXO 23:5; DEU 22:4, DEU 22:6–22:7, DEU 25:4; PSA 8:6–8:8

title: 5054: responsibility, examples of
content:
Scripture provides examples of individuals and situations in which responsibility is accepted, delegated or denied.

Examples of responsibility accepted

Noah to build the ark

GEN 6:13–6:14, GEN 6:22 See also HEB 11:7

Joseph over Potiphar's household

GEN 39:4 See also GEN 39:1–39:6

Joseph over the other prisoners

GEN 39:22 See also GEN 39:20–39:23

Joseph over the whole of Egypt

GEN 41:39–41:41 See also GEN 41:55–41:57, GEN 45:8–45:9

Levites to be priests

NUM 3:5–3:7 See also NUM 8:5–8:26

Solomon, not David, to build the temple

1CH 22:2–22:10

Ezekiel to be a watchman

EZK 3:16–3:21

Jesus Christ in dying on the cross

PHP 2:8 See also MAT 26:39; JHN 10:18; ROM 5:19

Examples of delegation of responsibility

Moses chose leaders to judge

EXO 18:24–18:26 See also EXO 18:13–18:23

The apostles delegated responsibility to seven men

ACT 6:3 See also ACT 6:1–6:6

Responsibility delegated to elders

ACT 14:23

Examples of denial of responsibility

Adam and Eve in eating the fruit

GEN 3:11–3:13 God held them both responsible.

Aaron after making the golden calf

See also EXO 32:19–32:24

Saul after not destroying everything belonging to the Amalekites

1SA 15:3, 1SA 15:7–15:9, 1SA 15:15

Pilate after ordering Jesus Christ to be crucified

MAT 27:24

Judas after betraying Jesus Christ

See also MAT 27:3–27:5

resource.label: 8446: hospitality, a duty of God's people

title: 5056: rest
content: Scripture recognises the need for physical and spiritual relief and stresses that the true resting-place of humanity lies in God, the Creator and Redeemer.

title: 5057: rest, physical
content:
The need for physical rest is recognised in Scripture, and provision is made for ensuring that people are allowed time for rest.

Jesus Christ needed physical rest

JHN 4:6 See also MRK 4:38, MRK 6:31; LUK 9:58

The provision of rest

The need for rest

MRK 6:31 See also PSA 23:2–23:3; PRO 17:1; ECC 4:6; MAT 11:28–11:30

Provision of sleep for rest

PSA 4:8 See also PSA 127:2; ECC 5:12

Provision of a Sabbath-rest

EXO 34:21; MRK 2:27 See also EXO 20:8–20:11 parallel DEU 5:12–5:15; EXO 31:15, EXO 35:2; LEV 23:3; NEH 13:15; ISA 58:13–58:14

The purpose of rest

To renew strength

LAM 5:5 See also ISA 40:29–40:31

To know peace

MAT 6:25–6:34 See also JOB 11:18–11:19; PSA 3:5, PSA 16:8; PRO 3:24; PHP 4:6–4:7

The character of rest

The absence of war

JOS 11:23 See also JOS 14:15; 1KI 5:4; 1CH 22:9; PSA 46:9–46:10; PRO 1:33; ISA 14:3

The absence of social strife

2CO 13:11 See also ECC 10:4; 1CO 1:10; 1TH 4:11; HEB 12:14; JAS 3:17–3:18; 1PE 3:8

The absence of fear

MRK 4:37–4:38 parallels MAT 8:24–8:25, LUK 8:23–8:24 See also GEN 32:11; PSA 127:2; MIC 4:4; MAT 6:31 parallel LUK 12:29

The absence of anxiety

1PE 5:7 See also MAT 6:25; PHP 4:6

The presence of God

EXO 33:14 See also DEU 33:27; MAT 11:28

The experience of security

DEU 33:12 See also PRO 19:23

The experience of peace in death

REV 14:13 See also DEU 31:16; JOB 3:13–3:17

The destruction of rest

By business

PSA 39:6 See also GEN 31:40; ECC 1:13, ECC 2:23, ECC 8:16; LUK 21:34

By conflict

2CO 7:5 See also LAM 5:5; 2CO 6:5, 2CO 11:27

By grief

JER 45:3 See also JOB 3:26; PSA 77:4; DAN 6:18

By unconfessed guilt

PSA 32:3–32:5 See also GEN 4:12; DEU 28:65–28:67; ISA 48:22, ISA 57:20–57:21; REV 14:11

By sickness

JOB 30:17 See also JOB 7:4–7:5

title: 5058: rest, spiritual
content:
To be at rest spiritually is to find peace with God through Jesus Christ. This rest is promised to all who put their trust in God and obey him.

The human desire for spiritual rest

LAM 5:19–5:22 See also PSA 55:4–55:8; LAM 3:25–3:26; 1TI 2:2

Spiritual rest is to be found in God alone

MAT 11:28–11:30 See also EXO 33:14; PSA 23:2, PSA 51:12, PSA 62:1–62:2, PSA 62:5–62:8, PSA 91:1–91:13; ISA 26:3–26:4; JHN 14:27; ROM 5:1; GAL 1:3, GAL 5:22; COL 1:20

God promises his people spiritual rest

HEB 4:9–4:11 See also PSA 1:3, PSA 37:7, PSA 116:7, PSA 119:165, PSA 125:1, PSA 131:1–131:3; PRO 29:25; ISA 30:15, ISA 32:17–32:18, ISA 58:11; JER 6:16, JER 17:7–17:8; JHN 14:1; ROM 8:6; 1PE 3:4

Spiritual rest is not for the wicked

PSA 1:4–1:5 See also PSA 112:10; ECC 2:23; ISA 48:22, ISA 57:20–57:21

God's offer of rest rejected by a faithless people

ISA 28:12; JER 6:16

title: 5059: rest, eternal
content:
Eternal rest consists of peace with God, an absence of toil and tribulation and a final deliverance from pain, sorrow and death. It is promised as the inheritance of the people of God.

Eternal rest foreshadowed in the OT

In God's rest after creation

HEB 4:3–4:4 See also GEN 2:2–2:3

In the rest promised to Joshua

HEB 4:8 See also DEU 31:7; JOS 22:4; PSA 95:7–95:11

The eternal state described as rest

HEB 4:9 See also JOB 3:11–3:19; REV 14:13

Aspects of eternal rest

Being in the presence of God

LUK 23:43 See also JHN 14:3; PHP 1:23; 1TH 4:17–4:18; REV 3:4, REV 7:15

Happiness

2CO 5:8 See also MAT 25:23; LUK 13:29

Refreshment and satisfaction

REV 7:17 See also PSA 16:11, PSA 17:15; EZK 47:1–47:12; REV 22:1–22:2

The absence of trouble

2TH 1:6–1:7 See also REV 6:10–6:11, REV 7:14

The absence of labour

REV 14:13 See also JOB 3:17; ISA 57:2, ISA 65:22–65:23; HEB 4:1–4:11

The absence of pain, sorrow and death

REV 21:4 See also ISA 25:8, ISA 65:19; LUK 20:36; ROM 8:23; 1CO 15:24; REV 7:16–7:17

The absence of conflict and harm

ISA 65:25 See also ISA 11:6–11:9; HOS 2:18

The absence of the curse

REV 22:3

Eternal rest is conditional upon faithful obedience

HEB 4:11, HEB 4:1–4:2

title: 5061: sanctity of life
content:
Scripture treats human life as a divine gift and something for which humans are responsible. It is thus to be valued and respected. No human being has the right to take the life of another.

The sanctity of all human life

It proceeds from God

GEN 2:7; ACT 17:25

It is precious to God

GEN 1:27 See also GEN 4:10–4:11; 2SA 18:12–18:13; MAT 6:25–6:26

It is protected by God

DEU 22:8 See also GEN 4:15; NUM 35:11–35:12; JER 22:3

Death is by God's appointment

HEB 9:27 See also JOB 14:5; PSA 90:3, PSA 90:5

God prohibits unlawful taking of life

EXO 20:13 parallel DEU 5:17 See also MAT 19:18; ROM 13:9 So precious is human life that some situations which required the death penalty in the OT are dealt with differently in the NT (e.g., Jn 8:5,11).

God punishes unlawful taking of life

GEN 9:6 See also EXO 21:14; 2SA 12:9; 2KI 21:16

The sanctity of children's lives

Children are planned by God

GEN 18:10; ; JDG 13:3–13:4; ; 1KI 13:2; ; 2KI 4:16–4:17; ; JER 1:5; ; LUK 1:13–1:17, LUK 1:24–1:25, LUK 1:31–1:33, LUK 1:35

Children are precious and to be treasured

PSA 127:3–127:4 See also GEN 33:5, GEN 48:9; PSA 113:9, PSA 128:3

Child sacrifice is opposed

GEN 22:10–22:12; ; LEV 18:21; ; DEU 12:31; ; 2KI 3:27, 2KI 16:3 parallel 2CH 28:3; ; PSA 106:38; ; ISA 57:5; ; JER 7:30–7:31, JER 19:5; ; EZK 16:20–16:21

Warnings against murder of children

EXO 1:16–1:17; ; ACT 7:19

Antenatal life is fully human

JOB 31:15; ; PSA 22:9, PSA 119:73, PSA 139:13–139:16; ; ISA 46:3–46:4, ISA 49:1, ISA 49:5; ; JER 1:5; LUK 1:41, LUK 1:44

Injury to a pregnant woman is serious

EXO 21:22–21:25; ; AMO 1:13

The sanctity of old age

The old are to be respected

PRO 23:22 See also LEV 19:32; JOB 32:6; PSA 71:18; 1TI 5:1–5:2

The old are to be cherished

1TI 5:4 See also GEN 47:12–47:13; 1SA 22:3; JHN 19:26–19:27

title: 5062: spirit
content: In Scripture the innermost aspect of human nature. The three-fold division of spirit, soul and body is sometimes used to refer to this distinction between the physical and spiritual aspects of human existence.

title: 5063: spirit, nature of
content:
The life-giving principle of human nature, to be distinguished from the purely physical aspects of life.

The human spirit as distinct from the body

MAT 26:41 parallel MRK 14:381TH 5:23 See also ROM 8:10; 1CO 5:3–5:5, 1CO 7:34; 2CO 7:1; COL 2:5; HEB 4:12 “spirit” and “soul” may be two names for the inner being penetrated by the word of God, or they may distinguish the inner person in relation to God (“spirit”) from their relation to the world (“soul”); JAS 2:26; REV 18:13

The human spirit vitalises the body

JAS 2:26 See also GEN 2:7; JOB 34:14; LUK 8:55; 1CO 15:45; REV 13:15 “breath” is the same word as “spirit” in Greek.

The human spirit as the seat of thought and feeling

The seat of perception

EZK 13:3; ; MRK 2:8; ; ROM 8:16; ; 1CO 2:11

The seat of feeling

2SA 13:39; ; JOB 32:18; ; ISA 54:6, ISA 57:15, ISA 66:2; ; EZK 3:14; ; DAN 7:15; ; MAT 5:3; ; LUK 1:47; ; JHN 11:33, JHN 13:21

The seat of volition

MAT 26:41 parallel MRK 14:38; ; 2CO 12:18; ; PHP 1:27

The human spirit survives physical death

2CO 5:1–5:5 See also 1SA 28:13–28:14; MAT 10:28; ACT 7:59; ROM 8:23; HEB 12:23; 1PE 3:19, 1PE 4:6

Jesus Christ had a human spirit

JHN 13:21 See also MAT 27:50 parallels LUK 23:46, JHN 19:30; JHN 12:27

title: 5064: spirit, emotional aspects of
content:
A human being is made up of a variety of emotions and attitudes. Sometimes one trait is or becomes so dominant as to make it characteristic of the entire personality.

Examples of a bad spirit

Pride

PRO 16:18

Jealousy

See also NUM 5:14

Fear

2KI 19:7 parallel ISA 37:7

Unfaithfulness

HOS 4:12, HOS 5:4

Despair

ISA 61:3

Spiritual dullness

ROM 11:8; ; DEU 29:4; ; ISA 29:10

Examples of a good spirit

Humility

PRO 29:23 See also NUM 12:3; ISA 57:15

Submission

NUM 14:24 See also NUM 14:6–14:9

Wisdom

DEU 34:9; ; 1KI 3:11–3:12; ; JOB 32:8; ; DAN 4:9

Steadfastness

PSA 51:10, PSA 51:12

Strength

LUK 1:17; ; MAL 4:5

Zeal

ROM 12:11; ; JHN 2:17

Gentleness

1CO 4:21; ; 1PE 3:4

Trust

2CO 4:13

God can effect a change of spirit

EZK 36:26 See also EZK 11:19, EZK 18:31; HAG 1:14; ZEC 12:10

title: 5065: spirit, fallen and redeemed
content:
Every aspect of the human personality, including the spirit, was affected by the fall. At regeneration the human personality is transformed by the Holy Spirit.

The human spirit is directly created by God

NUM 16:22 See also ISA 42:5; ZEC 12:1; HEB 12:9 “human fathers” is literally “fathers of our flesh (bodies)”, i.e., there is an antithesis between those who are the fathers of people's bodies and God, who is the Father of their spirits. Thus bodies are derived from parents but souls from God.

The human spirit was affected by the fall

JER 17:9 See also GEN 6:5; PSA 64:6, PSA 78:37; MAT 15:19 parallel MRK 7:21; EZK 18:31

The human spirit is renewed by the Holy Spirit at regeneration

EZK 36:26–36:27 See also PSA 51:10; JER 31:33; EZK 11:19; JHN 3:6; ROM 8:10; GAL 5:22–5:23

The regenerated human spirit beyond death

It is perfected in heaven

HEB 12:22–12:23 See also 2CO 5:8

It is incomplete without a resurrection body

ROM 8:23 See also 2CO 5:1–5:4

title: 5067: suicide
content:
The deliberate taking of one's own life, a rare occurrence in Scripture.

Psychological causes of suicide

A sense of guilt leads to suicide

MAT 27:5 See also ACT 1:18–1:19

Defeat leads to suicide

1SA 31:4 See also 1SA 31:5–31:6 parallel 1CH 10:4–10:5; 2SA 1:9, 2SA 17:23; 1KI 16:18

Defiance leads to suicide

JDG 16:26–16:30; ; 2SA 17:23

Failure leads to attempted suicide

ACT 16:27

Desire for death is more frequently expressed in the Bible than actual suicide

The desire for death in a prophet's depression

1KI 19:3–19:4 See also JER 15:10, JER 20:14–20:18; JON 4:1–4:3 A desire for death does not lead to taking of one's own life, but to entrusting the place and time of one's death to the Lord.

The desire for death arising from grief and pain

JOB 10:1 See also JOB 3:1–3:4, JOB 7:15–7:16

The desire for death because of judgment

REV 9:6 See also HOS 10:8; REV 6:16

Life hated because of its apparent futility

ECC 2:17 See also PSA 90:8–90:10; ECC 4:1–4:3

Suicide usurps God's sovereignty over life

God is Creator, and thus has authority over his creation

JOB 10:12 See also GEN 2:7, GEN 2:17; PSA 90:1–90:10, PSA 139:13–139:15

God controls life and death

JOB 1:21 See also EXO 23:25–23:26; DEU 32:39; JOB 30:23; ECC 8:8; LUK 12:22–12:25; HEB 9:27

title: 5071: Aaron
content: The elder brother of Moses and Miriam. He served as a spokesman for his brother in the confrontation with Pharoah, which eventually led to the exodus from Egypt. He was later consecrated as high priest.

title: 5075: Abraham
content: The OT patriarch born in Ur and called by God to live in Canaan. God promised to make his descendants into a great nation, a promise fulfilled initially in Israel, and subsequently in the Christian church. His trust in God is seen as exemplary by NT writers.

title: 5076: Abraham, life of
content:
God called Abraham to live as a nomad in Canaan and promised the land to his descendants, naming him “father of many”, although he had no heir until his old age.

content:

content:
Whereas Jews see Abraham as the father of their nation on account of God's covenant with him, Christians see Abraham as the father of all who believe in Jesus Christ.

title: 5080: Adam
content: The Hebrew word “adam” is used both for “man” in general and also as the personal name of the first man that God created. It sounds like the word “adamah”, meaning “ground”.

content:
Adam is portrayed as the height of God's creation, made in the image and likeness of God, and entrusted with the stewardship of creation.

title: 5085: David
content: The youngest son of Jesse and great-grandson of Ruth and Boaz, who became Israel's greatest king. Born in the town of Bethlehem, he probably lived c. 1040–970 B.C.

content:
David rose from humble origins to become Israel's greatest king. His rise to power is seen by OT writers as evidence of God's guiding hand upon both David and Israel.

content:

content:

JDG 5:1–5:3, JDG 5:28–5:31 In this respect she is like Moses and Miriam (Ex 15:1,20).

title: 5092: Elijah
content:
Living in Israel, his ministry as a prophet was to oppose the worship of Baal in Israel, and the sin, injustices and idolatry of Ahab, Jezebel and Ahaziah. He came, probably, from Tishbe in Gilead, but his parentage is not certain. His name means “the LORD is God”.

title: 5094: Jacob
content: The grandson of Abraham, and one of the two twin sons of Isaac. As the firstborn son of Isaac, Esau was entitled to inherit all of Isaac's property. However, he sold this to his brother Jacob to satisfy his immediate physical hunger. Through subsequent deception, Jacob was able to gain Isaac's blessing, and inherit all that was rightly Esau's. Despite such major faults, Scripture regards Jacob as further confirmation of God's promises to Abraham, and a model of faith and obedience.

content:

title: 5107: Paul
content: The “apostle to the Gentiles”. Converted from Judaism by an encounter with the risen Christ, Paul planted and corresponded with churches through much of the Mediterranean. In his letters, Paul stresses the universality of the gospel, which knows no distinction between Jew and Gentile, and the effects of Christian faith upon life and conduct.

A.D. 35) led to his becoming the apostle to the Gentiles, with a mission to proclaim the gospel throughout the Gentile world. He was probably martyred during the persecutions of Nero, possibly in A.D. 67.

His disagreement with Barnabas and his new partnership with Silas

ACT 15:36–15:41

In Asia Minor

ACT 16:6–16:8

In Macedonia

ACT 16:9–16:12, ACT 17:1, ACT 17:10

In Greece

ACT 17:15, ACT 18:1 It was from Corinth that Paul wrote to the Thessalonians.

His return to Antioch

ACT 18:18–18:22

Paul's third missionary journey (c. A.D. 53–57)

His general purpose in making his journey

ACT 18:23

At Ephesus

See also ACT 19:1–19:12; 1CO 15:32, 1CO 16:8–16:9

His visit to Corinth

2CO 1:15–1:16, 2CO 1:23–2:4, 2CO 13:2 Most scholars believe that Paul wrote 1Corinthians from Ephesus, and that he also visited Corinth during this period. This visit, however, proved to be such a painful experience for him that he abandoned plans for a third visit, and instead wrote the Corinthians a “tearful” letter, calling them to repent of their sinful behaviour.

His journey to Greece

ACT 20:1–20:6; ; 2CO 2:12–2:13 Paul had hoped that Titus would bring him news from Corinth. They finally met in Macedonia, and Titus brought good news about the Corinthians' change of heart. Paul then wrote 2Corinthians before visiting Corinth for a third time.

His return to Jerusalem with the collection

ACT 20:6, ACT 20:13–20:16, ACT 21:1–21:8, ACT 21:15, ACT 21:17–21:19; ; ROM 15:25–15:26 Paul wrote Romans at this point in his travels. There is a considerable degree of uncertainty as to precisely when Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians and Philemon were written.

Paul under arrest

His life threatened in Jerusalem

ACT 21:27–21:34, ACT 23:12–23:21

In Caesarea (c. A.D. 57–59)

ACT 23:23–23:35, ACT 24:23–24:27

His appeal to Caesar

ACT 25:1–25:12

His shipwreck

ACT 27:1–28:10

His visit to Rome (c. A.D. 60)

ACT 28:11–28:16, ACT 28:30–28:31

These verses from the Pastoral Epistles may indicate that Paul was ultimately released and undertook further journeys in the Eastern Mediterranean before his death: 1TI 1:3; ; 2TI 4:13, 2TI 4:20; ; TIT 1:5, TIT 3:12

title: 5109: Paul, apostle to Gentiles
content:
Paul saw his encounter with the risen Christ as a call to apostleship, with a special mission to proclaim the gospel to the Gentile world. Paul's complete dedication to Jesus Christ made his own personal weaknesses a vehicle for the power of God.

Paul's calling as an apostle: origins and implications

His calling began with his encounter with the risen Christ

GAL 1:15–1:16 See also ACT 9:3–9:19 parallels ACT 22:6–22:16, ACT 26:12–26:18; 1CO 9:1

His calling involved his being sent to the unevangelised Gentile world

GAL 2:9 See also ACT 22:21; ROM 15:18–15:21; 2CO 10:13–10:16; EPH 3:7–3:9

His calling put him under an obligation to preach the gospel

1CO 9:16 See also ROM 1:14–1:15; 2CO 5:11–5:14

Paul's commitment to his apostolic calling

He supported himself in order to present the gospel free of charge

1TH 2:6–2:9 See also 1CO 9:3–9:18; 2CO 12:13

He put the gospel before everything else

2CO 4:5 See also ROM 9:1–9:3; 1CO 9:19–9:23; PHP 1:12–1:26

He boasted in his weaknesses

2CO 12:7–12:10 See also 2CO 4:7–4:10, 2CO 6:3–6:10, 2CO 11:21–11:29

He experienced God's power at work through him

2CO 12:11–12:12 See also ACT 13:6–13:12, ACT 19:11–19:12; ROM 15:18–15:19; 1CO 2:4–2:5; 1TH 1:4–1:5

He had a confident attitude to death

PHP 3:10–3:11 See also 2CO 5:6–5:10; PHP 1:20–1:24; 2TI 4:6–4:8

Paul and the example of Jesus Christ

His appeal to Jesus Christ as an example to the churches

2CO 8:9 Paul here uses the example of Jesus Christ in order to encourage the Corinthians in their giving. See also ROM 15:1–15:3; PHP 2:5–2:11

His own exemplary imitation of Jesus Christ

1CO 11:1 See also 1CO 4:14–4:17; PHP 3:12–3:17, PHP 4:8–4:9; 2TH 3:6–3:9

His sharing of Jesus Christ's sufferings

COL 1:24 Paul is not suggesting here that there is any deficiency in Jesus Christ's atoning sacrifice. Rather, there are some aspects of suffering which Christ could not experience because they arose only as a result of people preaching the message of the cross and suffering because of it. See also 2CO 1:5–1:9, 2CO 4:7–4:12; GAL 6:17

Paul and the churches

His integrity in dealing with the churches

2CO 1:12 See also ACT 20:17–20:21; 2CO 2:17, 2CO 4:1–4:2; 1TH 2:10–2:12

His love for the churches

PHP 1:8 See also 2CO 11:7–11:11, 2CO 12:14–12:15; 1TH 3:12

His prayers for the churches

1TH 1:2 See also ROM 1:8–1:10; EPH 1:15–1:19; 2TH 1:11–1:12

His dependence on the prayers of the churches

1TH 5:25 See also ROM 15:30–15:32; EPH 6:19–6:20; PHM 1:22

Paul's imagery of apostleship

As Jesus Christ's ambassador

2CO 5:20; ; EPH 6:19–6:20

As a builder

ROM 15:20; ; 1CO 3:10

As a farmer

1CO 3:5–3:9

As a father

1CO 4:15; ; 1TH 2:11–2:12

As a mother

GAL 4:19; ; 1TH 2:6–2:7

As God's captive

1CO 4:9; ; 2CO 2:14–2:16 Paul portrays God as a victorious Roman general, with himself as a captive, bringing up the rear of the triumphal procession.

As Jesus Christ's slave

The word translated servant'' in these verses commonly meantslave'': ROM 1:1; ; 2CO 4:5; ; PHP 1:1; ; TIT 1:1

Paul's successors were to safeguard the truth of the gospel after his death

2TI 2:1–2:2 See also 2TI 1:13–1:14, 2TI 3:10–4:8

title: 5110: Paul, teaching of
content:
Paul's understanding of the Christian life was dominated by the importance of Jesus Christ's death and resurrection, by means of which he saw God as having acted decisively to redeem the world. Paul emphasised that Jews and Gentiles alike are justified by faith, and share together in the glorious new era of the Holy Spirit, which is to be consummated at Christ's return.

The redeeming work of Jesus Christ

God's work of redemption in Jesus Christ's death and resurrection

ROM 3:25 See also ROM 8:3–8:4; 2CO 5:18–5:19; COL 1:21–1:22

Jesus Christ as substitute, exchanges places with the sinner

2CO 5:21 See also GAL 3:13–3:14, GAL 4:4–4:5

Jesus Christ reverses the effects of Adam's sin

1CO 15:21–15:22 See also ROM 5:12–5:19

The death and resurrection of Jesus Christ mark the beginning of God's new order

New life comes through the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ

GAL 2:20 See also 2CO 5:16–5:17; EPH 2:4–2:7; COL 2:13

Jesus Christ's death and resurrection are the basis for a new moral life

ROM 6:11–6:13 See also ROM 6:1–6:7; 2CO 5:15; COL 2:20–3:11

Those who participate in God's new order are ``in Christ''

1CO 1:30 See also ROM 8:1–8:2; EPH 1:3–1:14 Paul extends the scope of the phrase “in Christ” to include believers, their activity, and the salvation they have received.

Both Jews and Gentiles are justified by faith

Paul stresses that salvation is by grace through faith alone

EPH 2:8–2:9 See also ROM 3:21–3:26, ROM 4:16, ROM 5:1–5:2

Jewish works of the law have no role in salvation

GAL 2:15–2:16 See also ROM 4:13–4:15, ROM 9:30–10:4; GAL 3:6–3:14; PHP 3:8–3:9

Both Jews and Gentiles are united in the one body of Christ

1CO 12:13 See also GAL 3:26–3:28; EPH 2:14–2:18, EPH 3:6

The Holy Spirit

His indwelling is an integral part of Christian experience

ROM 8:9 See also ACT 19:1–19:7; GAL 3:2–3:5 Paul's questions suggest that he identifies receiving the Spirit with becoming a Christian.

He equips the church with gifts

1CO 12:1–12:11 See also 1CO 14:1–14:33

He enables believers to relate to God as Father

GAL 4:6–4:7 See also ROM 8:14–8:17; EPH 2:18

He guides believers into a right understanding of the law

ROM 7:6 See also ROM 2:29, ROM 8:3–8:4; 2CO 3:3, 2CO 3:6

He overcomes believers' sinful human nature

ROM 8:13 See also ROM 8:5–8:8; GAL 5:16–5:25, GAL 6:8

He is the guarantee of eternal life

ROM 8:11 See also ROM 8:23; 2CO 5:4–5:5; EPH 1:13–1:14

The return of Jesus Christ

Paul lived in the hope of the forthcoming personal return of the risen Christ

PHP 3:20–3:21 See also 1CO 15:22–15:28; 1TH 4:14–4:17; 2TH 1:6–1:10

Believers are to be raised with Christ upon his return

1TH 4:14 See also 1CO 15:12–15:23

The whole created order will be renewed at the return of Jesus Christ

ROM 8:19–8:21 See also EPH 1:9–1:10

title: 5112: Peter
content: The foremost of the disciples of Jesus Christ during his lifetime and of the apostles after the resurrection.

title: 5113: Peter, the disciple
content:
The son of Jonas or John, he was called Simon until Jesus Christ gave him the name Peter meaning “rock”.

Peter's background and family

He lived in Capernaum

MAT 8:14 parallels MRK 1:29, LUK 4:38; ; JHN 1:44 He originally came from Bethsaida.

He was a fisherman by trade

LUK 5:10

Peter as Jesus Christ's disciple

He was called by Jesus Christ

MAT 4:18–4:20 parallel MRK 1:16–1:20; ; LUK 5:10; ; JHN 1:40–1:42

He witnessed Jesus Christ perform many miracles

MAT 8:14–8:15 parallels MRK 1:30–1:31, LUK 4:38–4:39; ; MAT 17:24–17:27; ; LUK 5:4–5:8; ; JHN 21:2–21:6

He was chosen to be with Jesus Christ on certain occasions

MAT 17:1–17:2 parallels MRK 9:2, LUK 9:28–9:29 at the transfiguration of Jesus Christ; ; MAT 26:36–26:37 parallel MRK 14:32–14:33 in the Garden of Gethsemane; ; MRK 5:37 parallel LUK 8:51

He sometimes acted as spokesman for the other disciples

He asked Jesus Christ to teach them: MAT 15:15, MAT 18:21; MAT 16:15–16:16 parallels MRK 8:29, LUK 9:20; ; JHN 6:69; MAT 17:4 parallels MRK 9:5, LUK 9:33 He asked Jesus Christ to prolong the transfiguration experience; ; MAT 19:27 parallels MRK 10:28, LUK 18:28; ; MRK 1:36–1:37; ; LUK 5:4–5:5; ; JHN 6:68

His impetuous nature interacted with his devotion to Jesus Christ

MAT 14:28–14:29 He wanted to walk to Jesus Christ on the water; ; MAT 16:22 parallel MRK 8:32 He tried to prevent Jesus Christ from going to his death; ; MAT 26:35 parallels MRK 14:31, LUK 22:33, JHN 13:37 He vowed that he was willing to die for Jesus Christ; ; JHN 13:6–13:8, JHN 18:10

He was the subject of both special commendation and rebuke

MAT 16:17–16:19 He was commended for his confession of faith in Jesus Christ; ; MAT 16:23 parallel MRK 8:33 He was rebuked for his opposition to Jesus Christ's prediction of his suffering; ; MAT 26:34 parallels MRK 14:30, LUK 22:34, JHN 13:38 He was warned that he would disown Jesus Christ; ; MAT 26:40–26:41 parallel MRK 14:37–14:38 He was rebuked for falling asleep in the Garden of Gethsemane; ; JHN 18:10–18:11, JHN 21:20–21:22

Peter's denial of Jesus Christ and his reinstatement

He denied that he knew Jesus Christ

MAT 26:69–26:74 parallels MRK 14:66–14:71, LUK 22:54–22:60, JHN 18:15–18:18, JHN 18:25–18:27

He repented of his denial

MAT 26:75 parallels MRK 14:72, LUK 22:61–22:62

The risen Christ appeared to him on his own

LUK 24:33–24:34; ; 1CO 15:4–15:5

He was reinstated by Jesus Christ in front of other disciples

JHN 21:15–21:17

title: 5114: Peter, the apostle
content:
As a result of the coming of the Holy Spirit, Peter was transformed into a dynamic apostle and witness to Jesus Christ.

Peter's credentials as an apostle

MAT 10:2; ; ACT 2:37, ACT 5:29; ; 1PE 1:1; ; 2PE 1:1

Peter as an apostle to the Jews

GAL 2:8

Peter's leadership

See also ACT 1:21–1:22, ACT 2:14, ACT 3:12, ACT 4:8, ACT 5:29, ACT 8:20

Peter and the Gentiles

He was the first to baptise Gentiles who had not been circumcised

ACT 10:47–10:48

He defended this action against critics

ACT 11:17, ACT 15:7–15:11

He later wavered in his attitude to the Gentiles

GAL 2:11–2:14

The miraculous power of the Holy Spirit at work in Peter

ACT 3:2–3:7, ACT 5:9–5:10, ACT 5:15–5:16, ACT 9:34, ACT 9:40, ACT 12:1–12:11 Peter himself experienced a miracle when imprisoned by Herod Agrippa.

Peter's missionary travels

1CO 1:12 He visited Corinth; ; 1CO 9:5 He took his wife with him; ; 1PE 1:1 He visited northern Asia Minor; ; 1PE 5:13 One interpretation of this verse is that Peter was writing from Rome and was using the name “Babylon” symbolically to refer to Rome.

content:
Peter preached mainly to the Jews. He taught both through his preaching and his letters.

Peter's commission

JHN 21:17

Referring to the death of Judas: ACT 1:16, ACT 1:20; ACT 2:16–2:20, ACT 2:25–2:28, ACT 2:34–2:35; ACT 3:22–3:23, ACT 4:11; 1PE 1:15–1:16, 1PE 1:24–1:25, 1PE 2:6–2:8, 1PE 3:5–3:6, 1PE 3:12, 1PE 3:14, 1PE 3:20, 1PE 4:18, 1PE 5:5; ; 2PE 2:5–2:9

ACT 4:12 See also ACT 2:38, ACT 3:19, ACT 10:43

Peter taught that God cared for all people

ACT 10:34, ACT 15:7–15:9

Peter wrote his first letter to encourage Christians

1PE 1:1, 1PE 5:12 See also 1PE 2:1 He exhorted them to live holy lives; 1PE 2:13–2:14 They must obey authority; 1PE 3:161PE 4:12–4:16, 1PE 4:19 1PE 5:10 God will vindicate and save his people.

Peter wrote his second letter to strengthen Christians who were at risk from false teaching

2PE 1:12 See also 2PE 1:16 He reminded them of the truth of the gospel; 2PE 2:3 He warned them of the judgment awaiting false teachers; 2PE 3:13 They must keep alive their hope in the coming day of the Lord.

title: 5117: Ruth
content:
A young Moabite widow, who, because of her selfless devotion to her mother-in-law Naomi, and to Naomi's God, gained a husband and a child, a place in Jewish history and became the great-grandmother of David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

Ruth faces the problems of widowhood

RUT 1:3–1:5 See also RUT 1:6–1:13

Ruth commits herself to Naomi

RUT 1:16–1:17 See also RUT 1:18, RUT 1:22, RUT 2:11

Ruth and Boaz

Boaz allows Ruth to glean in his fields

RUT 2:8–2:9 See also RUT 2:14–2:23

Ruth asks Boaz to be her ``kinsman-redeemer''

RUT 3:9 The kinsman-redeemer was the closest male relative who had responsibility to marry a widow within the family and thereby protect the interests of needy members of the extended family.

Boaz negotiates with a nearer relative of Ruth's

See also RUT 4:1–4:8

Boaz marries Ruth

RUT 4:9–4:10 See also RUT 4:11–4:13

She has a son who is presented to Naomi

RUT 4:13 See also RUT 4:17

Ruth is included in the genealogy of Jesus Christ

MAT 1:5–1:6

title: 5118: Solomon
content: The son of David and Bathsheba, who succeeded David as king of Israel. Noted for his great wisdom, Solomon was responsible for the building of the temple of the LORD. In his latter years, influenced by his many foreign wives, he turned to idolatry.

content:
Solomon succeeded his father David as king and secured Israel's stability through treaties with foreign powers.

Solomon's birth

content:
Solomon was a man of outstanding gifts and abilities. Initially he was approved by God, but the latter years of his reign were marred by idolatry and apostasy.

content:

Weapons carried on the back

1SA 17:6

Animals carry people and goods on their backs

ISA 30:6 See also EXO 15:1, EXO 15:21; 2SA 13:29, 2SA 16:1–16:2, 2SA 18:9, 2SA 19:26; 2KI 18:23 parallel ISA 36:8; ISA 21:7, ISA 30:16; JER 6:23; HAG 2:22; REV 9:17

content:

title: 5149: eyes
content:
The part of the body designed for seeing. In Scripture eyes are often associated with light, watchfulness or spiritual understanding, whereas blindness may be a metaphor for darkness, ignorance of God or rebellion against him. The eyes of God watch over all his creation.

title: 5150: face
content:
The main visual characteristic of a person. Facial features are recognisable as uniquely those of a particular person. The face also indicates mood and attitude. The showing or directing of the face towards someone or something may indicate regard, approval or determination, while hiding or turning away of the face indicates the opposite.

The face is the main recognisable feature of a person

Examples of facial recognition

MAT 26:71 parallels MRK 14:66–14:67, LUK 22:56 See also EST 5:2, EST 5:9; MAT 13:55 parallel MRK 6:3; MAT 14:35 parallel MRK 6:54; JHN 1:36, JHN 1:47–1:48

content:
Parts of the hand used in various kinds of activity, both good and bad. They were prominent in the OT sacrificial ritual, and were also used as a symbol for authority, accusation and minimum effort.

The front of the head between the eyes. Often used figuratively in phrases denoting a stubborn or persevering attitude. The forehead is the place where symbols of remembrance or allegiance can be placed. Such symbols may particularly represent allegiance to God or Satan.
