EXO 32:9 See also EXO 34:9; DEU 9:6, DEU 31:27; 2KI 17:14; NEH 9:16–9:29; PRO 29:1; JER 19:15; ACT 7:51

An outstretched neck as a sign of pride

ISA 3:16 See also PSA 75:5

Placing the foot on the neck as a sign of conquest

JOS 10:24

Ornaments were hung around the neck

See also PRO 3:3, PRO 6:20–6:21

A millstone placed around the neck as punishment

MAT 18:6 parallel MRK 9:42

resource.label: 7135: Israel, as the people of God

title: 5171: nose
content:
The nose as part of the human body

Human life is given and sustained through the nostrils

GEN 2:7 See also GEN 7:22; NUM 11:20; JOB 27:3; ISA 2:22

The nose and the sense of smell

GEN 27:27 See also JOB 39:25; SNG 4:11; DAN 3:27; AMO 4:10; 1CO 12:17

Animals snort and sniff through their noses

JOB 39:20, JOB 41:18, JOB 41:20; ; JER 2:24, JER 8:16

The nose and sneezing

2KI 4:35

The nose as an object of beauty

SNG 7:4

The nose may be adorned with rings

EZK 16:12 See also GEN 24:22, GEN 24:30, GEN 24:47; ISA 3:21

The nose is vulnerable to attack

PRO 30:33 See also EZK 23:25

Captives are led by rings or hooks in the nose

2KI 19:28 parallel ISA 37:29 See also 2CH 33:11; AMO 4:2

Contempt is communicated by means of the nose

PSA 10:5; ; ISA 57:4; ; MAL 1:13; ; LUK 16:14, LUK 23:35; ; ACT 17:32

Offence is taken, metaphorically, by the nose

People take offence

2SA 16:21 See also GEN 34:30; EXO 5:21; 2SA 10:6 parallel 1CH 19:6

God takes offence

ISA 65:5

God's power is indicated by the blast of his nostrils

EXO 15:8 See also 2SA 22:9 parallel PSA 18:8; 2SA 22:16 parallel PSA 18:15

Lifeless idols have noses

PSA 115:6 See also DEU 4:28

title: 5172: offal
content:
The internal organs of an animal, traditionally regarded as being inferior to meat, and used as a symbol of disgrace.

Offal is symbolic of disgrace

MAL 2:3 See also NAM 3:6

In animal sacrifices the offal was removed and burnt outside the camp

EXO 29:14 See also LEV 4:11–4:12, LEV 8:17, LEV 16:27; NUM 19:3–19:5, NUM 19:5

Jesus Christ bears the believer's disgrace

HEB 13:11–13:13

title: 5173: outward appearance
content:
That which is visible on the outside may reveal the true person, but is sometimes misleading. Judging by it and boasting in it are typical of sinful humanity. God sees the inner reality.

Outward appearance can reveal the truth

Spiritually

MAT 7:16–7:20 parallel LUK 6:43–6:45 See also MAT 5:16, MAT 12:33–12:37; JHN 15:8; JAS 2:17–2:18

Emotionally

PRO 15:13 See also 1SA 1:16–1:18; PRO 17:22; ECC 8:1; DAN 5:5–5:6; MRK 10:22

Outward appearance can be deceptive

MAT 23:25–23:28 See also ISA 29:13, ISA 53:2–53:3; MAT 7:15; LUK 11:39–11:41; 2CO 11:13–11:15; COL 2:23; HEB 13:2

While people may judge by outward appearance, God does not

People take note of outward appearance

JHN 7:23–7:24 See also LUK 16:14–16:15; JHN 8:15; 2CO 10:7; JAS 2:1–2:4; REV 3:17

God looks at the heart

1SA 16:6–16:7 See also 1KI 8:39 parallel 2CH 6:30; PSA 139:1–139:2; PRO 16:2, PRO 21:2; ISA 11:3–11:5; LUK 16:15; GAL 2:6; REV 2:23

The folly of boasting in outward appearance

LUK 20:45–20:47 See also MAT 6:2, MAT 6:5, MAT 6:16; 2CO 5:12; GAL 6:12

What is unseen is more important than outward appearance

2CO 4:16–4:18 See also PSA 51:6, PSA 147:10–147:11; ROM 2:28–2:29

Beautiful physical appearance

Examples of the problems and opportunities caused by beautiful outward appearance

GEN 12:11–12:15 Sarah's beauty led to Abraham's folly; ; GEN 39:6–39:7 Joseph's handsome appearance led to his being tempted by Potiphar's wife; ; 1SA 9:2, 1SA 16:12, 1SA 25:3; ; 2SA 11:2–11:3 Bathsheba's beauty tempted David; ; 2SA 14:25–14:26; ; EST 1:10–1:11, EST 2:7 Esther's beauty was an opportunity for God.

The cultivation of inner beauty encouraged

1PE 3:3–3:5; ; 1TI 2:9–2:10

title: 5174: prostration
content:
The act of falling down upon one's face in front of someone, as a gesture of fear or reverence before God or a person of high rank.

Prostration before God

In reverence or fear

NUM 20:6; 1CH 29:20; REV 7:11 See also GEN 17:3; LEV 9:24; NUM 24:4; 1SA 5:3; 1KI 18:39; NEH 8:6; EZK 1:28; MAT 2:11, MAT 17:6, MAT 26:39; LUK 5:12

As an expression of grieving over sin

DEU 9:18, DEU 9:25; ; JOS 7:6; ; ISA 15:3; ; EZK 9:8

Prostration before God's messenger

NUM 22:31 See also JOS 5:14; JDG 13:20; 1CH 21:16; DAN 8:17; LUK 24:5

Prostration before other people

1SA 24:8; ISA 51:23 See also RUT 2:10; 1SA 25:23, 1SA 28:14; 2SA 14:4, 2SA 19:18; ISA 49:23; DAN 2:46

title: 5175: reading
content:
The gaining of information through written documents. The Law was read regularly in the synagogue. Jesus Christ expected the Scriptures to be read. NT letters were read in the churches to which they were sent.

Reading of the Law to Israel

By Moses

EXO 24:7 See also DEU 31:10–31:11

By Joshua

JOS 8:34–8:35

By Josiah

2KI 23:2 parallel 2CH 34:30

In Ezra's time

NEH 8:2–8:3, NEH 8:18, NEH 9:3, NEH 13:1

Reading of the Law in the synagogue

ACT 15:21 See also LUK 4:16; ACT 13:15, ACT 13:27; 2CO 3:14–3:15

Other examples of reading

DEU 17:18–17:20; JER 36:6–36:8, JER 51:61; DAN 9:2 Daniel foresaw the end of the exile through reading the Scriptures.

Jesus Christ expected the Scriptures to be read

MAT 12:3–12:5 parallels MRK 2:25–2:26, LUK 6:3–6:4 See also MAT 19:4, MAT 21:16, MAT 21:42 parallels MRK 12:10–12:11, LUK 20:17; MAT 22:31, MAT 24:15 parallel MRK 13:14

Reading of NT letters

COL 4:16 See also ACT 15:31; 1TH 5:27

Reasons for reading the Scriptures

They are God-breathed

2TI 3:16

God's word is true

JHN 17:7

To understand the truth about Jesus Christ

LUK 24:26–24:27; ; EPH 3:4

To believe and be saved from God's wrath

JHN 20:31; ; 2TI 3:15

To learn how to serve and please God

PSA 119:105, PSA 119:130; ; 2TI 3:16; ; REV 1:3

They teach Christians and give them hope

ROM 15:4; ; 1JN 2:1, 1JN 2:12–2:14, 1JN 2:21

They enable Christians to discern truth from error

ACT 18:28 See also ACT 17:11; GAL 1:6–1:9; 2PE 3:14–3:16; 1JN 2:26, 1JN 4:1

resource.label: 2363: Jesus Christ, preaching and teaching of

title: 5176: ring
content:
An ornament or a status symbol, sometimes used in sacred furnishings or as a charm.

Rings worn as jewellery

Gold nose rings, worn especially by women

These were often given by a suitor as a symbol of betrothal: GEN 24:22, GEN 24:30, GEN 24:47; ; PRO 11:22; ; ISA 3:21; ; EZK 16:12

The signet ring as a sign of authority

GEN 41:42; ; NUM 31:50; ; EST 3:10, EST 3:12, EST 8:8; ; DAN 6:17; JER 22:24; ; HAG 2:23

Gold ear-rings, worn by men and women

Ear-rings were sometimes used as charms or amulets: GEN 35:4; ; EXO 32:2–32:3, EXO 35:22; ; JDG 8:24–8:25

Rings as indications of wealth or status

JOB 42:11; ; HOS 2:13; ; LUK 15:22; ; JAS 2:2

Rings used in sacred furnishings

On the ark of the covenant

EXO 25:12–25:15

On the table

EXO 25:26–25:27

In the tabernacle

EXO 26:24–26:29

On priestly garments

EXO 28:23–28:24

For carrying altars

EXO 27:4–27:7, EXO 30:4, EXO 37:27

title: 5177: robes
content:
A formal style of clothing, often indicating priesthood, royalty or elevated social status.

Priestly robes

Aaron's priestly robes

EXO 28:4 See also EXO 28:31–28:34, EXO 29:5, EXO 39:22–39:26; LEV 8:7; PSA 133:2

Other wearers of priestly robes

1SA 2:19; ; 1CH 15:27

Royal robes

The majestic robes of God

PSA 93:1; ; ISA 6:1, ISA 63:1

Robes for kings and queens

EST 5:1 See also 1KI 22:10 parallel 2CH 18:9; 1KI 22:30 parallel 2CH 18:29; EST 8:15; JON 3:6; ACT 12:21

Jesus Christ robed as a king and mocked

MRK 15:17 parallel MAT 27:28 See also JHN 19:2, JHN 19:5

Robes indicating office, favour or wealth

GEN 41:42 See also GEN 37:3; JOS 7:21; 1SA 18:4; 2SA 13:18; 1KI 10:25; EST 6:7–6:11; ISA 3:18–3:23, ISA 22:21; MIC 2:8; MRK 12:38; LUK 20:46, LUK 15:22

Robes associated with righteousness and purity

ISA 61:10 See also REV 6:11, REV 7:9, REV 7:13–7:14, REV 22:14

Tearing of robes to show mourning or repentance

JOB 2:12 See also 2CH 34:27

resource.label: 9414: heaven, as community of the redeemed

title: 5178: running
content:
Scripture gives pictures of running in both its literal and metaphorical senses, the image of the Christian life as a race being particularly significant.

Running away

Fleeing in battle

EXO 23:27 See also LEV 26:36–26:37; JOS 7:12, JOS 8:3–8:19; 1SA 14:20–14:22

Escaping from danger

PRO 18:10 See also GEN 19:12–19:22; NEH 6:10–6:11; ISA 10:1–10:3; JER 17:16, JER 48:4–48:6, JER 51:6, JER 51:44–51:45; AMO 2:14–2:16; JHN 10:12–10:13

Running away from individuals

1SA 19:11–19:12 See also GEN 16:6–16:8, GEN 31:20–31:21, GEN 39:11–39:15; JHN 10:2–10:5

Running away from God

JON 1:1–1:10

Running away from evil

2TI 2:22 See also 1CO 6:18, 1CO 10:14; 1TI 6:11

Running after people or things

PSA 16:4 See also RUT 3:10; ISA 5:11; JER 2:23–2:25; EZK 16:32–16:34; MAT 6:28–6:34 parallel LUK 12:27–12:31

Running in eagerness

JHN 20:1–20:4 See also 2CH 23:12; MRK 9:25; LUK 17:22–17:23; ACT 3:11, ACT 21:30

Running swiftly

JOB 9:25 See also JOB 39:13–39:18; ECC 9:11; JER 12:5

Heralds running ahead of a dignitary

1SA 8:11 See also 2SA 15:1; 1KI 1:5, 1KI 18:46

Messages carried by runners

2SA 18:19 See also 2SA 18:21–18:32; 2KI 4:25–4:31, 2KI 5:20–5:23, 2KI 9:1–9:3; PSA 147:15; JER 23:21; HAB 2:2; ZEC 2:3–2:5

The life of the believer likened to running a race

GAL 2:2 See also PSA 119:32; PRO 4:10–4:12; ISA 40:30–40:31; ACT 20:24; 1CO 9:24–9:27; GAL 5:7; PHP 2:14–2:16; 2TI 4:6–4:8; HEB 12:1; 2JN 1:9

title: 5179: sandal
content:
A form of open shoe worn in warm climates, and the only form of foot-covering to be of major importance in Scripture. Both the wearing and the removal of sandals is often seen as symbolic; to go barefoot was often a sign of shame, mourning or poverty.

Sandals were normally worn by an official, soldier or messenger

1KI 2:5; ; EPH 6:15

Untying and carrying sandals was the task of a servant

MAT 3:11 parallels MRK 1:7, LUK 3:16, JHN 1:27 John considers himself unworthy even to be a slave of Jesus Christ. See also ACT 13:25

The removal of sandals as a gesture

As a mark of respect in the presence of God

EXO 3:5 See also JOS 5:15; ACT 7:33

To show rejection of any claim to property

DEU 25:9–25:10; ; RUT 4:7–4:8; ; PSA 60:8 parallel PSA 108:9

To predict the defeat and disgrace of Egypt and Assyria

ISA 20:2–20:4

As a sign of mourning and repentance

2SA 15:30; ; EZK 24:17, EZK 24:23; ; MIC 1:8

The symbolic use of sandals

As symbols of readiness for action

EXO 12:11

As symbols of oppression and injustice

See also AMO 2:6, AMO 8:6

Fine sandals as a status symbol

EZK 16:10; ; LUK 15:22

Sandals as an example of the need for minimum possessions in God's service

MAT 10:10 parallels MRK 6:9, LUK 10:4; ; LUK 22:35

title: 5180: shaving
content:
The removal of hair with a razor or other sharp implement. Both male and female Israelites allowed their hair to grow long. Barbers trimmed, but did not crop, men's hair, so giving special significance to the shaving of the head or whole body. These actions indicated shame or grief.

Personal toilet

GEN 41:14; ; 2SA 14:26

Symbolic shaving

Shaved head a sign of grief

JOB 1:20 See also DEU 21:10–21:14; ISA 15:2; JER 47:5, JER 48:36–48:37; EZK 27:31; AMO 8:10; MIC 1:16; JER 7:29, JER 41:5

A shaved head a sign of shame

2SA 10:4 parallel 1CH 19:4 See also EZR 9:3; ISA 7:20, ISA 50:6; JER 2:16; EZK 7:18; 1CO 11:5–11:6

Shaving in ritual cleansing

LEV 14:8–14:9; ; NUM 8:7; ; ACT 21:24

Shaving as a visual aid

EZK 5:1–5:4

After a period of dedication

NUM 6:18

Shaving forbidden

As a pagan practice

LEV 19:27, LEV 21:5 See also DEU 14:1 Pagans shaved the front of their heads as a sign of mourning. God's people should have a different attitude to bereavement from those who have no hope; EZK 44:20

For the sake of a Nazarite vow

NUM 6:5 See also JDG 16:17; 1SA 1:11

title: 5181: sitting
content:
A bodily posture associated with resting, eating or instruction. When used of God, the image often conveys the idea of kingly authority over creation.

Sitting to rest

GEN 18:1; JHN 4:6 See also EXO 2:15, EXO 17:12; 1KI 19:4; MAT 26:36

Sitting to eat

EXO 32:6; LUK 17:7 See also JDG 19:6; RUT 2:14; 1SA 20:24; PRO 23:1; JER 16:8; MAT 14:19; 1CO 10:7

Sitting to teach or to learn

MAT 5:1–5:2 See also MAT 13:2; MRK 9:35; LUK 2:46, LUK 10:39; JHN 8:2

Sitting for prayer

JDG 21:2 See also 2SA 7:18

Sitting as a sign of authority

Human authority

EXO 11:5 See also 1KI 1:13, 1KI 3:6; 2KI 10:30; ZEC 6:13; MRK 10:37

Divine authority

PSA 29:10 See also 1KI 22:19; PSA 47:8, PSA 80:1; ISA 6:1; MAT 26:64; LUK 20:42; HEB 1:3, HEB 10:12, HEB 12:2; REV 3:21, REV 4:10, REV 7:10

Sitting to judge

EXO 18:13; MAT 25:31 See also 2SA 19:8; PRO 20:8; ISA 28:6; JER 38:7; DAN 7:26; JOL 3:12; MAT 27:19; LUK 22:30; ACT 23:3

Sitting as a sign of possession and peace

MIC 4:4 See also ZEC 3:10

Jesus Christ seated at God's right hand

LUK 22:69; ; EPH 1:20, EPH 2:6; ; COL 3:1

resource.label: 2363: Jesus Christ, preaching and teaching of

title: 5182: skin
content:
The outer covering of the body. Diseased skin is often subject to pain and regarded as unclean.

Skin as the outer covering of the body

JOB 10:10–10:11 See also GEN 3:21, GEN 27:11; EZK 37:6, EZK 37:8

Violence against the skin

MIC 3:2–3:3 See also JOB 2:4–2:5

Skin and bones

PSA 102:5 To be reduced to skin and bones is a mark of severe suffering. See also NUM 4:8–4:14 animal skins used for covering the ark of the Testimony; JOB 19:20; LAM 3:4, LAM 4:8

Skin diseases

Skin diseases are painful

JOB 30:30 See also JOB 7:5, JOB 18:13; LAM 5:10

They can be defiling

NUM 5:2–5:3 See also LEV 13:1–13:11, LEV 13:43–13:46, LEV 22:4

As God's punishment for sin

NUM 12:10–12:11 Miriam; ; 2KI 5:26–5:27 Naaman; ; 2CH 26:19–26:20 Uzziah

Healed by Jesus Christ

MAT 8:2–8:3 parallels MRK 1:40–1:42, LUK 5:12–5:13; ; LUK 17:12–17:14

Skin cannot be changed

JER 13:23

A person can know God even when the skin has been destroyed

JOB 19:26–19:27

title: 5183: smell
content:
An aroma; God is pleased by the aroma of sacrifice, whether a literal sacrifice or the figurative offering of Christian service is a picture of its acceptability to him. Bad smells can indicate physical decay or the results of judgment. To be a stench to someone is to be held in contempt or hated by that person.

The aroma of sacrifice

GEN 8:21 See also LEV 1:9, LEV 2:2, LEV 3:5, LEV 4:31, LEV 6:15, LEV 6:21, LEV 8:21, LEV 23:13, LEV 23:18; NUM 15:14, NUM 15:24 offerings to be made for unintentional breaking of the LORD's commandments; NUM 18:17, NUM 28:2, NUM 29:2

Substances to create a pleasing smell

EXO 30:7–30:8 See also EXO 30:22–30:29, EXO 30:34–30:38, EXO 35:28, EXO 37:29, EXO 40:26–40:27; NUM 4:16; 2CH 2:4, 2CH 13:11

The aroma of sacrifice is not always pleasing to God

LEV 26:31; ; EZK 8:11–8:13, EZK 20:27–20:29

Jesus Christ was the supreme fragrant offering

EPH 5:2

God accepts his people as fragrant incense

EZK 20:41 See also HOS 14:5–14:6

A pleasing aroma depicts acceptable Christian service

2CO 2:14–2:16 See also PHP 4:18

Fragrance associated with the expression of love

SNG 1:2–1:3, SNG 4:16–5:1 The beloved's garden is an image of her body. See also PSA 45:8; SNG 1:12–1:13, SNG 3:6, SNG 4:10–4:11, SNG 5:13, SNG 7:8JHN 12:3

A bad smell

Indicating decay

JHN 11:39 See also EXO 16:20 Manna soon smelled bad if kept. This meant the Israelites had to trust God afresh for each day's supply.

As the result of God's judgment

The first plague on Egypt, which made the Nile smell bad: EXO 7:18, EXO 7:21; ISA 34:3; ; AMO 4:10

As a picture of the results of judgment

ISA 3:24, ISA 19:6; ; JOL 2:20

As a figurative cause of contempt or hatred

GEN 34:30; ; EXO 5:21; 1SA 13:4; ; 2SA 10:6 parallel 1CH 19:6; ; 2SA 16:21

Idols cannot smell

PSA 115:4–115:6 See also DEU 4:28

title: 5184: standing
content:
The bodily posture of being in a stationary upright position.

Standing as a sign of authority

ACT 7:55

Standing merely to wait or rest

EXO 33:21 See also JOS 3:8; 1KI 20:38; MAT 12:47, MAT 20:3, MAT 26:73; LUK 19:24; JHN 8:9

Standing ready for action

NUM 22:23; ACT 5:23 See also DEU 10:8; JOS 5:13; 1SA 17:16; 1CH 21:16; LUK 1:11; ACT 16:9; REV 7:1

Standing to show respect or honour

DAN 2:2 See also 1KI 10:8, 1KI 22:19; 2CH 6:3; NEH 8:4; JER 36:21; DAN 10:11

Standing in the presence of God

In heaven

LUK 1:19 See also ZEC 6:5; REV 7:9, REV 8:2

On earth

GEN 19:27; EXO 3:5; NEH 9:5 See also EXO 33:10; DEU 4:10, DEU 29:10; 1SA 1:26; 1CH 23:30; 2CH 20:9; PSA 24:3; JER 28:5; MAT 6:5; MRK 11:25; LUK 18:11; ROM 14:4

EXO 18:13; ROM 14:10 See also NUM 5:16, NUM 35:12; DEU 19:17; 1SA 12:3, 1SA 12:7; ZEC 3:1; MAT 27:11; LUK 11:32; ACT 23:6, ACT 25:10; REV 20:12

Standing firm as a believer

PRO 10:25; 1CO 15:58 See also LUK 21:28; ROM 5:2, ROM 11:20; 1CO 15:1, 1CO 16:13; 2CO 1:21, 2CO 1:24; GAL 5:1; PHP 4:1; COL 4:12; 2TH 2:15; JAS 5:8; 1PE 5:12

Against evil and temptation

1CO 10:13; ; EPH 6:11–6:14

Against enemies and opposition

PSA 94:16 See also EXO 14:13; 2CH 20:17; ISA 7:9; JER 1:17; EPH 6:11–6:14; PHP 1:27

God's purpose will stand

ISA 46:10 See also ISA 14:24

Standing in the gap

EZK 22:30 See also PSA 106:23

title: 5185: stomach
content:
As well as the physical stomach, the term is used in association with God's judgment or in a figurative sense.

Stomach as part of the physical body

1CO 6:13 See also JOB 40:16; SNG 7:2; DAN 2:32

Jonah in the stomach of a huge fish

MAT 12:40 See also JON 1:17–2:1

Ritual laws concerning the stomach

MRK 7:18–7:19 parallel MAT 15:17 See also LEV 11:41–11:45

Afflictions of the stomach

LUK 15:16 hunger; ; 1TI 5:23 illness

Fatal wounding in the stomach

JDG 3:21; ; 2SA 2:23, 2SA 3:27, 2SA 4:6, 2SA 20:10

The stomach and God's judgment

Severe stomach pain

JER 30:6–30:7 See also NUM 5:20–5:22, NUM 5:27

Crawling on one's stomach as a sign of submission

GEN 3:14 Part of God's curse upon Satan. See also PSA 72:9; ISA 49:23, ISA 65:25; MIC 7:17

Hunger as a result of God's judgment

MIC 6:14 See also JOB 20:12–20:15, JOB 20:20–20:23; PRO 13:25; ISA 9:20; EZK 7:19

An empty stomach as a warning

AMO 4:6

The stomach and God's blessing

In the OT a full stomach was one sign of God's blessing: PSA 34:9–34:10, PSA 37:19, PSA 37:25; ; PRO 10:3

Figurative uses of the stomach

Stomach as a symbol of inner thoughts

EZK 3:3 See also PRO 18:8, PRO 26:22; REV 10:9–10:10

Stomach as a symbol of worldliness

PHP 3:19 See also ROM 16:18

Stomach as something to be filled

PRO 18:20 See also JOB 15:2; JER 51:34

title: 5186: stumbling
content:
Faltering or falling in the course of running or walking. The term is also used metaphorically to refer to failure, hesitation or difficulty.

Physical stumbling

LEV 19:14; LEV 26:37; ; ISA 21:4; ISA 28:7 through drunkenness; NAM 2:5, NAM 3:3

God protects his people from stumbling

PSA 56:13 See also 1SA 2:4; JOB 4:4; PSA 37:24, PSA 116:8

The enemies of God's people will stumble

JER 20:11 See also PSA 9:3, PSA 27:2

God's people will stumble if they sin

ISA 8:14; ; JER 13:16

Avoiding stumbling by keeping God's law

PSA 119:165 See also PRO 3:23, PRO 3:26, PRO 4:11–4:12; ISA 26:7–26:8, ISA 40:30–40:31

The wicked stumble because they reject God's way

PRO 4:19; ; HOS 14:9

Causes of stumbling

Dishonesty

ISA 59:14

Arrogance

JER 50:32; ; HOS 5:5

False teaching by religious leaders

HOS 4:5; ; MAL 2:8

Idolatry

JER 18:15

Trust in riches

EZK 7:19

Trust in secular political alliances

ISA 31:3

Stumbling as a consequence of sin and divine judgment

Making one's own stumbling-block

EZK 14:3–14:4, EZK 14:7

Stumbling over obstacles sent by God

JER 6:21, JER 13:16; ; EZK 3:20

Some stumbling is educative or disciplinary

DAN 11:35; ; ROM 9:32–9:33

Jesus Christ as the light that prevents believers from stumbling

JHN 9:5, JHN 11:9–11:10

Jesus Christ as a stumbling-block for unbelievers

1CO 1:23 See also 1PE 2:8

Stumbling and sin

All sin and stumble

JAS 2:10, JAS 3:2

None should feel superior to others

PRO 24:17; ; 1CO 10:12

None should cause others to stumble

ROM 14:20; ; 1CO 10:32

title: 5187: taste
content:
The act of tasting is used figuratively of experiencing the goodness of God and his word and of a variety of experiences: misery, sin, wisdom, love, death and blessing.

The taste of food or drink

EXO 16:31 See also GEN 25:28, GEN 27:4, GEN 27:7, GEN 27:9, GEN 27:14, GEN 27:17, GEN 27:31; NUM 11:7–11:8; 2SA 19:34–19:35; JHN 2:9

COL 2:20–2:22

Taste used figuratively

Of the experience of misery

JOB 6:6–6:7 In his complaint against God, Job compares the unacceptability of his lot to inedible food. See also JOB 27:2

Of the experience of the goodness of God

content:

title: 5195: veil
content:
Generally, an item of female dress worn by an unmarried woman in the presence of her future husband and also by a prostitute. Head-coverings were worn by men and women as a sign of mourning. The term is also used metaphorically to indicate a lack of understanding of God's truth. Scripture uses the imagery of “removing a veil” to refer to God's final self-revelation at the end of the age, or the making known of God's will and nature through Jesus Christ or other means.

The veil as an item of female dress

Worn by women in general

SNG 4:1 The veil covered the lower part of the face, so focusing attention on the eyes and temples. See also GEN 24:65 Rebekah veils herself in the presence of her future husband, Isaac; SNG 4:3, SNG 6:7

Worn by prostitutes

GEN 38:14–38:15 See also SNG 1:7

Worn by female sorcerers

EZK 13:18, EZK 13:21

Worn as a sign of wealth and status

ISA 3:19, ISA 47:2 Babylon's veil will be removed as a mark of her humiliation.

2SA 15:30 See also LEV 13:45 A veil worn by the ceremonially unclean signifies grief at separation from God; JER 14:4

Veils customarily worn by mourners

2SA 19:4 See also EZK 24:17, EZK 24:22

content:
Scripture expressly forbids making false accusations, but God's people have often been subjected to them and many false accusations were made against Jesus Christ.

False accusation forbidden

Satan associated with false accusation

ZEC 3:1 Although taken as a proper name in English, “Satan” is in fact simply the Hebrew word meaning “accuser”. See also JOB 1:6–1:12; REV 12:10

Examples of false accusation

In the OT

PSA 41:5–41:6 See also GEN 39:7–39:18; 2SA 10:1–10:3; 1KI 21:7–21:14; EZR 4:6–4:16; NEH 6:5–6:7; PSA 35:19–35:20

title: 5204: age
content:
The number of years reached or expected to be reached in a human life. The span of life is determined by God and may be divided into distinct phases, each with its own characteristics. The term may also refer to an era of history, particularly in contrasting the present age with the coming age to be inaugurated at Jesus Christ's return.

The span of life

In God's hands

MAT 6:27 parallel LUK 12:25 See also 1SA 2:6; PSA 139:16; ECC 8:8; JAS 4:14–4:15

title: 5205: alliance
content:
The coalition of two or more parties in order to achieve a particular aim. Political alliances might be formalised in a treaty or sealed by marriage. Human rebellion against God is demonstrated in hostile alliances against his people culminating in the rejection of Christ and the final gathering and overthrow of the nations outside Jerusalem. Because God's people are to depend on him alone, unholy alliances are condemned; however God does work in partnership with human allies and encourages his people to work together.

As sons as a blessing from God

content:
Skilful, creative work, carried out using a variety of materials. Purposes included decoration, ornamentation and representation of objects of worship, the last of which Scripture firmly condemns.

Decorative panelling

1KI 7:34–7:37 See also EXO 28:9–28:12, EXO 28:15–28:21, EXO 28:36–28:38, EXO 39:6–39:7, EXO 39:8–39:14, EXO 39:30–39:31; 1KI 7:31, 1KI 7:36; 2CH 2:5–2:7, 2CH 2:13–2:14

Forbidden

2KI 21:7 parallel 2CH 33:7 See also EXO 32:1–32:4; JDG 17:1–17:6, JDG 18:11–18:31; ISA 46:1–46:2; JER 50:1–50:2; EZK 8:9–8:12

Condemned

HAB 2:18 See also EXO 34:10–34:14; NUM 33:51–33:52; DEU 7:25–7:26; 2CH 34:1–34:4; ISA 44:9–44:20; EZK 7:20–7:22; HOS 13:1–13:3; MIC 5:13–5:14; NAM 1:14

content:
Artistic skills, usually practised by craftsmen and passed on from generation to generation, of which a wide variety are mentioned in Scripture.

Metalwork

EXO 39:2–39:3 See also EXO 31:1–31:5 parallel EXO 35:30–35:33; 1SA 13:19–13:21; 1KI 7:13–7:14; ISA 41:7; JER 10:9; ACT 19:23–19:41

Stonework

Building

1CO 3:10–3:15 See also 2CH 34:11; EZR 3:10; ISA 9:8–9:10; AMO 5:11; HEB 3:3–3:4

Pottery

Carpentry

Engraving

EXO 36:19 parallel EXO 26:14 See also EXO 35:22–35:23

Tanning

ACT 9:43 See also ACT 10:5–10:6, ACT 10:32–10:33

Making idols

LEV 26:1 See also 2KI 17:14–17:16; ISA 40:18–40:20, ISA 41:5–41:7, ISA 44:9–44:20

title: 5213: assembly
content:
Assemblies of the Israelites

LEV 23:1–23:2 See also EXO 35:1; LEV 4:14, LEV 8:1–8:5; NUM 10:1–10:7, NUM 15:35–15:36, NUM 16:45–16:47; 1SA 7:5; 1KI 8:22; 1CH 15:3; 2CH 29:28; EZR 3:1; PSA 22:25, PSA 40:9–40:10, PSA 149:1; AMO 5:21

Assembling armies for war and groups for self-protection

JDG 20:2 See also JDG 10:17; 1SA 7:6, 1SA 13:5, 1SA 17:2; EST 8:11, EST 9:16

Assemblies of the Christian church

ACT 14:27 The Greek word for “church” can also be translated “assembly”. See also MAT 16:18; ACT 13:1–13:2, ACT 14:23; 1CO 11:18, 1CO 14:23, 1CO 16:19

Assemblies for other purposes

ACT 19:39 See also LUK 23:1; ACT 19:32, ACT 19:41, ACT 23:7

title: 5214: attack
content:
A violent act of aggression often associated with intent to invade, sometimes as an act of retribution and occasionally as a strategic act of self-defence. Scripture also recognises the possibility of spiritual aggression through attack by evil forces.

Examples of God's people attacking others

GEN 14:14–14:16 Abraham attacks the captors of the king of Sodom; ; JDG 7:19–7:21 Gideon attacks the Midianites; ; 1SA 14:13–14:14 Jonathan attacks the Philistines; ; 2SA 5:6–5:7 parallel 1CH 11:4–11:5 David attacks the Jebusites; ; DEU 20:1–20:20 Moses gives detailed instruction on going to war.

The Israelites attack the inhabitants of Canaan

JOS 6:2, JOS 6:20 See also JOS 8:1–8:3, JOS 8:21–8:22, JOS 10:9–10:10, JOS 10:29–10:42, JOS 11:7–11:8, JOS 11:16–11:23

Examples of God's people attacked by others

By the Amalekites

EXO 17:8–17:13

By the Midianites

See also JDG 6:1–6:6

By the Ammonites

JDG 10:9, JDG 11:4–11:6; ; 2SA 10:8 parallel 1CH 19:9; ; 2CH 20:1

By the Philistines

1SA 7:7 See also 2SA 5:17, 2SA 5:22 parallels 1CH 14:8, 1CH 14:13; PSA 56:1–56:2

By Syria (Aram)

1KI 20:1 See also 1KI 20:26; 2KI 3:21–3:27 the Moabites seek to attack Israel but are routed; 2KI 5:2, 2KI 6:24–6:25, 2KI 12:17; 2CH 16:1–16:4, 2CH 28:5

By the Egyptians

2CH 12:1–12:4, 2CH 12:7–12:9

Attacks on God's people resulting in exile

Israel attacked by the Assyrians

2KI 17:3–17:6 See also 2KI 18:9–18:12

Judah attacked by the Babylonians

2CH 36:5–36:7 parallel 2KI 24:1 See also 2KI 24:10–24:16, 2KI 25:1, 2KI 25:8–25:11 parallel 2CH 36:15–36:20; JER 32:24; EZK 33:21

God's people attack each other

Intertribal warfare

JDG 9:22–9:23, JDG 9:39–9:45, JDG 20:18–20:48

The north (Israel) and south (Judah) attack each other

2KI 14:11–14:14 parallel 2CH 25:20–25:24 See also 2CH 13:1–13:3

Attacks within the church

JAS 4:1–4:2 See also PHP 3:2; 1TH 5:15; JAS 4:11–4:12; 1PE 3:9

Examples of individuals who were attacked

GEN 4:8; ACT 16:22 See also EXO 21:12–21:20; 1SA 19:9–19:10, 1SA 24:7

The danger of attack by Satan and his agents

1PE 5:8–5:9 See also MAT 4:1–4:11 parallel LUK 4:1–4:13; EPH 6:12; REV 11:7

God provides protection against both physical and spiritual attack

EPH 6:13–6:18 See also PSA 7:10, PSA 18:1–18:3, PSA 138:7; 2TI 4:18

title: 5215: authority
content: The right to act or speak in certain ways, in accordance with the authorisation of a higher power. All human authority derives from God, and is to be exercised in a responsible manner.

title: 5216: authority, nature of
content:
The God-given freedom of action expressed in rightful power to control the actions of others.

Ultimate authority belongs to God, who does as he pleases

PSA 115:3 See also 2CH 20:6; JOB 9:12, JOB 23:13, JOB 42:2; PSA 135:6; ISA 14:27, ISA 43:13, ISA 45:9, ISA 46:10; DAN 4:35 Nebuchadnezzar acknowledges God's authority; ROM 9:19–9:21; EPH 1:11 God's authority is demonstrated in election.

Human authority

All human authority is given and established by God

ROM 13:1 See also DAN 2:21, DAN 4:17, DAN 5:18–5:21; JHN 19:11

It involves the rightful freedom to give orders

MAT 8:9 parallel LUK 7:8 The centurion to Jesus Christ. See also GEN 41:35; NUM 27:20; DEU 1:15 Moses delegates authority; JDG 9:29; EZR 7:24; NEH 3:7; EST 9:29; ISA 22:21; JER 38:10; MAT 25:23 parallel LUK 19:17 the parable of the talents; MRK 13:34; LUK 20:20, LUK 23:7; JHN 19:10ACT 9:14, ACT 26:10, ACT 26:12 1PE 2:13

It is limited, unlike God's authority

JHN 19:10–19:11

Responsibilities of those with authority

They are to act as servants, not lording it over people

MAT 20:25–20:28 parallel MRK 10:42–10:45 See also JHN 13:4–13:15

Their authority is to be used for the benefit of others

2CO 10:8 See also 2CO 13:10

It is sometimes necessary to withhold exercising authority for others' good

1CO 9:4–9:18 See also 1CO 6:1–6:7, 1CO 8:8–8:13, 1CO 10:23–10:24

Examples of the authority of believers

Authority over possessions

ACT 5:4 Peter to Ananias regarding the land he sold.

Authority over the will

1CO 7:37 Paul on marriage.

Authority to become children of God

JHN 1:12

The authority of the law over believers during their lifetime

ROM 7:1

title: 5217: authority, in the church
content:
The exercise of freedom under Jesus Christ's authority for the good of the church.

Supreme authority belongs to Jesus Christ as head of the church

EPH 5:23 See also EPH 1:22, EPH 4:15, EPH 5:24; COL 1:18

Spiritual authority under Jesus Christ in the church is possessed by elders

As shepherds who teach and care for the flock

ACT 20:28 See also JHN 21:15–21:17; EPH 4:11–4:13; 1TI 3:2, 1TI 5:17; TIT 2:1–2:10; 1PE 5:2

As overseers ruling the church

ACT 20:28 See also ROM 12:8; 1TH 5:12 Those serving as overseers must rule their own homes well; 1TI 5:17

The response of the church to the authority of elders

Elders are to be obeyed

HEB 13:17

Elders are to be honoured and respected

1TH 5:12–5:13 See also 1TI 5:17

Paul limits the authority of women in the church

1TI 2:12 Some believe Paul's restriction to apply to the women in the Ephesian church who were seizing authority rather than having been granted it. Others believe Paul is prohibiting women from being official teachers in the assembled church. See also 1CO 11:5–11:6, 1CO 11:10, 1CO 14:33–14:37

The reason for this prohibition derives from God's order of creation

1TI 2:13–2:14 See also 1CO 11:3, 1CO 11:7–11:10

Kinds of authority within the church

Authority to preach the gospel

MAT 28:18–28:19; ; MRK 16:15

Authority to excommunicate

MAT 18:15–18:18; ; 1CO 5:1–5:5 “hand this man over to Satan” here means “send back into the world ruled by Satan”; ; 1CO 5:9–5:13

Authority to forgive sins

MAT 18:18; ; JHN 20:23

resource.label: 2212: Jesus Christ, head of the church

title: 5218: authority, in the home
content:
The exercise of God-given authority within the husband-wife and parent-child relationships.

A husband is given headship over his wife

EPH 5:23

The basis for this headship

God's headship over Jesus Christ

1CO 11:3

Jesus Christ's headship over the church

EPH 5:23

God's order of creation

1CO 11:8–11:9 See also GEN 2:20–2:22

This headship has been affected by the fall

GEN 3:16

How this headship is to be exercised

Lovingly and sacrificially

EPH 5:25 See also EPH 5:28, EPH 5:33; COL 3:19; 1PE 3:7

As Jesus Christ rules as head of the church

EPH 5:25–5:29

Regarding his wife as part of himself

EPH 5:28–5:29 See also 1PE 3:7

Christian wives are to submit to their husbands

EPH 5:22 parallel COL 3:18

They are to follow the example of the submission of the church to Jesus Christ

EPH 5:24

Fathers are heads of their families

GEN 18:19 See also GEN 35:2; JOS 24:15; EPH 6:4; 1TI 3:4, 1TI 3:12; TIT 1:6

Fathers' authority is to be exercised reasonably

EPH 6:4 See also COL 3:21

The response of children to parental authority

Obedience

EPH 6:1 parallel COL 3:20 See also PRO 6:20, PRO 23:22

Respect

EPH 6:2–6:3 See also DEU 5:16; EXO 20:12, EXO 21:15, EXO 21:17; DEU 27:16; PRO 19:26, PRO 20:20; MAT 19:19 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20

Kinds of authority within the family

Authority to discipline

PRO 19:18 See also PRO 23:13, PRO 29:17

Authority to teach

PRO 1:8 See also PRO 3:1, PRO 13:1

Authority to command

COL 3:20 parallel EPH 6:1 See also PRO 6:20–6:23

title: 5219: authority, of human institutions
content:
The exercise of God-established freedom to regulate society for the good of its members.

Without authority sin is unrestrained

ROM 1:24–1:26 See also GEN 6:5 This was before the giving of the law; JDG 21:25; ROM 13:4

All human authorities are instituted and established by God

ROM 13:1–13:2 See also GEN 9:5–9:6; DAN 2:21, DAN 2:37–2:38, DAN 4:17, DAN 5:18–5:21, DAN 5:26; JHN 19:11; 1PE 2:13

Rulers are God's servants to do good and restrain evil

ROM 13:4 See also ISA 45:1; JER 25:9, JER 27:6, JER 43:10; ROM 13:6; 1TI 2:2; 1PE 2:14

The proper response to human authorities

They are to be obeyed by everyone

ROM 13:1 See also ECC 8:2; MAT 22:17–22:21 parallels MRK 12:14–12:17, LUK 20:22–20:25; ROM 13:5–13:7; TIT 3:1; 1PE 2:13–2:14

They are to be honoured and respected

PRO 24:21 See also ROM 13:7; 1PE 2:17

They are not to be obeyed if their demands conflict with the law of God

ACT 4:19 See also EXO 1:17; 1KI 21:3; DAN 3:18, DAN 6:12; MAT 22:21 parallels MRK 12:17, LUK 20:25; HEB 11:23

They are to be prayed for

1TI 2:1–2:2 See also JER 29:7

Christians are to use rights granted by the authorities

ACT 16:35–16:39, ACT 22:22–22:29, ACT 25:1–25:12

title: 5220: authority, abuse of
content:
The misuse of a person's freedom of action in order to exploit, oppress or treat other people in a way that is not for their good.

Warnings against the abuse of authority

By employers over employees

EPH 6:9 See also LEV 25:43; DEU 24:14

By fathers over children

EPH 6:4 parallel COL 3:21

By husbands over wives

COL 3:19

By elders over the church

1PE 5:2–5:3 See also EZK 34:2–34:7

By those mistreating foreigners

EXO 22:21 See also EXO 23:9

By leaders over those who are led

MAT 20:25–20:27 parallel MRK 10:42–10:44 See also LUK 22:25–22:26

By those taking advantage of the helpless or poor

EXO 22:22 See also PRO 22:22; EZK 22:29; ZEC 7:10

By those who oppress others

JER 22:17 See also PSA 73:8, PSA 119:134; EZK 22:7

Examples of the abuse of authority

GEN 16:6 See also EXO 1:11; 1KI 12:14; JAS 2:6

title: 5222: baking
content:
Cooking in an oven or over an open fire. Bread baked in this way was the staple diet of the population in biblical times. Bricks were also sometimes produced by baking.

Baking bread

In ovens

LEV 26:26 See also EXO 8:3; LEV 7:9, LEV 11:35

Over open fires

1KI 19:6 See also ISA 44:14–44:19; EZK 4:9–4:15; JHN 21:9

Unleavened bread

EXO 12:39 Bread was usually baked with yeast, but where there was insufficient time for kneading and proving, the raising agent was omitted. See also GEN 19:1–19:3; LEV 6:14–6:17; 1SA 28:24

Baking of offerings

LEV 2:4–2:10 See also LEV 6:14–6:18, LEV 7:9–7:10, LEV 23:15–23:18, LEV 24:5–24:6; 2KI 4:42

Baking of manna

EXO 16:21–16:23

Baking of clay

DAN 2:32–2:33 See also GEN 11:3; DAN 2:41–2:43

Bakers

At home

GEN 18:6 See also LEV 26:26 Women baked at home or in communal ovens; 2SA 13:6–13:8

At royal courts

1SA 8:13 See also GEN 40:1–40:22, GEN 41:10

In the temple

1CH 9:31 See also 1CH 23:28–23:29; EZK 46:20

As tradesmen in towns

JER 37:21 See also HOS 7:4

title: 5223: banner
content:
Generally, a standard raised in battle as a rallying point for armies. God is described as Israel's banner in recognition of his powerful defence of his people. The Messiah will raise a banner to rally the scattered exiles of Israel.

Israel's tribes identified by banners

NUM 2:2 See also NUM 1:52, NUM 2:17, NUM 2:34, NUM 10:14

Banners carried into battle

Battle standards carried by armies

PSA 20:5 See also PSA 74:4; SNG 6:4; ISA 30:17 Banners to rally armies were often set up on the top of a hill; JER 4:21

The LORD as Israel's banner

EXO 17:15–17:16 The LORD is the rallying point for Israel and the source of the nation's confidence in battle. See also PSA 60:4–60:6

God's banner raised against his people

ISA 5:25–5:26 God raises a banner to rally nations to battle against Israel. See also JER 4:6, JER 6:1

God's banner raised against the nations

ISA 13:2–13:5 See also ISA 18:3, ISA 31:9; JER 50:2, JER 51:12, JER 51:27–51:28

The Messiah as a banner to the peoples

ISA 11:10–11:12 See also ISA 49:22, ISA 62:10; ZEC 10:8; JHN 12:32

Other references to banners

SNG 2:4 The king's love is like a banner, displayed for all to see; ; EZK 27:7 a banner made from embroidered linen

title: 5224: barn
content:
Barns were associated with industry and prosperity

Full barns were a sign of blessing

PRO 3:9–3:10 See also DEU 28:8; PSA 144:12–144:15

Empty barns were a sign of poverty

HAG 2:15–2:19

The priority of spiritual over material prosperity

LUK 12:15–12:21 See also MAT 6:25–6:26; LUK 12:23–12:24

God's barn is a metaphor for the kingdom of heaven

LUK 3:16–3:17 parallel MAT 3:11–3:12 See also MAT 13:24–13:30

title: 5225: barrenness
content:
A lack of fertility, especially the inability of a woman to conceive.

Barren land

Barrenness describes waste and unproductive land

JER 2:6 See also DEU 32:10; JOL 2:20

Barren land as a sign of God's disfavour

GEN 3:18 Thorns and thistles are often used to designate barren or unproductive land. See also HOS 10:8; HEB 6:8

Fertility, as opposed to barrenness, a sign of God's blessing

EXO 23:25–23:26 Consequently, the inability to conceive was regarded as a sign of God's displeasure. See also DEU 7:13–7:14, DEU 11:14–11:15; PSA 113:9; ISA 41:18ISA 54:1; GAL 4:27

The barren woman

Her desire for children

GEN 30:1–30:2 See also PRO 30:16

Examples of barren women

GEN 16:1 Sarah; ; GEN 29:31 Rachel; ; JDG 13:3 Manoah's wife; ; 1SA 2:5 Hannah; ; LUK 1:7 Elizabeth; ; LUK 1:36–1:37 The ability to bear a child in these circumstances, especially in old age, was seen as a sign of God's blessing and his miraculous power.

Barrenness was sometimes seen as a sign of God's disfavour

GEN 16:1–16:4, GEN 20:17–20:18, GEN 29:31–29:34; ; 1SA 1:1–1:20; ; ISA 4:1; ; LUK 1:5–1:25

Childlessness was not always the result of barrenness

DEU 28:41

Barrenness might be an advantage in some circumstances

LUK 23:29 Referring to the disasters about to come upon Jerusalem.

Metaphorically, barrenness may describe an unproductive or desperate condition

HEB 6:7–6:8 See also JOB 3:7; LUK 13:6–13:9

title: 5226: basin
content:
A receptacle for liquids, often used for washing or purification rites.

Basins used as receptacles

EXO 12:22 A basin is used to collect the blood of sacrifices. See also EXO 24:6; LEV 14:5, LEV 14:50

Basins used for ritual washing

Between the altar and the Tent of Meeting

EXO 30:18, EXO 40:11, EXO 40:30; ; LEV 8:11

In Solomon's temple

2CH 4:6 See also 1KI 7:30, 1KI 7:38 parallel 2CH 4:14; 2KI 16:171KI 7:40; JER 52:17–52:18

A basin used for ritual washing

JHN 13:5

title: 5227: basket
content:
Flat, open baskets to carry bread

In the chief baker's dream

See also GEN 40:16–40:18

For offering unleavened bread

EXO 29:23 parallel LEV 8:26 See also EXO 29:2–29:3 parallel LEV 8:1–8:2; NUM 6:15–6:17

Baskets used to hold food

To store household provisions

DEU 28:5 Signifying the continued provision of food for the household. See also DEU 28:17

To collect food

MAT 14:20 parallels MRK 6:43, LUK 9:17, JHN 6:13 See also MAT 13:48, MAT 15:37 parallel MRK 8:8; MAT 16:9–16:10 parallel MRK 8:19–8:20

Baskets used to carry fruit

JER 24:1–24:2 See also DEU 23:24; PSA 81:6; AMO 8:1–8:2

Other uses of baskets

EXO 2:3–2:5 Moses is put into a papyrus basket; ; DEU 26:2–26:4 firstfruits presented in a basket; ; 2KI 10:7 the heads of Ahab's sons sent to Jehu in baskets; ; ZEC 5:6–5:11 The wickedness of Jerusalem is removed, figuratively, to Babylon in a basket.; ACT 9:25; ; 2CO 11:33

title: 5228: battering-rams
content:
Battering-rams used to make breaches in the walls of besieged cities

Historic references to the breaking down of walls

2SA 20:15 The wall of Abel Beth Maacah. References to breached or broken walls are evidence that the use of battering-rams was common; ; 2KI 14:13 parallel 2CH 25:23; ; JER 39:2 parallels 2CH 36:19, JER 52:7; ; NEH 1:3

Figurative references to the breaking down of walls

PSA 89:40 referring to God's displeasure with David's dynasty

Prophetic references to the breaking down of walls as a picture of the LORD's power

ISA 22:5, ISA 24:12; ; EZK 21:22, EZK 26:9; ; MIC 2:13

Peace is symbolised by no breaching of walls

PSA 144:14

Model battering-rams were part of the symbolic representation of the siege of Jerusalem

EZK 4:2

title: 5229: bed
content:
A household item of furniture set aside for sleep, rest and quietness.

Various kinds of bed

DEU 3:11; AMO 6:4; ACT 9:34 See also MAT 9:6 parallels MRK 2:11–2:12, LUK 5:18–5:19; MRK 2:4 parallels MAT 9:2, LUK 5:24; ACT 5:15

The bed as a place of rest

2KI 4:10 See also 1SA 3:2; 2SA 4:5, 2SA 4:7, 2SA 11:13; EST 7:8; JOB 33:15; PSA 139:8; PRO 7:16–7:17, PRO 26:14; ISA 28:20 Beds were not always comfortable; DAN 4:5, DAN 7:1; LUK 11:7

The bed as a place of recuperation

PSA 41:3; ACT 28:8 See also GEN 48:2; EXO 21:18; 2SA 13:5; 1KI 17:19; 2KI 1:4, 2KI 4:21; JOB 7:13–7:14, JOB 33:19; DAN 8:27; MAT 8:14 parallel MRK 1:30; REV 2:22

The bed as a place in which to be alone

PSA 4:4; MIC 2:1 See also 1KI 21:4; 2KI 6:12, 2KI 11:2; PSA 6:6, PSA 63:6; ECC 10:20

The bed representing sexual union

DEU 22:30; HEB 13:4 See also GEN 39:7; DEU 27:20; 2SA 13:11; 1CH 5:1; EZK 22:10, EZK 23:17

Unusual places used as beds

GEN 28:11; ; 1KI 19:5; ; JON 1:5; ; MRK 4:38

Bed associated with a description of apostasy

ISA 57:7

title: 5230: beggars
content:
People in great need who appeal for help, both from others and from God.

Appeals for material help

2KI 6:26 During a time of famine; LUK 16:3 See also 2KI 8:3–8:5; JOB 19:16, JOB 24:4–24:5, JOB 29:11–29:12; PSA 37:25 never having to beg seen as God's blessing; PSA 109:10 begging seen as God's judgment; LAM 4:4

Appeals for mercy from others

title: 5269: cornerstone
content:
A stone that can be in the foundation, above ground level or at the summit of the roof (the “capstone”). The cornerstone of a large building gives it a reliable and firm foundation, leading to the cohesion and stability of the whole building. In Scripture, such foundation-stones are taken as symbolic of the basis of faith in Jesus Christ and the church. Jesus Christ is thus represented as both the foundation upon which the church is built, and the capstone which crowns the whole.

content:

content:
Imagination and skill used in the expression of visual or performing arts. Human creativity has its source in God, but may be used either to his honour or dishonour.

content:
Money or goods lent under pledge of repayment (with or without interest). In the spiritual sense, Jesus Christ's righteousness is credited to believers.

title: 5275: cremation
content:
The burning of a dead body. Cremation was not practised by Israel or the first Christians. In difficult circumstances a corpse might be burnt and the remains buried

Cremation of corpses

1SA 31:12–31:13 This was done to prevent any further abuse of the bodies by the Philistines. David later reburied the remains in a family grave (see 2Sa 21:12–14).

Burning a body as a punishment

See also LEV 20:14, LEV 21:9; JOS 7:15, JOS 7:25; 2KI 23:20

These were not for the purpose of cremating the king's corpse, but public demonstrations in his honour: 2CH 16:14; ; JER 34:5

title: 5276: crime
content:
An offence against the established laws of society including murder, adultery, theft, perjury and treason. Scripture contains both warnings and teaching to help young people avoid a life of crime.

Crime in Israel

DEU 6:1–6:2 Crime in Israel was the breaking of laws given by God.

title: 5280: crown
content:
An encircling ornament for the head, worn by monarchs as symbol of royal authority. Also a wreath, worn on joyful occasions or presented to the winner of a race. Used figuratively, the word indicates honour and blessing, the reward awaiting believers in heaven.

By kings

2KI 11:12 parallel 2CH 23:11 Crowns worn by the kings of Israel and Judah signified their consecration to God. See also 2SA 1:10; PSA 89:39, PSA 132:18; PRO 27:24; ZEC 9:16

By queens

EST 1:11, EST 2:17

2SA 12:30 parallel 1CH 20:2 See also PSA 21:3; ISA 23:8; JER 13:18; EZK 21:26; ZEC 6:11, ZEC 6:14; REV 12:3, REV 13:1, REV 19:12

title: 5281: crucifixion
content:
A most painful, cruel and protracted form of execution which involved the victim being roped or nailed to an elevated wooden cross. This form of execution was favoured by the Romans, who regarded it as a deterrent to political rebellion against the authority of Rome at the time of Jesus Christ.

The victim was scourged before crucifixion

JHN 19:1 parallels MAT 27:26, MRK 15:15, LUK 23:22 See also LUK 23:16

The victim carried his cross

JHN 19:17 MAT 27:32–27:33; ; MRK 15:21–15:22; ; LUK 23:26

The victim was fixed to the cross

LUK 23:33 parallels MAT 27:35, MRK 15:24, JHN 19:23 See also JHN 20:25

A charge board was fixed to the cross

MAT 27:37 parallels MRK 15:26, LUK 23:38, JHN 19:19

The victim's sufferings were protracted

MAT 27:54 parallels MRK 15:39, LUK 23:47JHN 19:32–19:33, JHN 19:34 See also MRK 15:25, MRK 15:33, MRK 15:37

content:
A drinking vessel, usually made of pottery but sometimes, in wealthy households especially, of gold or silver. Cups might take the form of goblets or of shallow bowls large enough for several people to share, as a sign of fellowship. The word is also used figuratively to refer to the portion of blessing or judgment divinely allotted to individuals or nations.

content:

content:

title: 5338: holiday
content:
A day or period of time during which regular work is suspended. title: 5347: injustice
content: The unnecessary and unjustified ill treatment of others, through false accusation or through the inflicting of pain or punishment. Having its origin in Satan, it works through the sinful human heart and shows itself in every sphere of life. It merits the wrath of God.

title: 5350: injustice, hated by God
content:

PSA 43:1 There are some OT passages where vengeance upon persecutors is called for (e.g., Ps 35:1–8; Ps 69:22–28; Jer 11:18–20; 18:19–23). These are called “imprecatory”. They arose from zeal for God's honour and from the desire for moral stability in society. They reflect an under-developed view of God's ultimate judgments and the failure to distinguish between the guilty and their innocent families. In the light of the NT the motives behind these prayers may be applauded but it is recognised that now they are best expressed in the denunciation of injustice accompanied by gospel witness, through which the hearts of oppressors are changed, leaving the matter of judgment as God's prerogative alone. title: 5359: justice
content: A concern to act rightly, and to be seen by others to act rightly. Divine justice embraces every aspect of the right ordering of human society according to the will of God, its creator.

title: 5360: justice, of God
content:
The moral righteousness of God is revealed in his laws and expressed in his judicial acts. God's commands and judgments meet perfect standards of justice, and his apportioning of punishments and rewards is also perfectly just. God's justice is impartial. Special praise is his for vindicating the penitent and the needy who have no human champions. Ultimately, all God's ways will be seen as just and equitable.

content:

title: 5368: kingship
content: The sovereignty and rule of a king. Scripture stresses that all human authority derives ultimately from God, and that human kings are required to acknowledge and respond to this divine authority.

content:

content:
The means of communication shared in common by groups of people. Scripture teaches that the diversity of languages in the world is a result of sin, but the outpouring of the Holy Spirit in Acts broke down the barriers of language and nationality.

Aramaic

Aramaic in the OT

2KI 18:26 parallel ISA 36:11 Aramaic is a language related to Hebrew, known from Assyrian times. Under the influence of the Persian empire Aramaic was the diplomatic language in later OT times. In Palestine, by the time of the NT, it was spoken widely, having largely displaced Hebrew as the everyday language of the Jews. See also EZR 4:7 The text of Ezr 4:8–6:18 and 7:12–26 is in Aramaic; JER 10:11 The text of Jer 10:11 is in Aramaic; DAN 2:4 The text of Da 2:4–7:28 is in Aramaic.

2KI 18:26 parallel ISA 36:11 Hebrew was the language of Israel in the period of the OT. By the time of the NT, it had been partially displaced in everyday use by Aramaic. See also 2KI 18:28 parallels 2CH 32:18, ISA 36:13; REV 9:11, REV 16:16

Greek

JHN 19:20 Greek was the major cultural and commercial language of the eastern Mediterranean world. The NT was written in this language, ensuring the rapid spread of the gospel in this region. See also ACT 21:37–21:39; REV 9:11

title: 5375: law
content: The God-given regulation of the life of the people of God in relationship with him. As the command of God, it enables and gives shape to the relationship between God and human beings on the one hand, and between fellow human beings on the other.

title: 5376: law, purpose of
content:
The law covers and regulates every area of life of the covenant people of God in accordance with the commands of God. Although the laws may be divided into categories of civil, criminal, social and cultic (or ritual) law, these distinctions are not clear-cut, and occasionally overlap with one another.

The origins of the law

Law as God's command is found in the story of creation

GEN 2:16–2:17

The law expresses the covenant relation between God and his people

DEU 4:44–4:45, DEU 5:1 See also EXO 20:1–20:17 parallel DEU 5:6–5:21; DEU 10:12–10:13, DEU 30:1–30:16

The purpose of the law

The law shows the proper response to the holiness of God

LEV 19:2

The law ensures that the people continue to receive the blessings of the covenant promises

DEU 6:24–6:25 See also GEN 22:17–22:18; EXO 20:12; DEU 6:3–6:7

Breaking the law leads to forfeiting the covenant blessings

JER 11:9–11:11 See also EXO 32:1–32:4

The law deepens the believer's knowledge of God through meditation

PSA 1:1–1:2 See also DEU 6:2; PSA 19:7–19:14, PSA 119:25–119:32, PSA 119:105–119:120

The law will finally be written on believers' hearts

JER 31:33 See also EZK 11:19–11:20

Justice

DEU 16:20

Righteousness

DEU 16:18

Holiness

LEV 19:2

Love

title: 5377: law, Ten Commandments
content:
The basic laws given to Israel through Moses following the exodus from Egypt (Ex 20:1–17; Dt 5:6–21). The first four commandments safeguard Israel's special relation to God; the remaining six protect individuals within the community and promote their well-being.

The Ten Commandments are to govern the life of Israel as the people of God

Israel should obey God alone

EXO 20:2–20:3 parallel DEU 5:6–5:7 See also DEU 6:13–6:15

Idolatry forbidden

EXO 20:4–20:6 parallel DEU 5:8–5:10 See also EXO 32:1–32:8; LEV 19:4; 1CO 10:7

God's name should not be misused

EXO 20:7 parallel DEU 5:11 See also MAT 7:21

A day of rest is commanded

EXO 20:8–20:11 parallel DEU 5:12–5:15 See also EXO 16:23; LEV 19:3; ISA 56:2; JER 17:21–17:22

Parents are to be honoured

EXO 20:12 parallel DEU 5:16 See also MAT 15:4; EPH 6:1–6:3

EXO 20:13 parallel DEU 5:17 See also GEN 4:8–4:16; MAT 5:21

title: 5378: law, OT
content:
OT laws and legal traditions govern every aspect of the life of the covenant people of God.

Kinds of OT law

Criminal law

EXO 21:12–21:14 Criminal law deals with crimes against persons punishable by a court.

Civil law

DEU 16:18–16:20 Civil law deals with the upholding in court of legally established rights against possible abuse. See also DEU 15:12–15:18

Social law

EXO 22:21–22:22 Social law deals with behaviour or standards of behaviour which are not strictly enforceable in the courts. See also DEU 24:19–24:22

Cultic law

Cultic law deals explicitly with the ritual or religious life of the people of God. Leviticus chapters 1–7 are totally devoted to this kind of law: LEV 1:10–1:13, LEV 4:13–4:21, LEV 7:11–7:18

Examples of OT law

Conditions for freeing servants

title: 5380: law, and gospel
content:
The law, which bears witness to the grace of God, points ahead to its fulfilment and climax in the gospel of Jesus Christ. The gospel does not abolish the law, but fulfils it, by allowing it to be seen in its proper light.

Human beings cannot fulfil the law by their own efforts

ROM 3:20; GAL 2:15–2:16 See also ACT 13:39; ROM 4:13–4:15

The law brings knowledge of human sin and the need for redemption

ROM 3:20, ROM 5:20 See also 1TI 1:9–1:10; 1JN 3:4

The law points to the coming of Jesus Christ

GAL 3:24

Believers are not justified by works of the law, but through faith in the blood of Jesus Christ

ROM 3:28; GAL 3:11 See also HAB 2:4; ROM 4:1–4:5; GAL 3:10–3:14; EPH 2:15

Dying to the law through Jesus Christ

title: 5381: law, letter and spirit of
content:

content: Solemn, binding promises, the truth of which are affirmed by appeal to God as witness. God himself makes solemn oaths to individuals. Scripture makes clear that oaths should be made wisely and not be broken.

content:

ACT 17:24–17:28 See also ECC 12:1; REV 4:11

Epicureanism

Paul meets some Epicureans in Athens

ACT 17:16–17:18 Followers of the Greek philosophy founded by Epicurus (341–270 B.C.). In strong contrast to the Stoics, they taught that pleasure, and the avoidance of all disturbance, pain and fear, was the chief goal of life.

Epicureans' assessment of Paul and his message

ACT 17:18, ACT 17:18 Paul's listeners mistook the Greek word for “resurrection” (“anastasis”) for the name of a strange god. While Epicureans did not deny the existence of gods, they believed they had no interest in the lives of human beings, and that therefore everything in life was the result of mere chance.

Epicurean and Stoic philosophers bring Paul to the Areopagus

ACT 17:19–17:20

The response of Epicureans and others to Paul's preaching

ACT 17:32

Docetism

Docetism questions the reality of the incarnation

2JN 1:7 Docetism is a denial of the physical reality of Jesus Christ's incarnation that may have been prompted by the typically Greek perception of physical matter as evil. See also 1JN 2:22–2:23JHN 1:14; 1TI 3:16; HEB 2:14ROM 8:3; PHP 2:6–2:8; 1JN 4:10

Docetic views are identified as heretical

1JN 4:1–4:3 See also JHN 6:53–6:56

Gnosticism

Contrary to the teaching of Gnosticism, the world is not inherently evil

1TI 4:4 Gnosticism was a religious philosophy whose fundamental belief in the inherent evil of the created realm led to a number of heretical teachings about creation, human nature, the person of Jesus Christ, salvation and ethics. GEN 1:31; ; NEH 9:6; ; PSA 19:1; ; ACT 17:24; ; COL 1:15–1:17; ; REV 4:11; ROM 8:20–8:21; ; EPH 1:9–1:10; ; COL 1:19–1:20

Contrary to the teaching of Gnosticism, human beings are not sparks of divinity trapped in evil, fleshly bodies

ACT 17:26 GEN 1:26–1:27, GEN 2:7; ; PSA 8:3–8:8; ROM 6:12–6:13, ROM 8:22–8:23, ROM 12:1; ; 1CO 6:12–6:18, 1CO 6:19–6:20; ; 1TH 5:23; ROM 8:10–8:11; ; 1CO 15:35–15:44; ; 2CO 5:1–5:4; ; PHP 3:20–3:21; ; 2TI 2:16–2:18

Contrary to the teaching of Gnosticism, Jesus Christ did not merely appear in human form

JHN 1:14 LUK 24:36–24:43; ; COL 2:9; ; HEB 2:14; ; 1JN 1:1–1:3, 1JN 4:2–4:3; ; 2JN 1:7; JHN 19:33–19:34; ; 1CO 2:8; ; PHP 2:6–2:8; ; COL 1:19–1:22; ; 1JN 5:6

Contrary to the teaching of Gnosticism, salvation is not found simply in a divine revelation of special knowledge

Salvation is by faith in the crucified Christ: 1CO 3:18–3:20; ; COL 2:8, COL 2:18–2:19; ; 1TI 6:20–6:21; 1CO 1:18–1:25; ; COL 1:19–1:20, COL 2:2–2:4, COL 2:8–2:10; ; 2PE 1:3

Contrary to the teaching of Gnosticism, Christian behaviour is not to be marked by licence and ritualistic self-denial

There is no value in empty ceremonial observance or ritualistic self-denial: MAT 15:10–15:11 parallel MRK 7:14–7:15; ; ROM 14:5–14:6; ; COL 2:16–2:17, COL 2:20–2:23; ; 1TI 4:1–4:5; 1CO 6:12–6:20; ; GAL 5:13; ; COL 3:5–3:14; ; TIT 1:15–1:16; ; 1PE 2:16; ; 1JN 1:5–1:6, 1JN 2:3–2:6, 1JN 3:3–3:10; ; JUD 1:4

Stoicism

Paul encounters the Stoics in Athens

ACT 17:16–17:18 The Stoics were a leading philosophical group based, like their rivals the Epicureans, in Athens. Stoics held that God was the inner reason of the universe and that salvation lay in accepting one's place in the established order.

Stoics ridicule Paul

ACT 17:18

Stoics misunderstand Paul's message

ACT 17:18

Paul presents a view of God very different from that of the Stoics

ACT 17:24–17:25 In contrast to Stoic belief God is the Creator; ACT 17:26–17:27 In contrast to Stoic belief God is a personal being.

Response of the Stoics to Paul's message

ACT 17:32–17:34

title: 5445: potters and pottery
content:
Pottery was in common use for both household and ceremonial utensils, though for sacred use precious metals were often preferred. Broken pottery symbolises worthlessness and judgment. The potter formed clay with his hands on a wheel which he turned with his feet. The descriptions of God as a potter and of his people as clay emphasise God's sovereignty and also his concern for what he has made.

Potters in Scripture

title: 5446: poverty
content: The state of being without material possessions or wealth. Scripture indicates that poverty is contrary to God's intention for his people, and that those who are poor and destitute are to be treated with special consideration and compassion.

title: 5459: prince
content:

title: 5466: promises
content: Binding offers or commitments on the part of one person or people to another. The value of such promises depends upon the reliability and trustworthiness of the person who makes the promises. Scripture stresses the total reliability of God, including his promise to bestow his Spirit and urges believers to demonstrate the same trustworthiness in their dealings with one another.

title: 5467: promises, divine
content:
The promises of God reveal his particular and eternal purposes to which he is unchangeably committed and upon which believers can totally depend. These promises are, however, conditional upon obedience on the part of believers.

God's promises are irrevocable

He is absolutely trustworthy

NUM 23:19 See also TIT 1:2; HEB 6:13–6:18

He is unchanging

PSA 110:4; ; MAL 3:6–3:7; ; JAS 1:17–1:18

ISA 55:11 See also ROM 4:21

JOS 21:45, JOS 23:14–23:15; ; 1KI 8:56; ; PSA 145:13; ; HEB 10:23

His promises stem from his goodness and glory

GEN 22:15–22:18 See also GEN 26:3; ISA 45:23; AMO 6:8, AMO 8:7

title: 5468: promises, human
content:
Believers must be faithful in keeping promises made to others and to God, because they have been called to live in integrity and truth. False or broken promises are considered as sin.

Examples of promises between people

GEN 14:22–14:24 Abraham and the king of Sodom; ; GEN 21:22–21:24 Abraham and Abimelech; ; GEN 47:29–47:31 Jacob and Joseph; ; NUM 30:1–30:16 in family life; ; JOS 2:12–2:21 Rahab and the spies

title: 5471: proof
content: A confirmation and verification of a belief, such as belief in the existence of God, in the trustworthiness of a witness or in the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

title: 5472: proof, as evidence
content:
In the judicial sense, evidence is required to confirm the testimony of a witness. In the lives of believers, practical evidence should be obvious as proof of the reality of their faith.

The Mosaic law required proof to be offered in various legal contexts

In giving testimony

DEU 19:15 See also EXO 23:2; LEV 5:1; DEU 17:6

In acccusations of immorality

DEU 22:13–22:21 See also NUM 5:11–5:31

content:

title: 5475: property
content: The ultimate source of all property is God. While property is entrusted to human beings, they have responsibilities towards God as a result of their stewardship.

title: 5477: property, land
content:

title: 5482: punishment
content: A form of physical pain or deprivation, generally in proportion to the offence which gives rise to it. Scripture stresses the reality of punishment by God for sin, while urging that human punishment should be humane.

title: 5483: punishment, nature of
content:
Punishment is the inevitable and equitable consequence of breaking the law of God. In keeping with God's justice and righteousness, punishment is administered by him or by human beings as his agents.

God warned Adam and Eve of the punishment for disobedience

GEN 2:16–2:17 See also GEN 3:1–3:5

Adam and Eve's original disobedience brought inevitable punishment

Upon the serpent

GEN 3:14–3:15 See also COL 2:15; REV 12:9, REV 20:1–20:3, REV 20:10

Upon the woman

GEN 3:16 See also PSA 48:6; ISA 13:8, ISA 21:3; JER 4:31; 1TI 2:14–2:15

Upon the man

GEN 3:19 See also JOB 5:7, JOB 7:1; PSA 90:5, PSA 90:7, PSA 90:8; ECC 1:3; ISA 40:2

Upon creation

GEN 3:17 See also GEN 5:29; JER 12:4; ROM 8:19–8:22

The punishment of death

ROM 6:23 See also EZK 18:4, EZK 33:8; ROM 5:12, ROM 6:21; 1CO 15:21–15:22

Banishment as punishment

GEN 3:23 See also GEN 4:10–4:16; DEU 29:27, DEU 29:28; 2KI 25:21; MAT 8:12

Punishment must be appropriate to the crime

GEN 9:6 See also EXO 21:23–21:25; LEV 24:17–24:22; JDG 9:24

EXO 22:3 See also EXO 21:2, EXO 21:26–21:27, EXO 22:4–22:9

content:
God's chastening of his children and his judgment on impenitent sinners and supernatural evil powers.

title: 5487: queen
content:
In OT times the chief wife of a king's harem or a female monarch. A queen mother, as a king's widow and the mother of the reigning king, would have held a position of some authority and influence.

A queen as the wife of a king

A chief wife among several

EST 2:17 See also EST 1:9–1:12, EST 2:4

Enjoying a position of some influence

EST 1:15–1:18, EST 2:22, EST 5:12, EST 7:5–7:8

Enjoying the king's special favour

EST 5:2–5:3 See also EST 7:1–7:3, EST 8:1, EST 8:7, EST 9:12; SNG 6:8–6:9; NEH 2:6; PSA 45:9

Sometimes granted considerable authority

EST 9:29 See also EST 9:31

The queen of Sheba

content:
A person's seniority and/or status, especially in military, government or priestly positions. Christians should not be concerned about rank or status.

title: 5490: refuge
content:
A safe retreat; a place of healing and renewal; also a stronghold from which to launch a counter-attack.

Idolatry

ISA 44:9 See also DEU 32:31, DEU 32:37–32:38

Human support

JER 17:5 See also PSA 20:7–20:8, PSA 142:4; ISA 30:1–30:2; ZEC 4:6; PHP 3:3

JER 6:14 See also EZK 13:10–13:12; MAT 7:26–7:27; REV 6:15–6:17

DEU 33:27 See also 1SA 2:2; 2SA 22:32; PSA 18:31, PSA 46:1, PSA 62:6–62:7; JHN 10:28–10:29; ROM 8:31–8:32, ROM 8:38–8:39; PHP 4:7

Fugitives driven from home because of personal, political or religious persecution, or because of physical danger.

title: 5492: restitution
content:
The return of something lost or stolen so that the original situation is restored. This central theme of the OT law is supremely fulfilled through Jesus Christ making restitution for Adam's sin, thus restoring fellowship with God and hope of eternal life.

Reasons for restitution

For crimes committed

EXO 22:2–22:3 See also EXO 22:7, EXO 22:16–22:17; LEV 6:1–6:6, LEV 24:17–24:21; NUM 5:6–5:7; EZK 33:14–33:15

For accidental loss

EXO 22:5–22:6 See also EXO 21:33–21:34, EXO 22:10–22:15

For unintentional sin

LEV 5:14–5:16

As part of confession

NUM 5:5–5:7

In cases of misplaced accusation

PSA 69:4

The basis of decisions regarding restitution

Arbitration

EXO 22:8–22:9

The amount of restitution is to exceed the amount stolen

EXO 22:1 See also EXO 22:4; LEV 6:5; 2SA 12:5–12:6; PRO 6:31

Land should belong to its rightful owners

2SA 9:7

Examples of restitution

1SA 6:17 The Philistines make restitution for desecrating the ark of God; ; 1KI 20:34 Ben-Hadad makes restitution for the cities his father had taken from Israel; ; 2KI 8:1–8:6 The king makes restitution to the Shunammite by returning her house and land; ; NEH 5:10–5:12 Nehemiah orders restitution to be made to the poor; ; LUK 19:8–19:9 Zacchaeus makes restitution to those he had cheated.

The act of restitution is to be motivated by love

ROM 13:8–13:10 See also MAT 5:23–5:24, MAT 5:44; COL 3:13–3:14

God promises physical restitution

ISA 57:18, ISA 61:3–61:4; ; JER 30:17–30:18

Jesus Christ makes restitution for sin

He restores fellowship with God

ROM 5:19 See also 2CO 5:21; HEB 9:28

1CO 15:21–15:22 See also 1CO 15:45–15:49

Restitution is made to Jesus Christ

PHP 2:8–2:9 Here God's exaltation of Jesus Christ is seen as restitution to his position of glory. See also ISA 53:10–53:12

Restitution is made to those who make sacrifices for the gospel

MAT 19:21 parallels MRK 10:21, LUK 18:22 See also MAT 19:29 parallels MRK 10:29–10:30, LUK 18:29–18:30; MRK 8:35 parallels MAT 16:25, LUK 9:24; JHN 12:24–12:25; PHP 3:8–3:10

title: 5493: retribution
content:
Recompense for evil. In Scripture this is the prerogative of God and of the authorities ordained by God, and never of individuals.

The principle of retribution

EXO 20:5–20:6; ROM 12:19; HEB 10:30 See also DEU 32:35; EXO 32:33–32:34; LEV 26:23–26:25; DEU 7:9–7:10, DEU 32:41–32:43; JOB 34:11; PRO 24:12; ISA 1:24; NAM 1:2

Divine retribution is just

GEN 18:25 See also DEU 32:3–32:4; 2CH 12:1–12:6; PSA 58:10–58:11; JER 5:7–5:9, JER 5:26–5:29; HOS 4:6

Retribution is often built into the nature of wrongdoing

PSA 7:15–7:16 See also PSA 37:14–37:15; PRO 1:18, PRO 26:27, PRO 28:10; ECC 10:8; MAT 26:52; GAL 6:7–6:8

Retribution is placed in the hands of governments

GEN 9:6; EXO 21:23–21:25 This “lex talionis” (law of exacting like for like) was not for private retribution. It insisted that justice be fair and not out of proportion to the crime; ROM 13:4 See also LEV 24:17–24:22; NUM 35:16–35:25; 1PE 2:14

Private retribution is forbidden

PRO 24:29 See also MAT 5:38–5:39; ROM 12:19

Prayer for retribution

PSA 28:4 Christians can agree with these prayers, hating all that opposes the Lord and goodness, and gladly anticipating the ultimate vindication of God's glory. Christians leave judgment in God's hands, but nonetheless grieve over the world's pain and over the death of every unrepentant sinner; 2TH 1:6–1:10 See also PSA 79:10, PSA 94:1–94:2, PSA 137:8–137:9; LAM 3:64–3:66

The final retribution

REV 20:13 See also PSA 62:11–62:12; JHN 5:28–5:29; ROM 2:5–2:11

GEN 3:14, GEN 3:17 See also GEN 3:15–3:16, GEN 3:18–3:19

In the flood

GEN 6:5–6:7

See also GEN 11:5–11:7

JDG 1:7, JDG 9:56–9:57; ; 2SA 18:17; 2KI 9:7, 2KI 9:24, 2KI 9:30–9:33

Natural retribution

ROM 1:27; 2TI 3:13

Examples of retribution by the state

See also JOS 7:25; 1KI 2:31–2:32; EST 7:10; LUK 23:40–23:41

JOS 10:13–10:14; ; JDG 11:36; ; EST 9:5 The special case of God's dealings with the nation of Israel and her enemies is not a basis on which to argue for a concept of a war, just or otherwise. A just war has to be in defence of the nation or of the defenceless, and involve a minimum of suffering.

Warnings of future retribution

ACT 17:31 See also MAT 25:31–25:32

title: 5494: revenge
content: The returning of injury or insult. Scripture insists that human revenge is unacceptable and is to be left in the hands of God.

title: 5495: revenge, and retaliation
content:
Scripture teaches that it is wrong to strike back or to return evil for evil, whether by immediate retaliation or by taking revenge later. Justice must be done, but this must be left in the hands of God, or of the authorities ordained by God.

OT teaching about revenge

Revenge forbidden in the OT

GEN 4:15; LEV 19:18; DEU 32:35; PRO 20:22 See also DEU 19:5–19:7, DEU 19:11–19:13, DEU 23:7; PRO 24:29; JER 29:7

The ``lex talionis'' (law of exacting like for like)

EXO 21:23–21:25 This was not a rule for personal revenge but to ensure that judicial punishments were neither unjust nor malicious. See also LEV 24:17–24:21; DEU 19:18–19:21

Personal revenge forbidden in the NT

By Jesus Christ

MAT 5:38–5:45 See also LUK 6:27–6:36

By the apostles

ROM 12:17; 1TH 5:15; 1PE 3:9 See also 1CO 13:4–13:5

The evil effects of revenge illustrated in the life of Samson

JDG 15:1–15:8, JDG 15:9–15:10, JDG 15:11–15:12

Alternatives to revenge

Avoiding the problem

ROM 12:18; ; 1PE 4:8

Evading the attack

MAT 10:23; ; LUK 4:29–4:30

Accepting the injury

1CO 6:7; ; HEB 10:32–10:34

Using the law

ACT 22:25; ; 1CO 6:1–6:6 going to law

LUK 23:34; ; ACT 7:59–7:60; ROM 12:19–12:21; ; PRO 25:21–25:22

LUK 18:7–18:8 See also DEU 32:43; 1SA 24:12; 2KI 9:7; PSA 18:47; REV 6:10, REV 19:2

title: 5496: revenge, examples of
content:
Ungodly people are often vengeful, and even Christians are not always exemplary in this respect. However, each case should be considered on its merits, and the claims of justice taken into account.

Revenge among the ungodly

LUK 6:11 parallels MAT 12:14, MRK 3:6 See also GEN 4:24 Compare Lamech's words with those of Jesus Christ in Mt 18:21–22; 1KI 19:2 Jezebel; 1KI 22:27 Ahab; EST 3:6 Haman; EZK 25:15 the PhilistinesMRK 6:19, MRK 6:24 ACT 5:33 the Sanhedrin; ACT 23:12 unbelieving Jews

Revenge among God's people

JDG 8:4–8:9; EST 9:1, EST 9:5 See also GEN 16:5–16:6; GAL 4:30; JDG 16:28–16:30 Samson; 1SA 25:10–25:13; 2SA 10:4–10:7 David did not retaliate at once, but only when a military threat appeared; 2SA 3:27 Joab; LUK 9:51–9:56 James and John; JHN 18:10–18:11 Peter; ACT 23:2–23:5 Paul

Examples of non-retaliation

By Jesus Christ

1PE 2:23 See also ISA 50:6–50:7, ISA 53:7; LUK 23:34

By David

1SA 24:1–24:12; ; PSA 35:11–35:14, PSA 35:17, PSA 38:12–38:15

By others

GEN 50:15–50:21 Joseph; ; 1SA 12:23 Samuel; ; 1KI 22:24–22:25 Micaiah; ; JOB 31:29 Job; ; ACT 7:59–7:60 Stephen

PSA 28:4, PSA 109:8–109:14, PSA 137:8–137:9; ; JER 15:15, JER 18:21; ; GAL 1:8–1:9, GAL 5:12; ; REV 6:10, REV 16:5–16:7, REV 18:6, REV 18:20

title: 5498: reward
content: Recompense in recognition of services rendered. Scripture stresses that while salvation is a gift of God, believers will be rewarded according to their deeds. Believers should be honest in rewarding others for their work.

title: 5499: reward, divine
content:
God's dealings with people are always in harmony with his grace and his justice, hating evil and loving good. No gift of God is on the basis of merit, but on the basis of his faithfulness to his promises.

God's reward is in harmony with his character

His graciousness

Weighing devices designed to ensure fair dealing. The terms are also used metaphorically in Scripture.

title: 5513: sceptre
content:
A staff, generally ornate, held as a symbol of sovereign authority.

The sceptre is a symbol of Jesus Christ's reign

HEB 1:8 See also PSA 45:6; GEN 49:10; NUM 24:17; PSA 110:2; REV 2:27; PSA 2:9; REV 19:15, REV 12:5

title: 5514: scribes
content:
Experts in the understanding and study of the law of Moses. Scribes had political power in NT times, and sat on the Sanhedrin. They were also referred to as lawyers and teachers of the law. They opposed Jesus Christ, who condemned their hypocrisy.

The duties of scribes

Writing records, legal contracts, letters and accounts

See also 2SA 8:16 parallel 1CH 18:15; 1KI 4:3; 2KI 12:10 parallel 2CH 24:11; JER 32:12, JER 36:26

Advising the king

2KI 18:18 parallel ISA 36:3; ; 2KI 19:2; ; 1CH 27:32

Conscripting people to the army

2KI 25:19 parallel JER 52:25

Shaphan

2KI 22:8 parallel 2CH 34:18

Baruch

JER 36:4–36:32

Ezra

Clans or families of scribes

1CH 2:55

The office of priest and scribe

Up to the time of the Babylonian exile only priests were allowed to be scribes: EZR 7:6; ; NEH 8:9, NEH 12:26

Scribes had political power in NT times and sat on the Sanhedrin

By this time, scribes were also referred to as teachers of the law'' andlawyers'': MAT 16:21 parallels MRK 8:31, LUK 9:22; ; MAT 26:3 parallels MRK 14:1, LUK 22:2

MAT 21:15; LUK 19:47 parallels MAT 21:15, MRK 11:18

MAT 23:27–23:28 See also MAT 23:1–23:7 parallels MRK 12:38–12:39, LUK 20:45–20:46

A long strip of leather or papyrus on which people wrote.

content:
Ideas and images drawn from seafaring are used in Scripture to illustrate important aspects of the Christian life. Although Israel was not a seafaring nation, ships and sailing played a part in her history, as they did in the spreading of the gospel in the NT.

Israel's harbours

GEN 49:13 See also JDG 5:17

The art of shipbuilding

EZK 27:3–27:9

Ships used for various purposes

Deliverance from danger: Noah's ark

GEN 6:1–9:17

Trade

1KI 9:27–9:28 parallel 2CH 8:18EZK 27:25 See also 1KI 10:11, 1KI 10:22 parallel 2CH 9:21; 1KI 22:48–22:49 parallel 2CH 20:35–20:37

Slavery

DEU 28:68; ; REV 18:11–18:13

Invasion

title: 5518: seal
content:
A personalised design used to produce an imprint in clay or wax which was then attached, usually to documents and letters as a mark of ownership, authenticity and authority. A seal might also refer to what is given as a pledge or guarantee or be used to keep something secure.

The nature and use of a seal

Seals engraved on precious stone

EXO 28:11 parallel EXO 39:6 See also EXO 28:21 parallel EXO 39:14; EXO 28:36 parallel EXO 39:30

Seals used to imprint soft clay

JOB 38:14

Ways of carrying a personal seal

Figuratively used

SNG 8:6

Worn round the neck

GEN 38:18 The seal took the form of an engraved cylinder pierced from end to end and worn on a cord round the neck. See also GEN 38:25

Worn as a signet ring

JER 22:24 See also NUM 31:50; ISA 3:21

A seal as a mark of authority

Given to signify delegation of authority

GEN 41:42; ; EST 3:10, EST 8:2; ; REV 7:2

God's seal validates his servants' ministry

JHN 6:27; ; 1CO 9:2

A seal authenticates documents

EST 8:8–8:10 See also 1KI 21:8; EST 3:12

A seal used to keep something secure

DAN 6:17 See also DEU 32:34; JOB 14:17; PSA 40:9; SNG 4:12; MAT 27:65–27:66; REV 20:3

The scroll and its seals

REV 5:1–5:4, REV 5:9 See also REV 5:5, REV 6:1–6:12, REV 8:1

DEU 29:12; ; HAG 2:23; ; ROM 4:11

2CO 1:21–1:22 The Holy Spirit both seals believers as belonging to God and guarantees their future inheritance. See also EPH 1:13–1:14, EPH 4:30

content:
A secretary was a royal official often responsible for correspondence

title: 5520: servants
content: Someone who serves another. Scripture provides guidance concerning the roles of servants, noting in particular that Jesus Christ chose to be a servant and commands believers to serve one another.

title: 5521: servant, Jesus Christ as
content: See 2327: Jesus Christ, as servant

title: 5522: servants, working conditions of
content:
Those who serve are to be treated fairly and with respect. Jesus Christ himself chose to be a servant and lays responsibility of service on those who follow.

Servants are to be treated fairly

They are not to be exploited

EPH 6:9 See also LEV 25:39–25:40, LEV 25:53

They are to be paid fairly and promptly

DEU 24:14–24:15 See also GEN 29:15; LEV 19:13; NUM 18:29–18:31; 1KI 5:6; JOB 7:1–7:2; JER 22:13; MAT 20:4, MAT 20:8; ROM 4:4; COL 4:1; 2TH 3:10

Examples of servants treated unfairly

JAS 5:4 See also GEN 31:7, GEN 31:41; EXO 2:23–2:24; JOB 24:10–24:11; MAL 3:5

Jesus Christ as a servant

MAT 20:28 See also PHP 2:7

Believers follow Jesus Christ's example as servants

They are servants of Jesus Christ and his church

ROM 1:1 See also LUK 1:38; 1CO 12:5, 1CO 16:15; EPH 4:12; COL 1:23, COL 3:24

They work to please God

EPH 6:5–6:6 See also COL 3:22–3:24; TIT 2:9–2:10

Christian workers should be paid honourably

1TI 5:17–5:18 See also LUK 10:7; 1CO 9:7–9:11; GAL 6:6

ROM 6:23 See also PRO 11:18; HOS 9:1; 2PE 2:15

Faithfulness

2KI 22:7 See also GEN 39:6; 2KI 12:15; TIT 2:9–2:10

Obedience

Respect

Bad servants are characterised by disobedience, idleness and dishonesty.

Dishonesty

content:
Shibboleth'' a Hebrew word meaningflood'' or ``ear of corn''

PSA 69:15 See also PSA 69:2; ISA 27:12 “Shibboleth” is here translated as flowing.

JDG 12:6

content:
A piece of armour used to fend off blows or missiles such as arrows. God is described as the shield of his people; protecting, giving help, strength and favour. Faith is the shield with which believers are to ward off spiritual attack.

Shields are pieces of armour

See also 2CH 11:11–11:12, 2CH 32:5; NEH 4:16; NAM 2:5 A number of shields were used to make a wall of defence.

Kinds of shield

Large and small shields

JER 46:3 See also 1KI 10:16–10:17 parallel 2CH 9:15–9:16; 2CH 14:8

Gold shields

2SA 8:7 parallel 1CH 18:7 See also 1KI 10:16–10:17, 1KI 14:26

Bronze shields

1KI 14:27

Shields made of combustible materials

EZK 39:9

Shields covered with leather

ISA 21:5 Leather shields were rubbed with oil to preserve them and to deflect blows from swords or arrows.

Shields in warfare

As part of an army's equipment

2CH 14:8 See also 1CH 12:23–12:24; 2CH 11:12, 2CH 26:14; NEH 4:16

Their use in battle

1CH 5:18 See also 1SA 17:7; 2KI 19:32; JER 46:3, JER 46:9, JER 51:11; EZK 23:24

The figurative use of shields

God is called a shield of his people

GEN 15:1 See also 2SA 22:3; PSA 7:10, PSA 18:2; PRO 2:7

God acts as a shield

EXO 14:19–14:20 See also ISA 52:12, ISA 58:8

God protects his people

ISA 31:5 See also PSA 3:3, PSA 12:7, PSA 32:10, PSA 125:2, PSA 140:7; ZEC 2:5, ZEC 12:8

God is a refuge for his people

PSA 144:2 See also PSA 18:30, PSA 119:114; PRO 30:5

God is the help and strength of his people

PSA 28:7 See also DEU 33:29; PSA 33:20, PSA 115:9–115:11

2SA 22:36 parallel PSA 18:35

God's favour is compared to a shield

PSA 5:12 See also PSA 3:3, PSA 32:10, PSA 84:9–84:11

PSA 91:4

EPH 6:16 See also 1PE 1:5

title: 5528: shouting
content:
A loud cry of joy, excitement or distress. Scripture often speaks of praise in terms of shouting, reflecting both the joy of the speaker and the greatness of God.

Shouting to be heard

1SA 17:20; LUK 23:21; ACT 22:23–22:24 See also JDG 7:20, JDG 15:14; 2KI 9:27; 2CH 13:15; JOB 39:25; PSA 60:8; ZEP 1:14; MAT 20:30–20:31; JHN 19:12; ACT 16:17, ACT 17:6, ACT 21:36

content:
Sustained battle against fortified cities, preventing renewal of supplies; a common tactic in OT times. Samaria and Jerusalem both fell to sieges.

Sieges used by and against Israel

DEU 20:12, DEU 20:19–20:20; ; JDG 9:50; ; 1SA 11:1; ; 2SA 11:1, 2SA 20:15

Ben-Hadad II twice besieged Samaria, unsuccessfully

1KI 20:1 See also 1KI 20:15–20:20; 2KI 6:24, 2KI 7:3–7:7

Shalmaneser V besieged Samaria

2KI 17:5–17:6 See also 2KI 18:9–18:12

Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem, unsuccessfully

2KI 18:17, 2KI 18:35–18:36; ; 2CH 32:1–32:5; ; ISA 29:5–29:8, ISA 37:36–37:37

Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem

2KI 25:1 See also 2KI 25:2–25:11 parallel JER 39:1–39:10; 2CH 36:17–36:20 parallel JER 52:4–52:15

Jesus Christ warned that Jerusalem would be besieged and destroyed

LUK 19:43 The Roman army destroyed Jerusalem in A.D. 70 using an embankment to besiege the city. See also LUK 21:20–21:24

content:
The process of separating different substances, especially grain and chaff, normally by passing them through sieves. It is used as a symbol of judgment in which the good are separated from the evil.
