JDG 7:4

Sifting as a symbol of judgment

ISA 30:28 See also AMO 9:9; LUK 22:31

content:
A trade or craft acquired by training or practice, or a special ability or expertise that may be an endowment of the Holy Spirit. Scripture lists many skills and abilities, particularly used in the building of the tabernacle and temple.

EXO 35:10; 1CH 22:15–22:16 See also 1CH 28:21

In working metal

2CH 2:7 JDG 17:4; ; ACT 19:24; 1KI 7:14–7:15, 1KI 7:41–7:45 parallel 2CH 4:12–4:16; 2CH 3:5–3:7; ; ISA 46:6; 2TI 4:14

In working stone

1CH 22:2 See also 1KI 5:15–5:18 parallel 2CH 2:2; 1KI 6:36, 1KI 7:9–7:12

With timber

1KI 5:6 parallel 2CH 2:8–2:9 See also 1KI 6:14–6:36

With fabrics

EXO 38:23 EXO 26:1, EXO 26:36, EXO 28:39; EXO 29:5, EXO 39:1–39:5; EXO 35:25 skill in spinning

With music

1CH 15:22; ; 2CH 34:12–34:13; ; PSA 33:3

Other skills

GEN 25:27 hunting; 1KI 9:27; ; EZK 27:8; JOB 32:22 flattery; ; PSA 45:1 writing; PSA 58:5; ; ISA 3:3; PSA 78:72 leadership; ; JER 2:33 love; ; JER 9:17 Mourning: professional mourners were a feature of life in Bible times; ; JER 50:9 fighting; ; EZK 28:5 trading

1CH 5:18; 2CH 2:13–2:14 GEN 14:14; ; 2CH 26:11; 1CH 25:7 musical skill; ; LUK 6:40 teaching abilities; ; 1CO 9:25 Athletic prowess requires strict training; ; HEB 5:14 distinguishing good from evil through proper training

title: 5532: sleep
content: A state of slumber or rest, reflecting tiredness and the need for refreshment. Although sleep is a natural physical process, Scripture also uses the term in a number of important spiritual senses.

title: 5533: sleep, physical
content:
A gift from God providing necessary rest, usually at night, for the restoration of mind and body. It is sometimes denied, sometimes used by God for his purposes and sometimes abused by people.

Sleep is a gift from God

It is pleasant and refreshing

ECC 5:12 See also 1KI 19:5; JER 31:26; JHN 11:12–11:13

It is God's gift to his faithful people

PSA 127:2 See also PRO 3:21–3:24

It is often denied to the wicked

ISA 48:22

Sleep as a nocturnal activity

It is associated with night-time

1TH 5:7 See also LUK 17:34; JHN 9:4; ROM 13:11–13:12

It is associated with dreams

GEN 28:11–28:12, GEN 41:1, GEN 41:5; ; ISA 29:7–29:8; ; DAN 2:1, DAN 4:5, DAN 7:1

It is associated with sexual activity

GEN 30:15–30:16; 2SA 11:4 GEN 16:2, GEN 16:4; GEN 26:10, GEN 30:3–30:5, GEN 35:22, GEN 38:18, GEN 39:14; ; EXO 22:16; ; DEU 22:22; ; 2SA 3:7; ; HEB 13:4

Protection

Light sleep

SNG 5:2

PRO 19:15; ; MAT 28:13; ; MRK 13:36

During harvest

PRO 10:5

JON 1:5–1:6; ; MAT 26:40 parallels MRK 14:37, LUK 22:45–22:46

During a sermon

ACT 20:9

At the transfiguration

LUK 9:32

Amidst danger

JDG 16:13–16:14, JDG 16:19; ; PRO 6:1–6:5, PRO 23:34; ; MAT 13:25

content:

title: 5535: sleep, and death
content:
Scripture often uses sleep as an image of death, indicating that believers will be awakened to resurrection on the last day.

The sleep of death for human beings in general

PSA 90:3–90:6 See also JOB 7:21, JOB 14:10–14:12; PSA 13:3; DAN 12:2; MAT 9:24 parallels MRK 5:39, LUK 8:52–8:53

1KI 2:10 See also DEU 31:16; 2SA 7:12; 1KI 11:43 Solomon; 1KI 14:20, 1KI 14:31, 1KI 16:6, 1KI 22:50 Jehoshaphat; 2KI 14:16, 2KI 15:7, 2KI 16:20, 2KI 20:21 Hezekiah; 2KI 21:18 Manasseh

Those who fall asleep in Christ

REV 14:13 See also JHN 11:11–11:14; ACT 7:60; 1CO 15:6, 1CO 15:17–15:19

JHN 5:28–5:29 See also JOB 14:13–14:15; PSA 17:15; ISA 26:19; DAN 12:3; LUK 16:22–16:23; 1CO 15:20, 1CO 15:51–15:57; 1TH 4:13–4:18

Sleep denoting the finality of judgment for the lost

JER 51:57 See also PSA 7:3–7:5, PSA 76:5; JER 51:39

title: 5537: sleeplessness
content:
The absence of or inability to sleep. Scripture suggests that sleeplessness will sometimes result from divine intervention. Scripture also provides examples of deliberate sleeplessness in order to seek God.

Anxiety and sorrow as causes of sleeplessness

ECC 2:22–2:23 See also PRO 6:1–6:4; ECC 5:12; JER 45:3

Work

PSA 127:2

Pain and sickness

Evil deeds

PRO 4:14–4:16 See also ISA 5:27

PSA 132:4–132:5 See also ISA 62:6; LUK 2:37, LUK 6:12; ACT 12:12

Jacob

GEN 31:40

Darius

Paul

title: 5538: sling
content:
Used by shepherds to defend their flocks, it consisted of a strip of leather broad enough to contain a stone. A string was attached to each end of this strip. It was swung around fast and when one string was released the stone could be hurled out with great force and accuracy.

David felled Goliath with a stone from his sling

1SA 17:40, 1SA 17:49–17:50

Slings were also used by soldiers as weapons

JDG 20:16; ; 2KI 3:25; ; 1CH 12:2; ; 2CH 26:14

Slings were known for their destructive power

JOB 41:28; ; ZEC 9:15

Slings used metaphorically

1SA 25:29; ; PRO 26:8; ; JER 10:18

title: 5539: sluggard
content:
Someone characterised by a settled attitude of slothfulness and idleness. Such people are consistently condemned throughout Scripture.

Sluggards are characterised by slothfulness and idleness

They are lazy and refuse to work

PRO 6:6–6:8 See also PRO 12:27, PRO 15:19, PRO 19:24, PRO 20:4, PRO 21:25, PRO 24:30–24:31, PRO 26:15

They love to stay in bed when they should be up and active

PRO 6:9 See also PRO 26:14

They make excuses to avoid work

PRO 22:13 See also PRO 26:13

Their desires are not met

PRO 13:4 See also PRO 20:4, PRO 21:25–21:26

Their laziness leads to poverty

PRO 6:10–6:11 See also PRO 10:4–10:5, PRO 12:24, PRO 18:9, PRO 19:15, PRO 20:13, PRO 24:33–24:34; ECC 4:5, ECC 10:18

PRO 10:26

They are conceited

PRO 26:16

title: 5540: society
content: The network of relationships, institutions and shared values that together make up the corporate aspect of human life. Though often regarded as hostile to God and threatening to faith, society can be viewed positively as capable of redemption and an object of God's saving activity.

title: 5541: society, negative aspects of
content:
Often pictured as an immoral city or a world of evil, it is regarded as corrupt and godless, hostile to true faith and therefore destined for judgment.

The city as a symbol of corrupt society

REV 18:2–18:3 Babylon stands for the corrupt Roman state and also for godless society in general. See also GEN 11:1–11:9, GEN 19:1–19:13; EZK 22:1–22:5; MAT 23:37–23:39 parallel LUK 13:34–13:35; REV 14:8

``The world'' as a description of society alienated from, and hostile to, both God and his people

GAL 3:22 The Greek word translated “world” often means not the physical world, but the world of human life. See also JHN 15:18; EPH 6:12; 1JN 5:19; REV 12:9

Fallen society becomes pluralistic

Israel was continually threatened by the pluralism of the surrounding societies

JOS 23:6–23:8 See also EXO 23:32–23:33; JOS 24:14–24:23; 1KI 11:1–11:6, 1KI 18:16–18:40 Baal was a name used for a variety of local Canaanite deities; EZR 9:1–9:2; ISA 2:6–2:8; DAN 3:1–3:12

Pluralism was also a feature of the societies of the NT

ACT 17:16–17:23 See also 1CO 8:4–8:6; 2TI 4:3–4:4; 1JN 5:21

Pluralism is to be resisted and faith in one God and Saviour maintained

1TI 2:5 See also ISA 43:10–43:11; JHN 14:6; ACT 4:12

Fallen society becomes secular

Life in a godless society becomes spiritually futile and morally depraved

ROM 1:21 See also ROM 1:18–1:32; 2TI 3:1–3:5; REV 18:1–18:3

Israel ignores warnings about becoming a society which has forgotten God

PSA 81:11–81:12 See also JER 3:19–3:21; HEB 3:7–3:11

Israel became an example of a society which, though outwardly religious, lived without reference to God

AMO 5:21–5:24 Amos here summarises, and rejects, current religious practices in Israel in the 8th century B.C. See also AMO 2:6–2:7, AMO 5:4–5:15 Bethel and Gilgal were popular national shrines, where religion had taken the place of righteousness and relationship; AMO 8:4–8:10

title: 5542: society, positive aspects of
content:
The object of God's love and the sphere of God's blessing. God's people should adopt a positive but critical attitude to, and involvement in society, and should seek to influence it for good, while guarding against its corrupting influence.

Society is the object of God's redeeming love and the sphere of his blessing

The city as a positive image of society

ISA 1:26–1:27 See also PSA 122:6–122:9; ISA 54:11–54:14; HEB 11:10, HEB 11:15–11:16; REV 21:1–21:4, REV 21:22–22:5

The world as the object of God's love

JHN 3:16–3:17 See also JHN 6:33; 2CO 5:19; 1JN 4:14; REV 11:15

God's people are to be positively involved in society

They are to seek to be a positive influence

JHN 17:15–17:18 See also JER 29:7 God's people, in exile in Babylon, are to seek the welfare of that society, rather than simply long to return home; MAT 5:13–5:16; 1CO 5:9–5:10

They are to avoid being corrupted by society's worldliness

JAS 1:27 See also ROM 12:2; JAS 4:4; 1JN 2:15–2:17

They do not owe society their ultimate loyalty

JHN 17:16 See also JHN 15:19; HEB 13:14; 1PE 2:11

They are to adopt a positive attitude to society's properly instituted authorities

ROM 13:1–13:7; TIT 3:1 See also MAT 22:17–22:21 parallels MRK 12:14–12:17, LUK 20:22–20:25; 1PE 2:13–2:17

While being submissive, they are not to give absolute obedience to any merely human authority in society

ACT 4:18–4:20 See also ACT 5:27–5:29

Examples of those positively involved in society

DAN 2:48–2:49 See also GEN 41:41–41:49 Joseph; EST 10:1–10:3 Mordecai; DAN 1:1–1:21 Daniel and his friends

content:
A weapon of warfare for stabbing or throwing. God promises a time when they will be changed into instruments of peace.

title: 5546: speech
content: The human capacity to express oneself and communicate with others through the spoken word. God addresses humans through the spoken word, and supremely in and through Jesus Christ.

title: 5547: speech, power and significance of
content:
A person's speech has an enormous influence for good or ill and is a sure guide to character.

The impact of speech

It has the power of life and death

PRO 18:21; JAS 3:1–3:12 See also PRO 15:2, PRO 15:4

It can bring ruin or joy to the speaker

PRO 12:13–12:14 See also PSA 140:9; PRO 10:14, PRO 13:3, PRO 14:3, PRO 18:6–18:7, PRO 18:20, PRO 21:23; ECC 10:12–10:14

It can destroy others

PRO 11:9 See also JOB 19:2; PSA 55:20–55:21, PSA 57:4, PSA 64:3–64:4, PSA 140:3; PRO 11:11, PRO 12:6, PRO 12:18, PRO 16:27

There is an appropriate time for speaking

1PE 2:22–2:23 See also MAT 26:63 parallel MRK 14:61; MAT 27:14 parallel MRK 15:5; LUK 23:9; JHN 19:8–19:9

MAT 12:34–12:37 See also PSA 5:9, PSA 15:1–15:5; MAT 15:10–15:20 parallel MRK 7:14–7:23; LUK 6:45; JAS 1:26; REV 14:5

title: 5549: speech, positive aspects of
content:
The way in which believers speak should reflect their calling as Christians. Christian speech should be sincere, godly and honouring to God.

In oneself

In others

NUM 6:22–6:27 See also GEN 1:22, GEN 1:28; DEU 21:5; 1CH 23:13

title: 5550: speech, negative aspects of

In Solomon's temple

content: The experience of pain or distress, both physical and emotional. Scripture is thoroughly realistic about the place of suffering in the world and in the lives of believers. To become a Christian is not to escape from suffering, but to be able to bear suffering with dignity and hope.

title: 5596: victory
content: The conquest of, or gaining a decisive advantage over, an enemy. The gospel proclaims the victory of God in Christ over the forces of evil in the world.

title: 5597: victory, as an act of God

title: 5605: warfare
content: The state of being at war with an opposing nation or people. Scripture neither condemns nor glories in warfare, but recognises it as a continuing aspect of this fallen world. In particular, the NT stresses the importance of spiritual warfare in the life of faith.

title: 5613: weights and measures
content: The peoples of the ancient Near East used a variety of standards of weights and measures, so that modern equivalents can only be approximate. The focus of Scripture is on the importance of keeping just weights and measures, and the prophets denounced those who used false balances and deceitful measures.

resource.label: 5619: weights and measures, distance and area

title: 5614: weights and measures, laws concerning
content:
God expects his people to use accurate weights and measures, and to use just balances. This is underlined in the Law, the Prophets and the wisdom literature.

The law demanded honesty in using weights and measures

LEV 19:35–19:36 Cheating by falsifying weights and measures was common in a culture where there was no standardisation or regulatory authority. See also DEU 25:13–25:16

The prophets called for the right use of weights and measures

A call for honesty

EZK 45:9–45:10

Condemnation of dishonesty

AMO 8:4–8:6 See also HOS 12:7–12:8; MIC 6:10–6:14

Instruction from Proverbs on weights and measures

PRO 20:10 See also PRO 11:1, PRO 16:11 Merchants carried stones of different sizes in a pouch for weighing silver for payment; PRO 20:23, PRO 22:28 To move a boundary stone was in effect to steal land.

title: 5615: weights and measures, weights
content:
Ancient weights were usually made of stone or metal, often inscribed with their weight and standard, the shekel being the basic weight of all Semitic nations. Weights of gold and silver served as currency, since coinage was not invented until the seventh century B.C. Weights are given in ascending order, with their approximate imperial and metric equivalents.

Gerah (1/20 shekel): about 1/50 ounce (about 0.6 gram)

LEV 27:25 See also EXO 30:13; NUM 3:47, NUM 18:16; EZK 45:12

Beka (10 gerahs): about 1/5 ounce (about 5.8 grams)

2CH 9:15–9:16 parallel 1KI 10:16–10:17 See also GEN 24:22; EXO 38:25–38:26

Pim (2/3 shekel): about 1/4 ounce (about 7.7 grams)

1SA 13:21 The Hebrew word translated “two thirds of a shekel” is “pim”, its only mention in Scripture.

Shekel (2 bekas): about 2/5 ounce (about 11.5 grams)

The shekel in relation to other weights

EZK 45:12

The shekel as a weight of metal objects

1SA 17:5 See also 1SA 17:7; 2SA 21:16

The shekel as a weight of food

EZK 4:10

The shekel as a weight of gold or silver objects

2CH 3:9 See also GEN 24:22; NUM 7:13–7:14; JDG 8:26

The shekel as a weight of gold or silver

GEN 23:14–23:16 The phrase “the weight current among the merchants” reflects the local variation in standards. See also GEN 37:28; DEU 22:28–22:29; JOS 7:20–7:21; JDG 17:1–17:4; 2SA 18:11–18:12; 1KI 10:29 parallel 2CH 1:17; 2KI 5:4–5:5; NEH 5:15; JER 32:9; DAN 5:25–5:27 “Tekel” can mean “weighed” or “shekel”.

The royal shekel

2SA 14:26 The royal shekel, also known in Babylonia, was slightly heavier (at about 13 grams) than the standard shekel and reflects David's attempts to bring some standardisation to this weight.

The sanctuary shekel

NUM 18:15–18:16 The sanctuary shekel was more precisely regulated than the common shekel, weighing exactly 20 gerahs. The common shekel may have weighed slightly less as a result of greater handling and wider circulation. See also EXO 30:13–30:15, EXO 30:22–30:25, EXO 38:24–38:26; LEV 5:15, LEV 27:1–27:7; NUM 3:46–3:50

Mina (50 shekels): about 1 1/4 pounds (about 0.6 kilogram)

EZK 45:12 Although the mina is valued here at 60 shekels, there is some evidence that in the pre-exilic period it was valued at 50 shekels. See also 1KI 10:17; EZR 2:69; NEH 7:71–7:72; DAN 5:25–5:26 “Mene” can mean both “numbered” and “mina”; LUK 19:11–19:27 By NT times the mina had become coinage rather than simply a weight of silver, and was worth about three months' wages.

Talent (3,000 shekels, 60 minas): about 75 pounds (about 34 kilograms)

1CH 29:7 See also EXO 25:39; 2SA 12:30 parallel 1CH 20:2; 1KI 10:14 parallel 2CH 9:13; 1KI 16:24; 2KI 18:14; EZR 8:26; EST 3:9; MAT 18:24–18:25 By NT times the talent had become coinage, and ten thousand talents would have been the equivalent of millions of pounds sterling; MAT 25:14–25:30

Other minor weights

Kesitah

GEN 33:19 The price in the original Hebrew is “one hundred kesitahs”, a unit of unknown weight and value.

Litra

The word translated pint'' in Jn 12:3 andpound'' in 19:39 is litra'', a loanword from the Latinlibra'', meaning ``pound'' and weighing 12 ounces (327 grams): JHN 12:3, JHN 19:39

Peres

DAN 5:28 “Peres” means “division” and denotes a half-shekel.

title: 5616: weights and measures, dry
content:
These terms derive originally from the containers used, which held a fixed amount. Measures are given in ascending order, with their approximate imperial and metric equivalents.

Cab (1/18 ephah): about 2 pints (about 1 litre)

2KI 6:25 This is the only mention in Scripture of this measure.

Omer (1/10 ephah): about 4 pints (about 2 litres)

EXO 16:16–16:22 This incident records the only mention in Scripture of this measure. See also EXO 16:32, EXO 16:36

Seah (1/3 ephah): about 13 pints (about 7.3 litres)

GEN 18:6 The seah was a measure used for flour and cereals. See also 1SA 25:18; 1KI 18:32; 2KI 7:1

Ephah: about 3/5 bushel (about 22 litres)

RUT 2:17 The ephah was used only for flour and cereals, and had subdivisions of 1/6 and 1/10. See also LEV 5:11, LEV 24:5; NUM 15:4–15:9; JDG 6:19; 1SA 17:17; EZK 45:10–45:11; ZEC 5:6–5:8 The word for “measuring basket” in the Hebrew is “ephah”.

Lethek (5 ephahs or 1/2 homer): about 3 bushels (about 110 litres)

HOS 3:2 Possibly a Phoenician measure, this is the only mention in Scripture of this measure.

Cor (10 ephahs): about 6 bushels (about 220 litres)

1KI 4:22 The cor was used for measuring flour and cereals, and also appears to have been used for measuring oil. See also 1KI 5:11; 2CH 2:10, 2CH 27:5; EZR 7:22; EZK 45:14

Homer (10 ephahs): about 6 bushels (about 220 litres)

LEV 27:16 The homer is an older word than the cor, but is equivalent to it. It originally meant “a donkey load” and was widely used throughout the ancient Near East from the second millennium B.C. as a measure for cereals. See also NUM 11:32; ISA 5:10; EZK 45:11, EZK 45:13–45:14; HOS 3:2

Other dry measures found in the NT

Quart (choinix): about 1 1/2–2 pints (about 1 litre)

REV 6:6 The word translated “quart” is “choinix”, a Greek measure.

Saton (equivalent to the OT seah)

MAT 13:33 parallel LUK 13:21 The “large amount” referred to is “three sata” in the Greek.

Bowl (modius): about 15 1/2 pints (about 8.75 litres)

MAT 5:15 parallels MRK 4:21, LUK 11:33 The word translated “bowl” is the Roman measure “modius”.

Koros (equivalent to the OT cor)

LUK 16:7 The measure translated as “a thousand bushels” is “one hundred korous” in the Greek.

title: 5617: weights and measures, liquid
content:
These terms derive originally from the containers used, which held a fixed amount. There is some uncertainty about the capacity of the bath, and therefore of other liquid measures dependent upon it. Measures are given in ascending order, with their approximate imperial and metric equivalents.

Log (1/72 bath): about 1/2 pint (about 0.3 litre)

LEV 14:10 This is the only mention in Scripture of the log, as a measure of oil used in the ritual for cleansing infectious skin diseases. See also LEV 14:12–14:18, LEV 14:21–14:22

Hin (1/6 bath): about 7 pints (about 4 litres)

EXO 29:38–29:41 The hin was used as a measure of oil, wine and water. See also LEV 23:12–23:13; NUM 15:4–15:10; EZK 4:11, EZK 46:5–46:7

Bath (1 ephah): about 5 gallons (about 22 litres)

EZK 45:11 The bath was the equivalent liquid measure of the ephah, and was used to measure oil, wine and water. See also 1KI 5:11, 1KI 7:38; 2CH 2:10; EZR 7:21–7:22; ISA 5:10; EZK 45:14; LUK 16:6 The measure translated as “eight hundred gallons” is “one hundred batous” in the original (“batos” being the Greek form of the Hebrew “bath”); JHN 2:6 The measure translated as “twenty to thirty gallons” is “two to three metretas” in the original, a Greek measure roughly equivalent to the bath.

title: 5618: weights and measures, linear
content:
These terms were based on natural units of measurement that could be easily applied. Measures are given in ascending order, with their approximate imperial and metric equivalents.

Finger (1/4 handbreadth): about 3/4 inch (about 1.85 centimetres)

JER 52:21 The finger was 1/4 handbreadth and was the smallest subdivision of the cubit. This is its only mention in Scripture.

Handbreadth (4 fingers): about 3 inches (about 8 centimetres)

EXO 25:25 parallel EXO 37:12 The handbreadth was the width of the hand at the base of the four fingers. See also 1KI 7:26 parallel 2CH 4:5; PSA 39:5 The handbreadth is here used figuratively of the shortness of human life; EZK 40:5

Span (half a cubit): about 9 inches (about 23 centimetres)

EXO 28:16 parallel EXO 39:9 The span was the width of the outstretched hand from thumb to little finger. See also 1SA 17:4 Goliath's height is given in the Hebrew as “six cubits and a span”; PSA 90:10 The span is here used figuratively of the shortness of human life; EZK 43:13

Cubit (2 spans): about 18 inches (about 0.5 metre)

EXO 25:10 parallel EXO 37:1 The cubit was the distance from the fingertip to the elbow, and was used to measure height, size, depth and distance. See also GEN 7:20 The Hebrew describes the depth of the water as “fifteen cubits”; EXO 27:9–27:18 parallel EXO 38:9–38:15; 1KI 6:2–6:3 parallel 2CH 3:3–3:4; 1CH 11:23 The Hebrew describes the man as “five cubits tall”; EZK 40:5, EZK 45:1–45:6, EZK 47:3–47:5; JHN 21:8 The Greek text describes the distance as “about two hundred cubits”; REV 21:17

Reed (6 cubits): about 10 feet (about 3 metres)

EZK 41:8 Originally a measuring instrument, the reed became a recognised measure of six cubits (the rod). See also EZK 40:3, EZK 40:5–40:7; REV 11:1, REV 21:15–21:16

Mile

MAT 5:41 The Greek word for “mile” here is “milion”, a transliteration of the Roman measurement “mille passuum”, “a thousand paces”. See also LUK 24:13 The measurement in the Greek is “sixty stadia”. Eight stadia were about one mile (about 1480 metres); JHN 6:19 The measurement in the Greek is “twenty-five or thirty stadia”; JHN 11:18 The measurement in the Greek is “fifteen stadia”.

title: 5619: weights and measures, distance and area
content:
Diverse expressions were used for these measurements, their being determined in the most practical way possible, reckoned by known averages.

Expressions of distance

A bow-shot

GEN 21:15–21:16

Some distance

EXO 33:7 A variety of distance often lies behind this expression, as can be seen in the examples that follow. See also GEN 35:16, GEN 36:6; NUM 2:2; 1SA 26:13; 2SA 15:17; MAT 8:30

A Sabbath day's journey

ACT 1:12 While this is the only mention of this phrase in Scripture, it was in fact a popular expression, indicating the distance a devout Jew could walk on the Sabbath. It was based on the rabbinical interpretation of Ex 16:29 in the light of Nu 35:5, and was limited to 2,000 cubits.

A day's journey

1KI 19:3–19:4 See also NUM 11:31

A three-day journey

GEN 30:36 See also EXO 3:18; NUM 10:33; EZR 10:7–10:9; JON 3:3

Far away

DEU 28:49 See also 1KI 8:46 parallel 2CH 6:36; ISA 6:12; EZK 11:15–11:16; JOL 3:8; ZEC 6:15; ACT 22:21

Expressions of area

Area expressed by the yoke

1SA 14:14 The area translated “about half an acre” in the Hebrew means “half a yoke”. The yoke was the area of land ploughed by a yoke of oxen in one day, approximately one acre. See also ISA 5:10 The Hebrew describes the area as “ten-yoke”, that is, the land ploughed by ten yoke of oxen in one day.

Area expressed by the amount of seed required to sow the land

LEV 27:16

Area expressed by its constituent measurements

EZK 40:47 See also EXO 28:16 parallel EXO 39:9; 1KI 7:23; EZK 45:1–45:6

title: 5621: wheel
content:
Early wheels were solid wooden discs. These were replaced around 1500 B.C. by lighter, spoked wheels. The most common use of wheels is on chariots and carts; they were also used by potters and in machinery for drawing water from a well. The chariot throne of God has wheels which are vividly described.

Chariot wheels

EXO 14:25; NAM 3:2 The sound of chariot wheels announces the approach of the enemy. See also 2KI 7:6; ISA 5:28; JER 47:3; JOL 2:5; REV 9:9

Wagon wheels

The Hebrew word for wheel'' is here used forwagon'': EZK 23:24, EZK 26:10

Threshing wheels

PRO 20:26 Threshing was carried out by driving a sledge or a cart with heavy wheels over the grain. See also ISA 28:27–28:28

Other examples of wheels

1KI 7:32–7:33 The stands for basins in Solomon's temple were mounted on wheels. See also 1KI 7:30; ECC 12:6 A wheel formed part of the machinery for drawing water from a well; JER 18:3 Potters turned their clay on a wheel.

The wheels of God's chariot throne

EZK 11:22–11:23; DAN 7:9 See also 2KI 2:11; ISA 66:15; EZK 1:15–1:21, EZK 3:12–3:13, EZK 10:1–10:19

title: 5622: witnesses
content: Individuals who, having observed something take place, are able to give an accurate and full account of what has happened. Witnesses were of central importance to OT law. The theme of giving account is also of major importance to evangelism, which rests upon believers explaining the impact of Jesus Christ upon their lives.

title: 5623: witnesses, legal
content:
God gave detailed instructions about the conduct of witnesses in the legal processes of Israel and also in the affairs of the church.

God himself as a witness

GEN 31:50; ; MAL 2:14

General legal requirements about witnesses

A witness to a crime was required to give evidence

LEV 5:1 See also PRO 29:24

Two or more witnesses were required to prove someone guilty

DEU 19:15 See also DEU 17:6; MAT 18:15–18:16; 2CO 13:1

The role of witnesses in capital cases

At least two witnesses were required

NUM 35:30 See also DEU 17:2–17:6; HEB 10:28

Witnesses were required to participate in the execution

DEU 17:7 See also LEV 24:13–24:16; DEU 13:6–13:11; ACT 7:57–7:58

The role of witnesses in other legal matters

Land transactions

JER 32:9–32:12 See also GEN 23:10–23:18; RUT 4:1–4:9; JER 32:25, JER 32:44

Levirate marriage

RUT 4:9–4:11

The role of witnesses in disputes concerning believers

MAT 18:15–18:17 See also 2CO 13:1; 1TI 5:19

title: 5624: witnesses, to Jesus Christ
content:
The NT identifies a variety of witnesses to Jesus Christ, who confirm his identity and importance. It also stresses the importance of believers bearing witness to Christ in the world.

The witness of the OT

ACT 26:22–26:23 See also LUK 24:27; JHN 5:39–5:40; HEB 12:1–12:2

The witness of John the Baptist

JHN 1:6–1:8 See also MAT 3:1–3:3; ISA 40:3; MAT 3:11–3:12 parallels MRK 1:7–1:8, LUK 3:15–3:18; JHN 1:15, JHN 1:19–1:31, JHN 3:26–3:30, JHN 5:33–5:35

The witness of the Holy Spirit

JHN 15:26 See also ACT 5:32; ROM 8:16; 1JN 5:6–5:9

The witness of the Father

JHN 8:18 See also MAT 3:17 parallels MRK 1:11, LUK 3:22; MAT 17:5 parallels MRK 9:7, LUK 9:35; JHN 5:37–5:38

The witness of Jesus Christ to himself

JHN 5:36, JHN 8:14 See also JHN 13:13, JHN 14:11

The witness of Jesus Christ's miracles

JHN 14:11 See also JHN 10:25, JHN 15:24

The witness of the first Christians

Commissioned by Jesus Christ

ACT 1:8 MAT 10:17–10:20; ; LUK 21:12–21:13; ; ACT 4:18–4:21; LUK 1:1–1:2, LUK 24:48; ; JHN 15:27; ; ACT 1:21–1:22, ACT 2:32, ACT 4:33, ACT 13:31; ACT 9:5–9:6, ACT 22:14–22:15, ACT 23:11, ACT 26:16; HEB 2:3; ; 1PE 5:1; ; 2PE 1:16; ; 1JN 1:1

The witness of converts

1PE 3:15–3:16 See also 2TI 1:8

title: 5625: witnesses, false
content:
Scripture prohibits individuals from bearing false witness against their neighbours.

False testimony forbidden

EXO 20:16 parallel DEU 5:20 See also EXO 23:1–23:2; LEV 19:12; PRO 6:16–6:19, PRO 24:28; LUK 3:14; MAT 15:19, MAT 19:18 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20

The effect of false witnesses on other people and society

PRO 25:18 See also PSA 27:12, PSA 35:11; PRO 12:17, PRO 14:5, PRO 14:25, PRO 18:5, PRO 19:28

False witnesses will be punished

DEU 19:16–19:21 See also LEV 6:1–6:7; PRO 19:5, PRO 19:9, PRO 21:28; ISA 29:20–29:21; ZEC 5:3–5:4

Examples of false witnesses

1KI 21:8–21:13; ; MAT 26:59–26:61 parallel MRK 14:55–14:59; ; MAT 28:12–28:15; ; ACT 6:11–6:14

title: 5627: word
content:
Jesus Christ is described as God's word. The word encompassed the promise of God and the gospel and is a help in trial and temptation. Human beings should use words wisely.

Jesus Christ and God's word

Jesus Christ described as the Word

JHN 1:1–1:3 See also JHN 1:14; HEB 1:1–1:2; 1JN 1:1–1:2; REV 19:13

Jesus Christ preaches the word

MRK 2:2 See also MAT 7:24–7:29 parallel LUK 6:47–6:49; MAT 13:20–13:23 parallels MRK 4:13–4:20, LUK 8:11–8:15 the parable of the sower; LUK 11:28; JHN 3:34, JHN 5:24, JHN 6:63–6:68, JHN 8:31–8:32, JHN 8:47, JHN 8:52, JHN 12:47–12:50, JHN 14:10–14:24, JHN 15:3, JHN 17:6–17:8

The word and the gospel

ACT 4:31 See also ACT 4:29, ACT 13:44–13:46, ACT 19:10, ACT 20:24; DEU 30:14; ROM 10:8–10:10; COL 1:5, COL 2:2; 1TH 1:5; HEB 4:2

God's word is a promise and help in trial and temptation

PSA 119:9–119:11 See also PSA 33:4–33:5, PSA 119:105, PSA 119:133; DEU 8:3; MAT 4:4; JHN 14:23–14:24, JHN 17:17; EPH 6:17; HEB 4:12; 1JN 5:3

Words should be used wisely

MAT 12:36–12:37 See also JDG 8:1–8:3; 2CH 10:13–10:14; PRO 10:19, PRO 12:18, PRO 12:25, PRO 15:1, PRO 16:24, PRO 25:15; ECC 12:11; JAS 3:1–3:12

resource.label: 2203: Jesus Christ, titles and names of
2363: Jesus Christ, preaching and teaching of

title: 5628: work
content: Work was ordained by God as a means of fulfilment, service and praise. It is to be supplemented by rest, following the pattern of God's creation of the world. Despite the effects of sin, work can still be honouring to God.

title: 5629: work, as ordained by God
content:
God ordained work as the normal routine of living. Every legitimate human task, therefore, is of intrinsic worth, however menial it may seem, and is potentially a means of glorifying God.

Work is ordained by God

GEN 1:27–1:28 See also EXO 20:9 parallel DEU 5:13; PSA 104:23 Work is part of the rhythm of life.

God's purposes in ordaining work

That people should be self-supporting

GEN 3:19 See also PSA 128:2; 1TH 4:12

That people should find self-fulfilment

ECC 2:24 See also PRO 14:23; ECC 3:22, ECC 5:19

That people should serve others

EPH 4:28 See also PRO 31:15; 1TH 2:9; 1TI 5:8

That people should glorify God

COL 3:17 See also 1CO 10:31; EPH 6:5–6:8 parallel COL 3:22–3:24

Consequences of viewing work as God's ordinance

Work is seen as a moral duty

TIT 3:14 See also PRO 6:6; ECC 9:10; 1TH 4:11; 2TH 3:7–3:12

Any legitimate work may be seen as God's calling

GEN 2:15 See also EXO 31:1–31:6, EXO 35:30–35:35; PSA 78:70–78:71; MAT 13:55 parallel MRK 6:3; ROM 13:6; 1CO 7:17, 1CO 7:20–7:24

Work is seen as a stewardship from God himself

COL 3:23–3:24 See also MAT 25:14–25:30 parallel LUK 19:12–19:27; EPH 6:5–6:8

Criticism of those who will not work

2TH 3:10–3:11

title: 5630: work, divine and human
content:
God has ordained that some of his purposes be fulfilled through the co-operation (conscious or unconscious) of human beings.

God works in co-operation with people's work

Human labour is futile apart from God

PSA 127:1 See also GEN 11:8; JHN 15:5

God often works through human means

PSA 77:20 See also ACT 9:15; ROM 13:6; 2CO 7:6

God gives the gifts needed for work

EXO 31:3, EXO 31:6; ; LUK 12:48; ; 1PE 4:11

Human workers should acknowledge their dependence upon God

DEU 8:18 See also PSA 90:17; NEH 6:9, NEH 6:16; 2CO 3:5

The apostles as God's fellow-workers

1CO 3:9; 2CO 6:1 See also MRK 16:20

Examples of divine and human co-operation in work

PHP 2:12–2:13

God creates and people cultivate

GEN 2:15; ; ISA 28:23–28:29; ; 1CO 3:7

God gives and people are generous

1KI 17:9; ; 2CO 8:1–8:5

God speaks through prophets' words

DEU 18:15–18:18; ; 2SA 12:25; ; JER 37:2; ; HOS 12:13; ; MAT 1:22; ; 2PE 1:21

title: 5631: work, of God
content: See 1300: God, work of

title: 5632: work, of Jesus Christ
content: See 2300: Jesus Christ, ministry and work of

title: 5633: work, of Holy Spirit
content: See 3200: Holy Spirit, ministry and work of, 3296: Holy Spirit, work in the world

title: 5634: work, and the fall
content:
Human work, which was once a pleasure, became a burden only on account of human disobedience.

Work is under God's judgment

GEN 3:17–3:19 See also GEN 5:29

Work is often frustrating

ECC 2:22–2:23 See also ECC 2:11, ECC 2:18, ECC 4:8, ECC 5:16–5:17

Work may exploit rather than enhance society

Through dishonesty

LEV 19:35; ; DEU 25:13; ; HOS 12:7

Through oppression

EXO 1:11–1:14; ; 1KI 12:4, 1KI 12:10–12:14

Work may be undervalued or overvalued

Some people avoid work to their cost

PRO 6:6–6:11, PRO 13:4, PRO 19:15, PRO 24:30–24:34; ; ECC 10:18; ; 2TH 3:10–3:11

Some people overwork to their cost

EXO 18:17–18:18; ; PSA 127:2; ; LUK 10:41–10:42, LUK 12:15–12:21

title: 5635: work, and redemption
content:
Although human activity cannot merit eternal redemption, work done in this life may, with God's enabling, substantially reflect the divine ideal, in anticipation of the perfect service of heaven.

Human work cannot merit redemption

EPH 2:8–2:9; ; 2TI 1:9; ; TIT 3:4–3:5

Jesus Christ's finished work secures redemption

JHN 17:4 See also JHN 4:34, JHN 19:30; HEB 9:12

Faith leads believers to perform good works

JAS 2:14 See also MAT 7:16–7:20, MAT 12:33; LUK 3:8–3:9; ROM 2:13; HEB 6:10–6:12; JAS 2:17–2:26

Redeemed workers fulfil God's purpose in work

By applying biblical virtues in employment

PRO 10:4, PRO 14:23; ; GAL 6:9; ; COL 4:1

By the pursuit of excellence

ECC 9:10; ; TIT 2:7–2:8, TIT 3:8; ; 1PE 2:12, 1PE 2:15

By doing their work as those responsible to God

ROM 12:1; ; 1CO 7:24, 1CO 10:31; ; EPH 6:7; ; COL 3:23

Work done, as for the Lord, will be rewarded by the Lord

COL 3:23–3:24 See also 2CH 31:21; MAT 25:21; 1CO 15:58

Work will continue in the life to come

REV 22:3 See also MAT 25:21, MAT 25:23; LUK 19:17, LUK 19:19

title: 5636: work, and rest
content:
In creation, God has established a pattern of work and rest that is to be a model for believers.

Work and rest built into creation

EXO 20:11 See also GEN 2:1–2:3; PSA 104:19–104:23

The pattern of work and rest confirmed in the OT

By Sabbath observance

EXO 20:10 parallel DEU 5:14; ; LEV 23:3

By observing holy festivals

EXO 12:16; ; LEV 16:29, LEV 23:6–23:8 parallel NUM 28:17–28:18; ; LEV 23:28–23:31 parallel NUM 29:7; ; LEV 23:35–23:36, LEV 23:39 parallel NUM 29:12; ; EST 9:17–9:19

Work and rest in the ministry of Jesus Christ

MRK 6:30–6:32 See also JHN 4:6

Wisdom needed to balance work and rest

To avoid idleness

PRO 6:9–6:11, PRO 10:4–10:5, PRO 14:23, PRO 20:13, PRO 24:30–24:34

To avoid overwork

EXO 18:13–18:24; ; PSA 127:2; ; LUK 10:38–10:42

Work and rest are both potential means of glorifying God

1CO 10:31 See also ECC 2:24; COL 3:17

Work and rest will be perfectly fulfilled in heaven

REV 14:13, REV 22:3

title: 5638: writing
content:
A form of communication, including the writing of books, letters and scrolls. Many kinds of materials have been written on. Figuratively speaking, the heart can be written on.

Uses of writing

Books

JER 30:2 See also LUK 1:3

The law

DEU 31:24 See also JOS 24:26; 2KI 23:21

Annals and records

1KI 11:41 See also 2KI 12:19; 1CH 29:29; 2CH 35:25

Agreements

NEH 9:38

title: 5654: betrothal
content:
The period of engagement preceding marriage; betrothal was a binding contract established between two families and sealed by the exchange of gifts. During this period the couple did not live together; sexual relations with each other at this stage was regarded as equivalent to adultery. Betrothal describes the relationship between God and his people and between Jesus Christ and the church.

Betrothal and the choice of a spouse

Wives were often chosen by parents for their sons

GEN 21:21 It was usual practice for the groom's parents to choose his wife and arrange the wedding. See also GEN 24:4, GEN 38:6

Suitable husbands were sought by parents for their daughters

RUT 3:1–3:4 Naomi, in the role of parent, assumes responsibility to find a husband for Ruth. See also JDG 1:12–1:13; 1SA 18:17, 1SA 18:21

Betrothal following the couple's wishes

JDG 14:1–14:4 Sometimes the man chose a prospective bride and his parents negotiated the marriage. See also GEN 34:1–34:4, GEN 24:57–24:58, GEN 26:34–26:35 Esau chose a bride against his parents' wishes.

Betrothal preceded marriage

GEN 29:21; ; DEU 20:7 A betrothed soldier was exempted from military service until after his marriage; ; MAT 1:24; ; 1CO 7:36–7:38

An exchange of gifts accompanyed betrothal

The bride-price

GEN 34:11–34:12 This gift, which was given by the groom to the bride's family as compensation, sealed the marriage contract. See also GEN 24:53, GEN 29:18, GEN 29:27; EXO 22:16–22:17; DEU 22:28–22:29; 2SA 3:14

The dowry

1KI 9:16 The dowry was a gift from the bride's father to the bride and/or groom. GEN 24:59, GEN 29:24, GEN 29:29; JDG 1:14–1:15

Betrothal was treated as marriage

DEU 22:23–22:24 Though there were no sexual relations within the betrothal period, the commitment was regarded almost as seriously as marriage and infidelity of a betrothed partner was treated as adultery. See also GEN 19:14 The men betrothed to Lot's daughters are described as his “sons-in-law”; MAT 1:18–1:20 Mary's pregnancy during betrothal left her open to the charge and consequences of unfaithfulness.

Betrothal portrays the relationship between God and his people

HOS 2:19–2:20; 2CO 11:2 See also JHN 3:29; EPH 5:25–5:27; REV 19:7–19:9, REV 21:2

title: 5655: birth
content:
The beginning or origin of life, in which a living creature comes into the world. Scripture draws a distinction between physical and spiritual birth, insisting that a person must be not only physically but also spiritually born in order to have life to the full.

Physical birth

God creates all life

JOB 10:8–10:12; ; PSA 71:6, PSA 139:13

Human beings are sinful from the moment of birth

PSA 51:5 See also JOB 15:14, JOB 25:4; PSA 58:3; JHN 3:6, JHN 9:34; ROM 5:12, ROM 5:17–5:19

The necessity of spiritual birth

Being born again

JHN 3:3

Being born of the Spirit

JHN 3:5–3:8 See also PSA 87:4–87:6; MAT 18:3; JHN 1:12–1:13; 1PE 1:3, 1PE 2:2

The agents of the new birth: word and Spirit

1PE 1:23 See also LUK 10:21; JHN 3:5, JHN 3:7–3:8; TIT 3:5; JAS 1:18

The fruit of the new birth: holiness and love

1JN 3:9, 1JN 4:7 See also MAT 18:4; 1JN 2:29, 1JN 5:3–5:4, 1JN 5:18

Spiritual birth and the nation of Israel

DEU 32:18 See also NUM 11:12 Moses implies that God himself gave birth to the people.

Birth seen as entry into a condition or status

Ethnic identity from birth

title: 5657: birthright
content:
The right of the firstborn son in ancient Israel to inherit his father's estate. Where the property was divided, the firstborn received a double share.

Birthright was recognised amongst the patriarchs

GEN 25:5–25:6, GEN 25:34

Birthright and the law

It was guaranteed under the law

DEU 21:15–21:17 See also 1CH 26:10 some ignored this law

Daughters and others could inherit if there were no sons

NUM 27:1–27:11

Only sons of a lawful marriage qualified

GEN 21:8–21:13; ; JDG 11:1–11:2

Birthright and kingship

Succession was normally to the firstborn

2CH 21:1–21:3 See also 2CH 11:18–11:22 favouritism could intrude here also

Transfer of the birthright

Through misconduct

1CH 5:1 See also GEN 49:3–49:4

By transaction

GEN 25:29–25:34 See also HEB 12:16–12:17

The Christian birthright

ROM 8:17 Jesus Christ is the firstborn over all creation; by the grace of God Christians share in his inheritance. See also GAL 4:7; COL 1:15; HEB 1:2

title: 5658: boys
content:
As those who would continue the family line boys were seen as a great blessing from God. Circumcised on the eighth day, as they grew towards maturity they were to be taught by their fathers. In the story of God's people, Israelite boys are seen serving God, being ministered to by men of God and suffering at the hands of ungodly kings.

Boys in general are seen as a blessing from God

PSA 127:3–127:5 See also RUT 4:13–4:17; PSA 128:3–128:4

Particular boys who are seen as a special gift from God

The boy Isaac, a gift to Abraham and Sarah

GEN 17:15–17:22 See also GEN 21:1–21:7

The boy Samson, a gift to Manoah and his wife

JDG 13:2–13:5 See also JDG 13:24–13:25

The boy Samuel, a gift to Elkanah and Hannah

1SA 1:1–1:20

The boy John, a gift to Zechariah and Elizabeth

LUK 1:5–1:25 See also LUK 1:57–1:66

The boy Jesus, a gift to Mary and Joseph

LUK 1:26–1:38 See also MAT 1:20–1:21

Boys were circumcised on the eighth day

GEN 17:9–17:14 See also LEV 12:3; LUK 1:59, LUK 2:21

Boys were taught by their fathers

PRO 4:1–4:4 While examples of fatherly instruction in Scripture are confined to wisdom literature and liturgical material, other sources indicate that the education provided was more wide-ranging, and would include the teaching of a trade. See also EXO 13:8; DEU 6:20–6:25; PRO 4:10–4:13

Israelite boys who served God

The boy Samuel served God in the temple

1SA 3:1–3:21

The boy David served God by killing Goliath

1SA 17:20–17:51

The boy King Joash served God

2CH 24:1–24:2 parallel 2KI 12:1–12:2

The boy King Josiah served God

2CH 34:1–34:2 parallel 2KI 22:1–22:2

The boy Jesus had a conscious relationship with God

LUK 2:41–2:50

Through Elijah, God restored the life of a widow's son

1KI 17:17–17:23

Through Elisha, God restored the life of a Shunammite's son

2KI 4:32–4:37

Jesus Christ healed a demon-possessed boy

MAT 17:14–17:18 parallels MRK 9:14–9:27, LUK 9:37–9:43

Both Herod and Pharaoh ordered that Israelite boys be killed

MAT 2:16 See also EXO 1:15–1:22

A woman who is about to be married or who has just got married. In the NT the church is described as the bride of Christ.

content:
A man who is to be married or who has just got married. In the NT Jesus Christ is portrayed as a bridegroom and the church as his bride.

The bridegroom wore special clothing

The bridegroom took part in the procession to the bride's home

See also MAT 25:1–25:12

JDG 14:10–14:11

JHN 3:29 See also JDG 14:20–15:2; JHN 2:7–2:10 The “master of the banquet” was probably the friend who attended the bridegroom.

JOL 2:16 See also PSA 19:4–19:5

content:
The son of one's parents, or of either mother or father. God's people may be referred to collectively as brothers, all being children of one heavenly Father.

GEN 29:4 See also 1SA 30:22–30:23; 2SA 1:26, 2SA 20:9; 1KI 13:29–13:30; ACT 1:16, ACT 2:37, ACT 3:17, ACT 7:2, ACT 22:1, ACT 28:17

title: 5662: certificate of divorce
content:
A certificate of divorce was required under Mosaic law

MRK 10:4 parallel MAT 19:7 The certificate provided a divorced wife with some legal protection and permitted her to remarry. See also DEU 24:1–24:4; HOS 2:2 These words may have been adapted from a divorce bill; MAT 5:31

God gave his unfaithful people a certificate of divorce

JER 3:8 See also ISA 50:1 Unlike Israel, Judah had been given no certificate of divorce. The exile is thus portrayed as only a temporary separation.

title: 5663: childbirth
content:
Seen by Scripture as a token of God's favour, and used figuratively to picture a number of central biblical themes.

Childbirth in the OT

Childbirth as a blessing

GEN 1:28 See also DEU 7:14; PSA 127:3–127:5

Childlessness a cause of shame in Israel

GEN 30:1 See also 1SA 1:6, 1SA 1:10–1:11; LUK 1:24–1:25

The nature of human childbirth

The pain of childbirth a consequence of the fall

GEN 3:16

The need for ceremonial purification after childbirth

See also LEV 12:1–12:8 Under the old covenant, unsanctioned contact with blood was ceremonially defiling; LUK 2:24

The role of midwives in childbirth

EXO 1:15–1:21

The joy of childbirth

GEN 21:6; ; JHN 16:21

Childbirth and salvation

The birth of a Saviour

GEN 3:15 Although childbirth is a focus of judgment, through it the human race continues, and the Messiah comes into the world. See also GEN 12:2–12:3, GEN 15:3–15:6; ISA 7:14, ISA 9:6–9:7; MAT 1:18–1:25; LUK 1:35, LUK 2:4–2:7; GAL 3:16, GAL 4:4; REV 12:5

Salvation in childbearing

1TI 2:15 A Christian mother fulfils her calling in childbearing; some take it to mean she will be kept safe in childbirth. Some, however, take this verse as a reference to Ge 3:15, and the coming of Jesus Christ, as above.

Childbirth used figuratively

To describe weakness and vulnerability

See also EZK 16:4–16:6

To describe weakness under judgment

2KI 19:3 parallel ISA 37:3 See also PSA 48:6; ISA 23:4, ISA 26:17–26:18; JER 4:31; HOS 2:3, HOS 13:13; MIC 4:10

GEN 25:22–25:23; ; PSA 139:13, PSA 139:16

ISA 7:14 See also MAT 1:22–1:23, MAT 1:18; LUK 1:30–1:31, LUK 1:34–1:37 “impossible” births demonstrate God's power and grace and show that salvation comes from the Lord.

title: 5664: children
content: Scripture indicates that children are a gift from God and are to be loved, disciplined and cared for. The term “children of God” is used to describe Christian believers, who must grow up in the faith which they have accepted.

title: 5665: children, attitudes towards
content:
Christians must welcome children as Jesus Christ did. They are used by Christ as an example of how believers should receive the kingdom, and as an example of immaturity by Paul.

Children as a gift from God

PSA 113:9, PSA 127:3 See also GEN 33:5, GEN 48:9; JOS 24:3

Jesus Christ welcomes children

MAT 19:13–19:14 parallels MRK 10:13–10:16, LUK 18:15–18:17

God's truth is revealed to the childlike

MAT 11:25 parallel LUK 10:21 See also 1CO 1:26–1:29

Children as people welcomed by Jesus Christ

MAT 18:2–18:5 parallels MRK 9:36–9:37, LUK 9:47–9:48 See also MAT 10:40–10:42 parallel MRK 9:41; MAT 18:10, MAT 18:14

Children as a picture of immature Christians

1CO 14:20; 1PE 2:2–2:3 See also 1CO 13:11; HEB 5:13

Promises to children

DEU 5:16; ACT 2:39 See also PRO 8:32; EPH 6:2–6:3

content:

title: 5667: children, responsibilities to God
content:
The responsibilities of children to God as their heavenly Father include honouring and obeying him.

The responsibilities of children to their heavenly Father

To honour and obey him in reverent fear

title: 5672: concubines
content:
A woman, often a servant or slave, with whom a man had regular sexual relations, but to whom he was not married. A concubine did not have the rights of a wife and her children were not rightful heirs, though a wife might offer a servant to her husband as a concubine to have children on her behalf.

Concubines and wives

Concubines were distinguished from wives

1KI 11:3 Having concubines alongside wives was accepted in a polygamous society. See also JDG 8:30–8:31; 2SA 5:13, 2SA 19:5; 2CH 11:21; DAN 5:2–5:3

Concubines were sometimes called wives

GEN 16:3 Hagar was Abraham's “wife” only in a secondary sense. See also GEN 25:1 Keturah was one of Abraham's concubines; JDG 19:1–19:4

Concubines did not have the rights of a wife

GEN 21:8–21:14 They were more easily dismissed; ; EXO 21:7–21:11 They did have some legal protection.

Maidservants were given as concubines

GEN 30:3–30:6 Bilhah's sons would be regarded by Rachel as her own and would thus share the inheritance with Jacob's other sons. See also GEN 30:9, GEN 16:1–16:2; GAL 4:22–4:23

The tension between concubines and wives

GEN 16:4–16:6 Though Abraham's concubine, Hagar's status was still that of servant. See also GEN 21:9; PRO 30:23; GAL 4:29

Children born to concubines were not rightful heirs

GEN 21:10–21:12 See also GEN 25:5–25:6; JDG 9:18; ROM 9:7; GAL 4:30; HEB 11:18

Concubines were a symbol of possession

By taking Jacob's concubine, Reuben laid premature claim to his father's estate

GEN 35:22 See also GEN 49:3–49:4; 1CH 5:1

Taking the concubine(s) of a king was tantamount to laying claim to the kingdom

2SA 3:7 Abner is accused here of trying to usurp Ish-Bosheth's inheritance. See also 2SA 12:8, 2SA 16:21–16:22; 1KI 2:21–2:22

Further examples of concubines

GEN 22:23–22:24 Nahor's concubine, Reumah; ; GEN 36:12 Eliphaz' concubine, Timna; ; JDG 19:1 a Levite's concubine; ; 2SA 15:16 David's concubines; ; 1CH 1:32 Abraham's concubine, Keturah; ; 1CH 2:46–2:48 Caleb's concubines, Ephah and Maacah; ; 1CH 7:14 Manasseh's concubine; ; EST 2:14 Xerxes' concubines; ; DAN 5:23 Belshazzar's concubines

title: 5674: daughters
content:
The female offspring of parents. Daughters lived in their father's house, under his protection, until marriage. Usually they became his heirs only if he had no sons to inherit his estate. Normally they shared in the inheritance of their husbands.

title: 5675: divorce
content: The legal dissolution of a marriage. Though not part of God's original intention for marriage, divorce is permitted under certain circumstances, especially marital unfaithfulness. In general, properly divorced parties are free to remarry.

title: 5676: divorce, in OT
content:
Usually initiated by the husband who issued his wife with a certificate of divorce and sent her from his home, divorce broke the marriage bond and allowed parties to remarry. It was not part of God's original purpose for marriage, and is permitted only because of human sinfulness. God is depicted as taking divorce proceedings against adulterous Israel.

The nature of divorce

Divorce dissolves a marriage

MRK 10:4 parallel MAT 19:7 The certificate of divorce was a legal document ending the marriage. See also LEV 22:12–22:13 Divorce ends the restrictions on a priest's daughter which were the result of her marriage; NUM 30:9 Following divorce a husband is no longer responsible for his wife; DEU 24:1–24:2 Divorce properly entered into allows the parties to remarry; HOS 2:2; MAT 5:31

Divorce was not God's original intention

MAL 2:10–2:16 God's displeasure at those of his people who divorced their Jewish wives to marry foreigners, thus breaking faith with their partners and with God; MAT 19:4–19:8 parallel MRK 10:5–10:9 The Law of Moses did not command divorce, but regulated an existing practice, particularly to protect the wife. See also GEN 1:27, GEN 2:24

Circumstances permitting divorce

Displeasure

DEU 24:1 See also DEU 21:13–21:14; MAT 19:3

Returning exiles were required to divorce their foreign wives

EZR 10:10–10:11 See also EZR 10:2–10:3

Circumstances where divorce was not allowed

DEU 22:13–22:19 where a husband makes false accusations about his wife's virginity; ; DEU 22:28–22:29 where the marriage is contracted following the rape of a virgin

DEU 24:3–24:4 See also JER 3:1

title: 5677: divorce, amongst believers
content:
Jesus Christ challenged the liberal approach to divorce taken by some rabbis of his day, and upheld the idea of marriage as a lifelong commitment. Remarriage after divorce is generally classed as adultery and, where possible, divorced parties should seek reconciliation. There are circumstances, however, where remarriage is permissible.

The liberal attitude to divorce

MAT 19:3 See also DEU 21:14, DEU 24:1

The undesirability of divorce

God's plan for marriage

MAT 19:4–19:6 parallel MRK 10:6–10:9 See also GEN 1:27, GEN 2:24; MAL 2:15; EPH 5:31

Divorce is permitted because of human sinfulness

MAT 19:8 parallel MRK 10:5

Christians should not seek divorce

1CO 7:10 This command, echoing Jesus Christ's words, applies where both parties are believers. See also 1CO 7:12–7:14

Remarriage after divorce

Believers should seek reconciliation

1CO 7:11 See also DEU 24:2–24:4 Marriage to another after divorce prevents reconciliation.

Remarriage after divorce is classed as adultery

LUK 16:18 parallel MRK 10:11–10:12 This is a general rule, though there may be exceptions (see below). See also ROM 7:2–7:3; 1CO 7:39

Remarriage may be permissible

1CO 7:27–7:28 “unmarried” means literally “freed from a wife” and thus may be applied to those widowed or properly divorced. It is no sin for them to (re)marry.

Possible grounds for divorce and remarriage

MAT 19:9; 1CO 7:15 See also JER 3:8 God divorced Israel because of her adultery; MAT 1:18–1:19, MAT 5:32

title: 5680: family
content: People who are linked by marriage or physical descent. The western idea of a “nuclear” family represents a narrow definition of the scope of the family. The ancient Near East had a broader and more extended understanding of family, which is often reflected in the Scriptural material.

title: 5681: family, nature of
content:
A unit ordained by God for the comfort and protection of its members. It is usually a group of relatives, but the people of God are also seen as a family.

The scope of the family in Scripture

The family unit

GEN 43:7 See also EXO 1:1, EXO 12:3; JDG 11:2; 1SA 1:21, 1SA 27:3; 2SA 2:3; 1KI 17:15; 1CH 13:14 The family of Obed-Edom is blessed by the presence of the ark; PRO 27:27, PRO 31:15 The wife of noble character provides for her family; MRK 3:21; LUK 12:52; ACT 16:33–16:34 The Philippian jailer and his family are baptised; 1TI 5:8

The extended family or clan

GEN 24:37–24:38 See also GEN 24:40, GEN 46:27, GEN 50:22; NUM 2:2, NUM 18:1 the priesthood of Aaron and his family; DEU 25:5 Levirate marriage provides for the continuity of the family; JOS 2:17–2:18, JOS 6:23, JOS 6:25; 1SA 22:22; 1KI 14:14; 2KI 11:1 parallel 2CH 22:10 Athaliah destroys the royal family of Judah; EZR 10:16; JER 35:3, JER 38:17; DAN 1:3

JHN 7:42 See also DEU 25:10; JOS 13:29; 1SA 2:31–2:32, 1SA 2:36, 1SA 3:11–3:13; DAN 11:7

The people of God

HEB 2:10–2:15 See also PSA 22:22; AMO 3:1; GAL 6:10; 1PE 4:17

NUM 27:1–27:11 See also LEV 25:25–25:28; JOB 42:13–42:15

GEN 14:8–14:16 Abraham and Lot; ; 2SA 18:31–18:33 David and Absalom; ; RUT 1:11–1:18 Naomi and Ruth; ; NEH 4:13; ; ACT 23:12–23:24; ; 1TI 5:3–5:4 Family solidarity is encouraged.

title: 5684: fathers
content: The male parent of children. Scripture indicates the role and responsibilities of fathers, and shows how God can be thought of as a loving father, who directs and guides his children.

content:

title: 5690: friends
content: Those to whom one is close. Scripture stresses that friendship is often but not always a positive thing: where good friends can be invaluable in the life of faith, bad friends can be obstacles to the faith of believers, or even lead them astray totally.

content:
Scripture provides insights into, and examples of, the way in which girls have a place in the purposes of God. title: 5700: headship
content:
The quality of being in a position of leadership or guidance. Headship has to do with God's relation to this created world, and to his ordering of relationships within it. Headship among human beings does not necessarily signify superior status, but rather a role of leadership and care. Scripture sees it as involving servanthood, and views Jesus Christ as the supreme model of this.

title: 5702: husband
content:
The male partner in a marriage relationship. The origin of this God-ordained institution is traced back in the Bible to the Garden of Eden. Scripture stresses that marriage is a God-ordained institution, within which the husband is pledged to love and care for his wife. Scripture contains many examples, both good and bad, of how husbands behaved. The ultimate examples of a good husband in Scripture are God as the husband of Israel and Jesus Christ as the bridegroom of the church.

EPH 1:13–1:14 See also REV 7:3, REV 9:4

The conditions of spiritual inheritance

It is conditional upon continuing obedience and faith

1PE 3:9–3:12 See also PSA 34:12–34:16, PSA 25:12–25:13, PSA 37:11, PSA 37:29, PSA 37:34, PSA 61:5; PRO 28:10; MAT 5:5; COL 3:24; HEB 6:12; JAS 2:5

It is denied to the ungodly

EPH 5:5 See also PSA 37:9, PSA 37:22; 1CO 6:9–6:10, 1CO 10:1–10:5; GAL 5:19–5:21; HEB 3:12–3:19; REV 21:27

title: 5707: male and female
content:
God created humanity as male and female. Although gender differences are evident in behaviour and role, Scripture teaches the equality and complementarity of the sexes.

The creation of male and female

GEN 1:27 See also GEN 2:20–2:24, GEN 5:2

The fall disrupted relationships between male and female

GEN 3:14–3:19 See also 2SA 13:1–13:19; PRO 5:3–5:14; MAT 5:28; ROM 1:26–1:27

The equality of male and female

Equality under many old covenant regulations

NUM 5:5–5:7 See also LEV 20:10–20:12; NUM 5:1–5:4; DEU 15:12–15:15, DEU 23:17–23:18

Equality in religious observance

EXO 35:22 See also NUM 6:1–6:4; DEU 31:12; 2SA 6:19

Equality of accountability

LAM 2:21 See also LEV 20:27; 2CH 36:15–36:17; ACT 5:1–5:11

Equality in Christ

GAL 3:26–3:28 See also ACT 2:17–2:18; JOL 2:28–2:29; 1CO 11:11–11:12

Variations in the treatment of male and female

In OT patriarchal society

LEV 27:1–27:7 See also GEN 17:9–17:14; EXO 13:1–13:2, EXO 13:14–13:15; NUM 3:14–3:15, NUM 5:11–5:31, NUM 18:8–18:10

In legislation protecting women under the old covenant

NUM 27:1–27:7 See also NUM 36:1–36:12; DEU 22:13–22:19, DEU 22:25–22:29

In roles within the NT church community

1CO 14:33–14:35 See also 1CO 11:3–11:10; EPH 5:22–5:24 The idea of “headship” is complex, but is generally regarded as including the ideas of responsibility and authority within a relationship; 1TI 2:11–2:15; TIT 2:1–2:5

In behaviour within the NT church community

1TI 2:8–2:10 See also 1CO 11:3–11:16; 1TI 5:1–5:2

Male and female roles within marriage

1CO 7:1–7:7 See also PRO 31:10–31:31; EPH 5:22–5:33; COL 3:18–3:19; 1PE 3:1–3:7

Male and female imagery used of God

Female imagery

MAT 23:37 parallel LUK 13:34 See also PRO 8:1–8:11; ISA 66:12–66:13

Male imagery

PSA 47:2 See also EXO 15:3; PSA 23:1; MAT 6:6; LUK 11:11–11:13 parallel MAT 7:9–7:11

title: 5708: marriage
content: The union of a man and a woman in a permanent relationship. Though a lifelong monogamous commitment is presented as the ideal, polygamous marriages were occasionally known in OT times and carried the same legal and moral rights and responsibilities. God's relationship with his people is described in terms of the marriage bond.

resource.label: 5712: marriage, between God and his people

title: 5709: marriage, purpose of
content:
Marriage is part of God's intention for humanity from creation and forms the basis for the family which is the primary unit of society. Where marriage flourishes it blesses both the couple and the wider community.

Marriage is part of God's plan for the human race

From creation

MAT 19:4 parallel MRK 10:6 See also GEN 1:27; 1CO 11:11–11:12 Man and woman are not independent of each other.

It is to provide companionship

GEN 2:18 See also GEN 2:20–2:22, GEN 3:12; PRO 31:10–31:12

It is to be a committed, exclusive relationship

GEN 2:23–2:24 See also MAT 19:5 parallel MRK 10:7–10:8; 1CO 7:2; EPH 5:31

It is a lifelong partnership

MAT 19:6 parallel MRK 10:9 See also ROM 7:2; 1CO 7:39

It is the intended context for raising children

MAL 2:15 See also 1CO 7:14

It will not exist in the life to come

MAT 22:30 parallels MRK 12:25, LUK 20:34–20:35; ; 1CO 7:29–7:31

Marriage as a covenant relationship

MAL 2:14 See also PRO 2:17; EZK 16:8

Sex and marriage

Sex belongs within marriage

1CO 7:9 See also GEN 29:21EXO 22:16–22:17; DEU 22:28–22:29 DEU 22:13–22:21 A woman was expected to be a virgin when she married.

The sexual relationship is exclusive

SNG 2:16 See also DEU 22:22–22:24 Marital unfaithfulness is condemned; PRO 5:15–5:19; 1CO 6:16, 1CO 7:3–7:5

Love and submission in marriage

Falling in love prior to marriage

GEN 29:20 See also GEN 34:3–34:4; 1SA 18:20

Husbands are to love their wives

EPH 5:25 See also GEN 24:67; 1SA 1:5; ECC 9:9; HOS 3:1; EPH 5:28–5:29, EPH 5:33; COL 3:19

Wives are to submit to their husbands

GEN 3:16; EPH 5:22–5:24 See also COL 3:18; TIT 2:4–2:5; 1PE 3:1–3:6

Celibacy as a calling from God

1CO 7:7–7:8 See also JER 16:2; MAT 19:10–19:12; 1CO 7:36–7:38 Whilst Paul commends the unmarried state, for those not so called it is no sin to marry; 1TI 5:11–5:14

title: 5710: marriage, customs concerning
content:
Marriage between two individuals united their families and involved the whole community. Parents, particularly fathers, took an active part in selecting partners for their children. There was often a long period of betrothal; wedding celebrations were usually elaborate and might last a week or more.

The choice of a marriage partner

Parents usually chose a suitable partner

GEN 38:6 See also GEN 24:2–24:4, GEN 21:21 Occasionally mothers made the wedding arrangements.

The wishes of the couple

GEN 24:57–24:58 Rebekah is consulted about her proposed marriage to Isaac. See also GEN 34:4, GEN 34:8–34:9; JDG 14:2; 1SA 18:20

The bride-price

Daughters were ``given'' by their fathers

GEN 29:28; ; EXO 2:21; ; 1SA 18:21

Fathers often received payment

GEN 29:18, GEN 34:12 See also GEN 29:30; EXO 22:16–22:17; DEU 22:28–22:29; 1SA 18:17, 1SA 18:27

Daughters were given as a reward

JDG 1:12–1:13 parallel JOS 15:16–15:17 See also 1SA 18:25

The exchange of wedding gifts

Gifts from the bridegroom's family

GEN 24:53

Gifts from the bride's father

Servants given to the bride as a dowry: GEN 24:59, GEN 29:24, GEN 29:29; JDG 1:14–1:15 parallel JOS 15:18–15:19; ; 1KI 9:16

The period of betrothal

Betrothal followed payment of the bride-price

2SA 3:14 See also GEN 29:19–29:20 Jacob worked for Laban during his period of betrothal to Rachel.

A betrothed couple were regarded as husband and wife

GEN 19:14; ; DEU 22:23–22:24 Unfaithfulness during the period of betrothal is treated as adultery; ; MAT 1:18–1:20 Divorce is required to break a betrothal.

Sexual relationships took place only after the wedding

GEN 29:21 JOL 1:8; ; LUK 1:27; MAT 1:25; ; 1CO 7:36–7:38

Soldiers and marriage

DEU 20:7 Engaged soldiers were to marry before going into battle; ; DEU 24:5 Recently married soldiers were exempted from military service for a year.

The wedding celebrations

The bride wore an elaborate dress and jewellery

EZK 16:9–16:13 An allegorical description of God dressing Jerusalem as a bride. See also PSA 45:13; ISA 61:10; JER 2:32; REV 21:2

Attendants on the bride and groom

PSA 45:14; JHN 3:29 See also JDG 14:11, JDG 14:20; MAT 9:15 parallels MRK 2:19, LUK 5:34; MAT 25:1–25:10

The wedding banquet

GEN 29:22; ; JDG 14:10; ; MAT 22:2; ; REV 19:9

Wedding festivities

PSA 78:63; ; ISA 62:5; ; JER 7:34, JER 33:11

The invitation to a wedding

MAT 22:3–22:4 Invited guests were called when the feast was ready.; MAT 22:5–22:7; ; LUK 14:18–14:21; MAT 22:11–22:12 Guests were expected to dress appropriately.

title: 5711: marriage, restrictions concerning
content:
The OT law forbade intermarriage with people who worshipped idols because it threatened the covenant relationship with God and his people. Marriage with close relations was also forbidden. Remarriage is permissible following the death of a spouse and, in certain circumstances, following divorce.

Intermarriage with foreigners

Examples of marriages to foreigners

GEN 38:2, GEN 41:45; ; EXO 2:21; ; LEV 24:10; ; RUT 1:4; ; 1CH 2:34–2:35; ; EZR 10:18–10:44

Warnings against marrying foreigners

EXO 34:16 See also DEU 7:3–7:4; JOS 23:12–23:13

Intermarriage with foreigners led to idolatry

JDG 3:5–3:6; 1KI 11:1–11:8 Royal marriages to foreigners brought disastrous consequences. See also 1KI 16:31; MAL 2:11EZR 9:1–9:2, EZR 9:14, EZR 10:1–10:2; NEH 13:23–13:27

Parents sought to avoid their children marrying foreigners

NEH 10:30 See also GEN 24:3–24:4 Abraham seeks a bride for Isaac from among his own people.GEN 26:34–26:35, GEN 27:46 GEN 28:1–28:2 Isaac forbids Jacob to marry a Canaanite woman; JDG 14:3 Samson's parents encourage him to marry an Israelite.

Marriage to foreigners may be permissible

RUT 4:13 Boaz' marriage to Ruth the Moabitess was acceptable because Ruth embraced the Israelite faith. Restrictions were on the grounds of religion not of race.

Foreign wives were put aside after the exile

EZR 10:3 See also EZR 10:10–10:17

Marriages between Christians and unbelievers

Christians should not marry unbelievers

1CO 7:39; ; 2CO 6:14

Christians should not leave an unbelieving spouse

1CO 7:12–7:16

Restrictions on marriage to close relatives

Sexual relations with close relatives is forbidden

LEV 18:6–18:18 See also LEV 20:11–20:12, LEV 20:14, LEV 20:19–20:21; DEU 22:30; EZK 22:10–22:11; MAT 14:3–14:4 parallel MRK 6:17–6:18

Examples of marriage to close relatives

GEN 20:12 Abraham was married to his half-sister; ; 2SA 13:13 Tamar suggests marriage with her half-brother, Amnon.

Levirate marriage

The levirate law was instituted to preserve the dead father's name

DEU 25:5–25:10; RUT 4:10 Levirate marriage refers to the legal obligation of a brother-in-law to produce heirs for his dead brother by marrying his widow. When there was no brother-in-law responsibility fell to a near relative, also described as a “kinsman-redeemer”. See also GEN 38:8, GEN 38:11; RUT 1:11–1:13, RUT 3:9, RUT 4:5; MAT 22:24–22:26 parallels MRK 12:19–12:22, LUK 20:28–20:31

Unwillingness to fulfil the levirate law

GEN 38:9, GEN 38:14, GEN 38:26; ; RUT 4:6

Regulations governing seduction and rape

EXO 22:16; ; DEU 22:28–22:29

Remarriage

Widows are free to remarry

ROM 7:2–7:3 See also RUT 1:9; 1CO 7:8–7:9; 1TI 5:14

Remarriage after divorce may be adultery

LUK 16:18 parallels MAT 19:9, MRK 10:11–10:12 See also 1CO 7:10–7:11

Remarriage after divorce permissible in certain circumstances

DEU 24:1–24:4; ; MAT 5:32; ; 1CO 7:15, 1CO 7:27–7:28

title: 5712: marriage, between God and his people
content:
Marriage is used to describe the relationship between God and Israel in the OT and between Jesus Christ and the church in the NT. Contemplating marriage deepens understanding of God's love for his people; examining God's covenant love for his people similarly enriches an understanding of marriage.

God's marriage relationship with Israel

God's marriage covenant with Israel

EZK 16:8–16:14 The covenant at Sinai was seen as a form of marriage. See also JER 31:32; EZK 16:59–16:60

God as Israel's husband

ISA 54:5 See also HOS 2:7; JOL 1:8

Israel's early devotion

JER 2:2 See also EZK 16:43; HOS 2:15

The breakdown of God's marriage to Israel

Israel's adultery

JER 3:20 See also JER 2:32; EZK 16:32–16:34; HOS 1:2, HOS 9:1

Israel's alienation from God is likened to a divorce

HOS 2:2 Israel's unfaithfulness led to a form of divorce between God and his people. This was sometimes identified with the exile. See also ISA 50:1; JER 3:6–3:10

The renewal of God's marriage to Israel

God calls his bride to return

JER 3:12–3:14; HOS 3:1–3:3 See also ISA 54:6–54:8; HOS 2:14

The renewed relationship

ISA 62:4–62:5 See also JER 31:31–31:33; EZK 16:62; HOS 2:16, HOS 2:19–2:20

Jesus Christ's marriage relationship with the church

Jesus Christ's love as a model for marriage

EPH 5:25–5:33

Jesus Christ is described as a bridegroom

JHN 3:29 John the Baptist describes Jesus Christ as the bridegroom and himself as the best man. See also MAT 9:15 parallels MRK 2:19–2:20, LUK 5:34–5:35; MAT 22:2, MAT 25:1–25:13

The church as Christ's bride

2CO 11:2; REV 19:7–19:9 See also REV 21:2, REV 21:9–21:10, REV 22:17

title: 5714: men
content:
God created both men and women in his image and likeness. Scripture portrays men in both their strengths and weaknesses, their successes and failures. While noting that they are incomplete without women, and share equally in the privileges and tasks entrusted to them by God, men have nevertheless been given specific responsibilities by God.

The place of men

Men are equal with women in creation

GEN 1:27 See also GEN 5:2

Men are incomplete without women

GEN 2:18 See also GEN 2:21–2:25; 1CO 11:11–11:12

Absence of men in society seen as a curse

ISA 3:1–3:3 See also LAM 5:14; EZK 17:11–17:14

Men are equal with women in redemption

GAL 3:28 See also ACT 2:17–2:18; JOL 2:28–2:29

The role of men

As leaders in marriage and family life

EPH 5:22–5:24 See also 1CO 11:3; COL 3:18–3:21

As leaders in Israelite society and worship

NUM 1:16 See also EXO 34:23–34:24; NUM 3:10–3:15; DEU 1:9–1:15; 1SA 8:1; EZR 10:16–10:17

As leaders in the early church

1TI 3:2 See also ACT 6:2–6:6; 1TI 2:12 The role of teaching and exercising authority is here restricted to men. Interpretations vary as to whether Paul is reflecting cultural circumstance or establishing theological principle; 1TI 3:8

The character requirements of men

To be prayerful and godly

1TI 2:8 See also DAN 6:10–6:11; 1TI 4:7–4:8, 1TI 6:11–6:12

To be courageous

1CO 16:13 While courage can be exercised by all, it is identified here as a specifically male characteristic. See also ACT 4:13, ACT 27:21–27:25

To be determined and decisive

MAT 11:12 See also 1CH 12:38

To be humble

1PE 5:5 See also NUM 12:3; DAN 10:12; MAT 11:29

To love their wives

COL 3:19 See also PRO 5:15–5:19; EPH 5:25–5:33

To be good fathers to their children

EPH 6:4 See also GEN 37:3–37:4 Jacob's favouritism was the cause of resentment developing in the family; 1SA 3:12–3:13 Eli is rebuked for having failed to father his sons properly; COL 3:21

To exercise proper sexual restraint

1TH 4:3–4:7 That Paul is particularly thinking of men here seems apparent from the NIV footnote at verse 4. See also LEV 18:1–18:22; PRO 6:23–6:29; MAT 5:27–5:28; 1CO 5:1–5:2, 1CO 7:2–7:5

Examples of godly men

GEN 6:9 Noah; ; GEN 22:1–22:12 Abraham; ; EXO 32:30–32:32 Moses; ; 1SA 24:1–24:7 David; ; 2KI 18:1–18:7 Hezekiah; ; JOB 1:1–1:8 Job; ; DAN 6:10 Daniel; ; ACT 4:13–4:20 Peter and John; ; ACT 7:54–7:60 Stephen; ; HEB 11:4–11:28 OT heroes of faith; ; JAS 5:17–5:18 Elijah

Examples of godly men who had moments of failure

GEN 20:1–20:3 Abraham was deceitful; ; NUM 20:2–20:12 Moses and Aaron showed unbelief; ; 2SA 11:1–11:27 David committed adultery with Bathsheba and plotted Uriah's death; ; 1KI 19:1–19:5 Elijah became fearful and wanted to die; ; JON 1:1–1:3 Jonah ran from God's call on his life; ; MAT 26:69–26:75 parallels MRK 14:66–14:72, LUK 22:55–22:62, JHN 18:16–18:18, JHN 18:25–18:27 Peter denied Jesus Christ; ; ACT 16:36–16:40 Paul and Barnabas fell into sharp disagreement.

Examples of ungodly men

GEN 19:4–19:5 The ungodliness of the men of Sodom lay in sexual immorality; ; GEN 38:8–38:10 Onan's ungodliness lay in failing to fulfil his obligations to his brother's wife; ; NUM 16:1–16:35 Korah's ungodliness lay in rebellion against God's leaders; ; 1SA 2:12 Eli's sons' ungodliness lay in their abuse of the sacrifices; ; 1KI 16:29–16:33 Ahab's ungodliness lay in intermarriage and idolatry; ; 2KI 21:1–21:9 parallel 2CH 33:1–33:9 Manasseh's ungodliness lay in idolatry, divination and human sacrifice; ; MAT 2:16 Herod's ungodliness lay in the wholesale slaughter of infants; ; MAT 14:3–14:11 parallel MRK 6:17–6:28 Herod the tetrarch's ungodliness lay in immorality and murder; ; ACT 8:9–8:23 Simon's ungodliness lay in the practice of magic; ; JUD 1:4–1:19 The ungodliness of men in the church lay in their rejection of apostolic doctrine and lifestyle.

Examples of fearful men

GEN 26:7–26:9 Isaac's fear of the Philistines led him to lie; ; NUM 13:26–13:33 The spies' fear led them to give a bad report; ; 1SA 28:5–28:7 Saul's fear of the Philistines led him to enquire of a medium when the LORD did not answer him; ; 2SA 3:7–3:11 Ish-Bosheth's fear of his brother led him to stay silent concerning sin; ; JHN 19:4–19:16 parallels MAT 27:19–27:26, MRK 15:9–15:15, LUK 23:13–23:25 Pilate's fear of the crowd led him to condemn Jesus Christ, even though he knew he was innocent; ; ACT 24:24–24:25 Felix' fear arose from the message of the gospel.

Examples of weak men

LEV 26:36–26:39 Men who are disobedient to God will be weak; ; 1SA 3:12–3:13 Eli's weakness lay in failing to restrain his sons; ; 1KI 21:1–21:16 Ahab's weakness lay in his allowing his wife to rule his life and his kingdom.

title: 5715: menstruation
content:
A woman was considered ceremonially unclean during menstruation

LEV 15:19–15:23 See also LEV 12:1–12:5, LEV 15:25–15:30; ISA 30:22

Sexual intercourse during menstruation forbidden

LEV 18:19 See also LEV 20:18; EZK 18:5–18:6, EZK 22:10

The discomfort of menstruation

GEN 31:35

title: 5716: middle age
content:
The period between youth and old age. Middle age is marked by physical strength and experience and should bring maturity and stability. Many of God's servants began ministry in middle age, often after having been prepared in their youth. Middle age may also bring complacency and the temptation to leave the devotion and commitments of youth.

Middle age defined

Adulthood reckoned from age 20

NUM 1:2–1:3 See also EXO 30:14, EXO 38:26; NUM 26:2–26:41CH 23:24 See also 2CH 31:17; EZR 3:8

Full maturity reckoned from age 30

LUK 3:23 See also NUM 4:30, NUM 4:43

Characteristics of middle age

Physical strength

LEV 27:3–27:7 Strength is greatest between 20 and 60. See also NUM 1:45 Men served in the army from age 20; JOS 14:10 Caleb, in his prime at 40, is still strong at 85.

Growth in wisdom and experience

ECC 1:16 See also 1SA 17:33; 2SA 17:8; 2CH 17:131CH 22:5 See also 1CH 29:1; PRO 7:7

Maturity and stability

EPH 4:13–4:14 See also 1CO 2:6; HEB 5:11–5:14; JAS 1:4

The responsibilities of middle age

The need to be prepared for these responsibilities

PRO 22:6 See also PRO 4:1–4:4 Solomon passes on wisdom learned from his father.LUK 1:801SA 2:26; LUK 2:40

The need to train for service

NUM 8:24 The period from 25 to 30 (see Nu 4:3) may have been a period of apprenticeship. See also 1CH 23:27 In later years the apprenticeship may have started at 20; NUM 11:28

The start of service in middle age

NUM 4:3 See also ACT 7:23 Moses showed concern for his fellow Israelites at age 40; JOS 14:7 Caleb was 40 when he explored Canaan; 1SA 7:3–7:4 Samuel became judge over Israel in his thirties; LUK 3:3 John the Baptist began his public ministry at about 30; JHN 8:57 Jesus Christ had not achieved the status of wisdom and authority associated with old age in Israel; 1TI 3:1–3:13 The mention of families in the instructions to elders and deacons suggests that these leaders were of middle age.

Rulers coming to office in middle age

GEN 41:46 Joseph; ; 1SA 13:1 Saul; ; 2SA 5:4 David; ; 2SA 2:10 Ish-Bosheth; ; 2CH 12:13 parallel 1KI 14:21 Rehoboam; ; 2CH 20:31 Jehoshaphat

Temptations of middle age

Complacency

2SA 11:1; ; ISA 32:9–32:11; ; AMO 6:1

Worldly distractions

2SA 11:4; ; 1KI 11:3–11:4; ; ECC 2:1–2:8; ; LUK 12:18–12:19

Turning from the commitment of youth

PRO 2:16–2:17; ; MAL 2:14

title: 5717: monogamy
content:
The practice of having and remaining faithful to only one marriage partner at one time. It is set out as God's ideal for human relationships; an ideal demonstrated in the use of the marriage bond to portray the relationship between God and his people.

Monogamy as God's original intention for marriage

GEN 2:22–2:24 See also MAL 2:15; MAT 19:4–19:6 parallel MRK 10:6–10:9; EPH 5:31

Monogamy is shown in God's relationship with his people

God's marriage with Israel

EZK 16:8 See also ISA 54:5–54:8; JER 2:2–2:3; HOS 2:16–2:20, HOS 3:1; EPH 5:32–5:33

God's exclusive commitment to Israel

DEU 14:2; AMO 3:2 See also EXO 19:5–19:6; DEU 26:18, DEU 32:8; PSA 135:4

Monogamy in marriage

The commitment to a lifelong, loving companionship

GEN 2:18; PRO 5:15–5:19 The satisfaction that may be found in marriage makes marital unfaithfulness and polygamy unnecessary. See also PRO 2:17; ECC 9:9; MAL 2:14

Polygamy undermines full commitment

DEU 21:15 Favouritism within polygamous relationships undermines the close companionship which should characterise marriage. See also GEN 29:30; 1SA 1:1–1:8; 2CH 11:21–11:22

Monogamy is implicit in teaching about divorce

MAT 19:9 parallel MRK 10:11 See also LUK 16:18

Monogamy is commanded

1CO 7:2–7:4 This is an implicit, but clear prohibition of polygamy; 1TI 3:12 Monogamy is obligatory in leaders. See also 1TI 3:2; TIT 1:6

title: 5718: mothers
content: The female parent of children. The role and influence of mothers are frequently stressed in Scripture, and their care for children is used as a picture of God's care for his people.

title: 5719: mothers, responsibilities of
content:
The fundamental importance of motherhood is recognised throughout Scripture.

Motherhood and childbirth

God plans happiness for women in motherhood

PSA 113:9

The need for a mother's cleansing after childbirth

See also LEV 12:1–12:8; LUK 2:22–2:24

A mother's relationship with her children

A mother loves and cares for her children

1TH 2:7 Paul's statement assumes that a mother's normal attitude towards her child is one of love and care. See also LUK 2:48

A mother's role as teacher

PRO 1:8 See also PRO 6:20; 2TI 1:5

The responsibility to discipline children

PRO 29:15

The joy or sorrow of parents at their children's conduct

PRO 10:1 See also PRO 23:25

The negative influence of some mothers upon their children

2CH 22:3 See also GEN 27:5–27:17; 1KI 22:52; MAT 14:6–14:8, MAT 20:20–20:22

Children's reponsibility to honour their parents

EXO 20:12 parallel DEU 5:16 “Honour” implies respect, obedience and care for the parents' needs. See also LEV 19:3; MAT 19:19 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20; EPH 6:1–6:3

This honour is due especially to mothers in old age

PRO 23:22

Penalties for disobeying parents

EXO 21:15, EXO 21:17; ; DEU 21:18–21:21; ; PRO 20:20; ; MAT 15:4–15:6 parallel MRK 7:10–7:13

Sexual relations with one's mother or mother-in-law are forbidden

LEV 18:7; ; DEU 27:23

Upon marriage the mother-child relationship becomes secondary

GEN 2:24 See also MAT 19:5 parallel MRK 10:7; EPH 5:31

Care for a mother-in-law

RUT 2:11 See also MAT 8:14–8:15 parallels MRK 1:29–1:31, LUK 4:38

The ministry of Jesus Christ may produce conflict within families

LUK 12:53 parallel MAT 10:35–10:36

Following Jesus Christ involves a commitment to him even deeper than love of one's parents

MAT 10:37 See also LUK 14:26

Jesus Christ regards those who do God's will as his own family

MAT 12:49–12:50 parallels MRK 3:31–3:35, LUK 8:19–8:21 See also MAT 19:29 parallels MRK 10:29, LUK 18:29–18:30

title: 5720: mothers, examples of
content:
Examples are given in Scripture of notable mothers, mothers-in-law and grandmothers.

Eve, the mother of all the living

GEN 3:20 See also GEN 3:16

Hagar, the mother of Ishmael

GEN 16:1–16:4, GEN 16:15

Sarah, the mother of Isaac

GEN 21:1–21:3 See also GEN 17:15–17:19, GEN 18:10–18:14

Rebekah, mother of Esau and Jacob

GEN 25:21, GEN 25:24, GEN 27:5–27:17

Rachel, mother of Joseph and Benjamin

GEN 30:22–30:24, GEN 35:16–35:18

Jochebed, mother of Moses

EXO 2:1–2:2, EXO 6:20; ; HEB 11:23

Naomi, Ruth's mother-in-law

RUT 1:15, RUT 4:13–4:17

Hannah, mother of Samuel

1SA 1:2, 1SA 1:11, 1SA 1:20

Jezebel, who taught her sons to worship Baal rather than the LORD

1KI 22:52; ; 2KI 9:22

The Shunammite woman

2KI 4:16–4:22, 2KI 4:32–4:37

Elizabeth, mother of John the Baptist

LUK 1:5–1:7, LUK 1:13, LUK 1:24–1:25, LUK 1:57
