title: 5725: old age
content: Living for a relatively long time was regarded as a blessing from God and the aged in society are to be respected. Advancing years can bring greater wisdom and in both the OT and NT elders are given authority and leadership. Old age brings physical weakness and Scripture recognises this but states God's ability to strengthen and sustain the aged.

title: 5726: old age, attainment of
content:
Attaining old age is regarded as a blessing from God, often as a reward for obedience. The physical weakness brought by old age is recognised; so too is God's ability to strengthen and sustain the aged. Old age is often accompanied by a growth in wisdom and discernment.

Life expectancy in the OT

Before the flood

GEN 5:5, GEN 5:8, GEN 5:11, GEN 5:27 Methuselah died in the year of the flood; ; GEN 9:29

After the flood

GEN 6:3 See also GEN 11:10–11:25 Following the flood, the span of life gradually reduces; GEN 25:7–25:8 Abraham's death at 175 is considered “a good old age”.

In later generations

PSA 90:10 See also 2SA 5:4–5:5, 2SA 19:34–19:35

Attaining old age is a blessing from God

Long life as a reward for obedience

DEU 5:33 See also EXO 20:12 parallel DEU 5:16; DEU 4:40; PRO 3:1–3:2, PRO 16:31; ECC 8:13

Reaching old age is a mark of God's favour

GEN 15:15 See also GEN 24:1, GEN 35:29 Isaac; JDG 8:32 Gideon; 1CH 29:28 David, like Abraham and Gideon is described as dying at “a good old age”; 2CH 24:15 Jehoiada; JOB 42:17 Job

God strengthens and sustains them

ISA 46:4 See also DEU 34:7; JOS 14:10–14:11; JOB 5:26; PSA 92:14

GEN 21:7 Abraham and Sarah; ; 2KI 4:16–4:17 the Shunammite woman; ; LUK 1:36 Elizabeth

JOB 12:12 See also JOB 15:10; PRO 20:29; JHN 8:9; TIT 2:2

title: 5727: old age, attitudes to
content:
Old age is generally held in honour and the aged in society are to be respected. Because of the wisdom associated with their advancing years elders had an important role of authority and guidance in Israelite society and the NT speaks of the leadership of elders within the church.

Respect for the aged

LEV 19:32; 1PE 5:5 See also JOB 29:8; PRO 16:31, PRO 20:29; 1TI 5:1

LEV 19:3; PRO 23:22 See also EXO 20:12, EXO 21:17; LEV 20:9; DEU 27:16; PRO 30:17; MAT 15:4 parallel MRK 7:10; EPH 6:1–6:3; COL 3:20

Old age is associated with wisdom

JOB 32:6–32:7 See also 1KI 12:6–12:8 parallel 2CH 10:6–10:8 Rehoboam rejected the advice of elders and rebellion ensued; JOB 12:12, JOB 15:10; PHM 1:9 Paul refers to his age to add authority to his words.

Elders in the church

content:
Children whose parents are dead; a vulnerable group of people to whom God shows special kindness. He expects his people to do the same. Those who exploit them incur God's judgment.

title: 5732: polygamy
content:
The practice of having more than one wife at one time. Although not explicitly forbidden in Scripture as a general practice, it is presented as problematic and monogamy is the clearly preferred option.

Monogamy is God's intention for marriage

GEN 2:24 See also JER 2:2; HOS 2:19–2:20; EPH 5:31

Early examples of polygamy

GEN 4:19 See also GEN 26:34, GEN 28:9, GEN 29:28

Reasons for the practice of polygamy

Sealing foreign treaties

1KI 3:1 See also 1KI 16:31

Producing offspring

GEN 16:1–16:3; 2CH 13:21 A large family, and especially numerous progeny, was regarded as a sign of divine blessing. See also GEN 30:3–30:5, GEN 30:9; JDG 8:30; 2SA 3:1–3:5; 1CH 7:4; 2CH 11:23, 2CH 24:2–24:3

Being led away from God

DEU 17:17 It was common for kings to cement foreign alliances by marriage. Israel's king is warned against the practice; 1KI 11:1–11:8 See also NEH 13:25–13:26; MAL 2:11

Conflicts within families

GEN 29:30, GEN 30:1; DEU 21:15–21:17 See also GEN 16:4–16:6 Sarah and Hagar; 1SA 1:4–1:7 Hannah and Peninnah; 2CH 11:21–11:22; 1KI 1:11–1:13 the conflict over the succession to David's throne

title: 5734: relationships
content:
God created people to be in relationship with himself and with one another in friendship, marriage, family, society and the church.

With God

GEN 2:18 See also PSA 127:4; PRO 17:6, PRO 17:17, PRO 18:24, PRO 27:10; ECC 4:9–4:12

title: 5735: sexuality
content:
Men and women are intended to complement one another and to take pleasure in one another. God has provided for the full and glad expression of this in marriage.

Sexuality comes from God

It was created by God

GEN 1:27

God intended men and women to complement one another

1CO 11:11 See also GEN 2:18–2:22

In strength

1PE 3:7

In role

1CO 11:3–11:5, 1CO 14:34–14:35; ; EPH 5:22–5:25; ; COL 3:18–3:19; ; 1TI 2:12–2:14; ; 1PE 3:1

DEU 22:5 See also 1CO 11:14–11:15

GEN 1:28 This command was made before the fall, and no guilt attaches to it.

title: 5736: singleness
content:
Not being married; the state prior to betrothal or following separation or the death of a spouse. In Scripture, an unmarried woman generally lives with, and is the responsibility of, her family. Whilst the unmarried are freer of worldly concerns and may devote themselves more fully to God, those already married should not separate, and those without the gift of celibacy should not remain single.

An unmarried woman is responsible to her father

An unmarried woman is dependent on her brothers

title: 5738: sons
content:
The male offspring of parents. While sharing in the general privileges and responsibilities of children, sons had special claims to inheritance from their parents. To refer to Christians as “sons of God” is to identify both their relationship to God and also their rights as heirs of God. A significant number of titles for Jesus Christ make use of the term “Son”, stressing the close relationship between the Father and Son.

Privileges of sonship

Inheritance

PRO 13:22; ; GAL 4:7; ; HEB 1:2

Being disciplined

Discipline is here seen as a loving means of enabling a child to grow to maturity: DEU 8:5; ; PRO 19:18, PRO 29:17; ; HEB 12:5–12:11; ; REV 3:19

Being loved and provided for

GEN 37:1–37:35 Jacob's eleven sons; ; LUK 15:11–15:32

GEN 19:12–19:14; ; JDG 19:5; ; 1SA 18:18–18:27

title: 5739: twins
content:
Two children born of the same parents at the same time. Figuratively used to describe a matching pair.

Examples of twins

GEN 25:21–25:26 Although Jacob and Esau were twins, their very different characters indicate that God deals with and relates to people individually. See also GEN 38:27–38:30; JHN 20:24 Didymus means “twin”. It is not known who his twin was; JHN 21:2; ACT 28:11 the mythical twin sons of Zeus regarded as special protectors of sailors

Twins used to illustrate God's election

ROM 9:10–9:16

Twins used figuratively for matching pairs

SNG 4:2, SNG 4:5, SNG 6:6, SNG 7:3

title: 5740: virgin
content:
Generally a young person, especially a female, who has not had sexual intercourse. Virginity is an important quality in a bride, and its surrender or violation prior to marriage is sternly condemned. In the miracle of the incarnation, Mary was still a virgin when Jesus Christ was conceived. Virginity is also used metaphorically to denote purity and innocence.

Virginity is important in a bride

Virgins were sought as brides

GEN 24:14–24:16; SNG 4:12 See also GEN 24:42–24:45 The word translated “maiden” might also refer to a virgin; LEV 21:13–21:14; DEU 22:13–22:19; EST 2:2, EST 2:17; ISA 62:5; EZK 44:22

The church presented as a virgin bride

2CO 11:2 See also EPH 5:25–5:27; REV 19:7–19:8

The loss of virginity before marriage

Of a virgin not pledged in marriage

EXO 22:16–22:17 See also DEU 22:28–22:29; 2SA 13:12–13:16

Of a virgin pledged in marriage

DEU 22:20–22:21 See also DEU 22:23–22:24 Betrothal was as serious a commitment as marriage itself; consorting with another person during this period was tantamount to adultery; DEU 22:25–22:27; MAT 1:18–1:19

Some fathers surrendered their daughters' virginity

GEN 19:8 See also JDG 19:24

Particular roles involving virgins

Maidens in victory processions

PSA 68:25; JER 31:4 See also EXO 15:20–15:21; JDG 11:34; 1SA 18:6

Virgins as bridesmaids

PSA 45:14 See also MAT 25:1

A virgin looked after King David

1KI 1:1–1:4

Virginity as a sign of purity and innocence

Virgins were spared after military victories

NUM 31:17–31:18 See also JDG 21:11–21:12

Israel's virgin purity lost

JER 18:13 See also JER 31:21–31:23; EZK 23:3–23:8

Virginity as a metaphor for (apparent) inviolability

2KI 19:21 parallel ISA 37:22; ; ISA 47:1

Lost opportunities of virgin youthfulness

AMO 5:2 See also JDG 11:36–11:40; ISA 23:12; JER 46:11; LAM 1:15–1:16, LAM 2:13; JOL 1:8

Paul's advice about virgins

A virgin is freer to serve God

1CO 7:32–7:35 The unmarried have fewer responsibilities and worldly cares and so may offer undivided devotion to God. See also 1CO 7:25–7:28

Remaining unmarried is a preferred option

1CO 7:8, 1CO 7:37–7:38

Marriage is the proper outlet for sexual passion

1CO 7:9 Though Paul urges abstinence, sexual passion is not wrong; however, sexual relationships must be confined to marriage; ; 1CO 7:36

Mary's virginity at Jesus Christ's conception

MAT 1:20–1:25 See also ISA 7:14; LUK 1:27, LUK 1:34–1:35

Parable of the ten virgins

MAT 25:1–25:13

title: 5741: vows
content:
Promises made to God, usually in the context of worship or religious practice. There was no requirement on any Israelite to make vows, but once made, they were binding and had to be kept.

Vows were binding

DEU 23:21–23:23 See also NUM 30:2, NUM 30:9; PRO 20:25; ECC 5:4–5:6; MAL 1:14

Exceptions to keeping vows

NUM 30:3–30:8 In certain cases vows made by daughters or wives could be nullified by fathers or husbands respectively. See also NUM 30:10–30:15

Vows made to God in the context of worship

To offer sacrifices

LEV 22:17–22:19 See also LEV 7:16, LEV 22:21, LEV 27:9; NUM 15:2–15:4, NUM 15:8–15:10; DEU 12:6, DEU 12:11; PSA 50:14, PSA 66:13; PRO 7:14; JON 2:9

To dedicate people, animals or property to God

LEV 27:1–27:25

To give money

2KI 12:4–12:5 See also DEU 23:18

To elicit God's help

1SA 1:11 See also GEN 28:20–28:22; NUM 21:2; JDG 11:30–11:40; 2SA 15:7–15:8; PSA 66:13–66:14

To express thanksgiving

PSA 116:12–116:14 See also PSA 50:14, PSA 56:12, PSA 116:17–116:18; JON 1:16, JON 2:9

To praise God

PSA 22:25 See also PSA 61:8, PSA 65:1

Vows of Nazirites

NUM 6:1–6:21; ; JDG 13:2–13:5 Samson was set apart as a Nazirite from birth; ; 1SA 1:11 Samuel may have been a Nazirite.

By David

PSA 132:2–132:5

By Paul

ACT 18:18 See also ACT 21:24–21:26

MAT 15:5–15:6 parallel MRK 7:11–7:13

Vows made to idols

title: 5742: wedding
content:
The public acknowledgment and celebration of a couple's marriage. The wedding followed betrothal and was a preliminary to sexual union. The occasion was marked by feasting, singing and rejoicing. The bride wore a wedding dress, jewellery and ornaments and both she and the groom were waited on by attendants.

Wedding garments

The bride's wedding dress

PSA 45:13 See also GEN 24:65; EZK 16:10; REV 19:7–19:8, REV 21:2

The bride's jewellery and ornaments

ISA 49:18 See also ISA 61:10; JER 2:32; EZK 16:11–16:12

Wedding festivities

Weddings were occasions for rejoicing

JER 33:11 GEN 29:27–29:28; ; JDG 14:12; SNG 3:11; ; ISA 62:5; ; JER 7:34

Wedding songs

PSA 45:0, PSA 78:63

The wedding banquet

JDG 14:10 See also GEN 29:21–29:22 A feast celebrates Jacob's wedding; MAT 22:2 a wedding banquet given by a king for his son; JHN 2:3–2:10 Jesus Christ changes water into wine at a wedding feast; REV 19:9 the marriage supper of the Lamb

Guests and attendants at weddings

Wedding guests

JHN 2:1–2:2 See also MAT 22:3–22:10, MAT 22:11–22:12 Wedding guests were expected to wear appropriate clothes; LUK 14:8–14:10

JHN 3:29 See also JDG 14:11, JDG 14:20; MAT 9:15 parallels MRK 2:19, LUK 5:34

Bridesmaids

PSA 45:14 See also MAT 25:1–25:10

Wedding gifts

1KI 9:16 See also GEN 24:59, GEN 29:24, GEN 29:29; JDG 1:14–1:15

Covering the bride

Sometimes the groom would cover the bride with his cloak as a symbol of protection: RUT 3:9; ; EZK 16:8

A covenanted commitment

PRO 2:17; ; MAL 2:14

Blessing the couple

GEN 24:60; ; RUT 4:11

Consummating the marriage

JOL 2:16 See also GEN 29:23; PSA 19:5

title: 5743: widows
content:
God's tender concern for bereaved wives is declared throughout the whole of Scripture. He defends their rights and expects his people to do the same.

God is the protector of widows

PSA 68:5 See also DEU 10:18; PSA 146:9; PRO 15:25; JER 49:11

Jesus Christ's concern for widows

MRK 12:41–12:44 parallel LUK 21:1–21:4; ; LUK 7:11–7:15, LUK 18:1–18:5

Widows are to be treated justly

DEU 27:19 See also EXO 22:22–22:24; JOB 24:21–24:22; PSA 94:6; ISA 10:1–10:4; JER 22:3–22:5; EZK 22:25

Widows are not to be exploited

EXO 22:22 See also ISA 10:1–10:2; EZK 22:7; MAL 3:5; MRK 12:38–12:40 parallel LUK 20:45–20:47

The Christian community are to care for widows

1TI 5:3 See also 1TI 5:4–5:16; 1CO 7:8–7:9; JAS 1:27

DEU 16:14; ; RUT 1:16–1:17; ; 1KI 17:13–17:14; ; JOB 24:3, JOB 29:13; ; LUK 2:36–2:38 Anna; ; LUK 4:25–4:26, LUK 7:11–7:17 the widow of Nain; ; ACT 6:1, ACT 9:36–9:41 Dorcas

Laws governing the remarriage of widows

LEV 21:13–21:14 See also EZK 44:22

LAM 1:1 A lament for desolate Jerusalem. See also ISA 54:4–54:5 a prophecy of the restoration of Jerusalem; REV 18:7 the boasts of Babylon

title: 5744: wife
content:
The female partner in a marriage relationship. The origin of this God-ordained institution is traced back in the Bible to the Garden of Eden. Scripture stresses that marriage is a God-ordained institution, within which the husband should love and care for his wife, just as the wife should obey, honour and care for her husband. A good wife is portrayed as a great blessing, but a bad wife influences her husband for evil. In the OT, Israel is sometimes portrayed as God's wife; in the NT, the church is described as Christ's bride.

God's pattern for marriage

Husband and wife are one flesh

GEN 1:27 See also GEN 2:23–2:24; MAL 2:15; MAT 19:4–19:6 parallel MRK 10:6–10:9

The wife as helper and companion

GEN 2:18 See also GEN 2:20–2:22

The husband is head of the wife

EPH 5:23 See also 1CO 11:3

The wife is the weaker partner

1PE 3:7 See also GEN 3:16

The Israelites were forbidden to take foreign wives

DEU 7:3–7:4 See also EXO 34:16; JOS 23:12–23:13

To submit to and respect her husband

COL 3:18 See also EPH 5:22–5:24, EPH 5:33; 1PE 3:1–3:6

To care for her husband and household

PRO 31:10–31:31 See also TIT 2:4–2:5

To be faithful to her husband

EXO 20:14 parallel DEU 5:18 See also NUM 5:11–5:31; PRO 23:27; MAT 14:3–14:4 parallel MRK 6:17–6:18; MRK 10:12; LUK 3:19

REV 21:2 See also EPH 5:25–5:27; REV 19:7

title: 5745: women
content:
God created both women and men in his image and likeness. Scripture shows women in a variety of roles, playing an important part in God's salvation plan. In Christ, there is no fundamental distinction between believers on account of gender, race or social status. Women played a significant part in the life of Jesus Christ and in the early church. The NT both records their role and faces the questions thereby raised.

The creation of women

GEN 2:20–2:24 See also GEN 1:27, GEN 5:1–5:2; 1TI 2:13

Women and the fall

1TI 2:14 See also GEN 3:1–3:16; 2CO 11:3

Examples of godly women

RUT 1:16–1:17 Ruth; ; 1SA 1:9–1:28 Hannah; ; 1SA 25:2–25:35 Abigail; ; EST 4:15–4:16 Esther; ; LUK 1:41–1:45 Elizabeth; ; ACT 9:36–9:42 Tabitha

Examples of women who are condemned or judged

2SA 6:16–6:23 Michal; ; 1KI 21:1–21:25 Jezebel; ; PRO 5:1–5:6 the adulteress; ISA 3:16–4:1; ; EZK 13:17–13:23

OT laws concerning women

EXO 21:22–21:25; ; LEV 12:1–12:8, LEV 15:19–15:30; ; DEU 22:5

As a judge or leader

JDG 4:4–4:5

As a prophetess

EXO 15:20–15:21 See also JDG 4:4; 2KI 22:14–22:20; ISA 8:3

As a queen

2KI 11:1–11:3 See also 1KI 10:1–10:13 parallel 2CH 9:1–9:12; EST 1:9–1:21, EST 2:17

Women as wives and mothers in the OT

PRO 12:4 See also GEN 2:24, GEN 21:11–21:12; PRO 18:22, PRO 31:10–31:31

Women in the life of Jesus Christ

In the birth narratives

LUK 1:26–1:56, LUK 2:16–2:19, LUK 2:36–2:38

In the ministry of Jesus Christ

LUK 8:1–8:3 Jesus Christ respected women and talked to them as individuals with spiritual understanding. This was a considerable deviation from the cultural conventions of the time. See also MAT 9:20–9:22 parallels MRK 5:25–5:34, LUK 8:43–8:48; MAT 15:21–15:28 parallel MRK 7:24–7:30; MRK 12:41–12:44 parallel LUK 21:1–21:4; LUK 10:38–10:42; JHN 4:7–4:30, JHN 11:17–11:44

In the passion narratives

MAT 27:55–27:56 parallels MRK 15:40–15:41, LUK 23:49 See also MAT 26:6–26:13 parallels MRK 14:3–14:9, LUK 7:37–7:38, JHN 12:1–12:8; MAT 27:61 parallels MRK 15:47, LUK 23:55–23:56; MAT 28:1–28:10 parallels MRK 16:1–16:11, LUK 24:1–24:11

COL 4:15 See also ACT 16:15; 1CO 16:19

As workers in the church

ROM 16:12 See also ROM 16:6; PHP 4:2–4:3

ROM 16:7 Interpreters disagree over whether Junias was a man or a woman, and also over whether Paul meant these two were notable in the ranks of the apostles or were well-known to the apostles.

Instructions to women in the early church community

JDG 4:4 Deborah; ; 2KI 22:14–22:20 Huldah; ; PRO 31:10–31:31 the wife of noble character; ; SNG 3:1–3:5 the beloved; ; ACT 16:13–16:15 Lydia

title: 5746: youth
content:
Scripture characterises youth as a time of vigour and strength. It speaks, too, of the pressures and expectations of youth, warns about the temptations facing young people, and instructs the young about what is expected of them.

The vigour of youth

PRO 20:29 See also JOB 33:25; PSA 103:5, PSA 144:12; SNG 2:3; ECC 11:9–11:10ISA 40:30 Even youthful strength and vigour may fail. See also JOB 20:11; PSA 78:31; AMO 8:13

The duties of youth

To remember God

ECC 12:1 See also 1KI 18:12; PSA 71:5; LAM 3:25–3:27PSA 119:9 See also PSA 71:17; EZK 4:14

To respect the elderly

LEV 19:32 See also JOB 29:8, JOB 32:6; 1TI 5:1; 1PE 5:5

To honour parents

EXO 20:12 parallel DEU 5:16 See also EPH 6:2–6:3; LEV 19:3; 1TI 5:4

To obey parents

PRO 1:8 See also PRO 6:20, PRO 23:22; EPH 6:1; COL 3:20

To remain faithful to one's partner

PRO 5:18 See also PRO 2:17; MAL 2:14–2:15

Godly young men

1SA 2:18 Samuel; ; 1SA 17:33 David, fighting Goliath; ; 2CH 24:1–24:2 parallel 2KI 12:1–12:2 Joash became king at the age of seven; ; 2CH 34:1–34:2 parallel 2KI 22:1–22:2 Josiah became king at the age of eight; ; LUK 2:42–2:52 Jesus Christ at the age of twelve; ; 2TI 1:5 Timothy

JDG 11:36 Jephthah's daughter; ; RUT 1:16–1:17 Ruth; ; EST 4:15–4:16 Esther; ; LUK 1:38 the virgin Mary; ; ACT 21:9 Philip's daughters

The promise of youth

Israel's youthful devotion

JER 2:2 See also JER 3:4; EZK 16:22, EZK 16:43HOS 2:14–2:15 See also ISA 54:4, ISA 62:5; EZK 16:60

Dying young as a sign of judgment

PSA 89:45 See also JOB 36:14; PSA 78:63; ISA 13:12; JER 9:21 The death of children and young people symbolises loss of hope for the future; JER 11:22

Particular pressures of youth

The inexperience of youth

1KI 3:7; ; 1CH 22:5, 1CH 29:1; ; 2CH 13:7; ; JER 1:6; ; 1TI 4:12

Temptations facing the young

2TI 2:22 See also PRO 7:7; LUK 15:13, LUK 15:30; MAT 19:22 parallels MRK 10:22, LUK 18:23; TIT 2:6

Troubles faced from the time of one's youth

Disrespect for older people

2KI 2:23–2:24; ; JOB 30:1; ; ISA 3:5; ; LAM 5:12

Dishonouring parents

DEU 21:18–21:20; ; PRO 15:20, PRO 30:11; ; 2TI 3:2

The sinfulness of Israel's youth

content:

content:
A person's actions or way of life. Good behaviour will not earn salvation, but believers must practise good behaviour in accordance with Scripture as evidence of their conversion. Scripture stresses that bad behaviour is inconsistent with Christian faith and urges believers to mend their ways.

title: 5785: ambition
content: A powerful personal drive towards achieving goals which are regarded as being of importance to the individual. Ambition is viewed negatively when these goals are selflish or evil, and positively when they are directed towards building up the church or furthering the kingdom of God.

title: 5786: ambition, negative aspects of
content:
In its negative sense, ambition is the pursuit of personal status and fortune, which is contrary to the purposes of God as expressed in Scripture.

Selfish ambition: a desire for personal aggrandisement

MRK 10:36–10:37 See also GEN 11:4 the men of Babel; 2SA 15:1–15:4 Absalom; 1KI 1:5 Adonijah; ISA 14:13–14:14 the king of Babylon; EZK 28:2 the ruler of Tyre; DAN 11:36–11:38; MIC 7:3; HAB 2:4–2:5; MAT 20:21; LUK 22:24; PHP 1:17; 2TH 2:4–2:7 the antichrist

The results of selfish ambition

Humiliation by God

MAT 23:12

The believer becomes spiritually unproductive

See also MRK 4:18–4:19; JAS 3:14–3:16

Warnings against selfish ambition

title: 5789: anger
content: A state of indignation and outrage, often resulting from distress caused by injustice or insult. Scripture affirms God's righteous anger against sin and urges moderation in regard to human anger.

title: 5790: anger, divine
content:
The anger of God is directed against all human sin, disobedience, rebellion and wickedness, which threaten to thwart his purposes for his creation and people.

Causes of divine anger

Disobedience

ISA 5:24–5:25 See also NUM 22:22; JOS 7:1; 2KI 22:13; PSA 78:21–78:22; MIC 5:15; ZEC 7:12; MRK 3:5; ROM 2:5; EPH 5:5–5:6; HEB 3:7–3:12

Sinfulness

ISA 57:17 See also 1KI 8:46, 1KI 11:9; 2CH 19:2, 2CH 32:25; EPH 2:1–2:3; COL 3:5–3:6

content:

content:

title: 5793: arrogance
content:
Proud and unpleasant behaviour towards other people, based on a belief in one's own superiority or greater importance.

title: 5794: asceticism
content:
Rigorous self-denial of bodily pleasures and needs. This can be motivated either by a praiseworthy desire to dedicate oneself completely to God, or by an erroneous belief that the physical body is evil.

title: 5795: bereavement
content: The experience or status of suffering the loss through death of a close relative or friend.

content:

Abraham

GEN 23:1–23:2

Jacob

GEN 37:35 See also GEN 42:38, GEN 48:7

Joseph

GEN 50:10

David

2SA 18:33 See also 2SA 1:11–1:12, 2SA 3:32, 2SA 12:15–12:21

Job

JOB 1:20 At the news of the deaths of his sons and daughters. See also JOB 17:7

Jesus Christ

JHN 11:35 Because of the death of his friend, Lazarus.

The early Christians

ACT 8:2 See also ACT 9:39

content:

God comforts the bereaved and the sorrowful

Mourning turned into joy

title: 5798: betrayal
content:
The treacherous exposing or deceiving of people by those they formerly trusted. It is usually associated with an enemy masquerading as a friend, or with a broken or abused relationship. Betrayal was suffered by Jesus Christ and can be expected by his followers.

Betrayal is part of human experience

Examples of those experiencing betrayal

Examples of those murdered through betrayal

The power struggles of Israel's early kingship period gave rise to many bloody betrayals: 2SA 3:27, 2SA 4:6, 2SA 11:15, 2SA 13:28–13:29, 2SA 20:10; ; 1KI 21:8–21:10

An unwillingness to act in a situation of danger or opposition, because of fear. Avoiding the source of one's anxiety or fear, rather than dealing with it directly.

JHN 12:42–12:43 See also JHN 7:13, JHN 9:22–9:23 parents of the man born blind; JHN 19:38, JHN 20:19

MAT 14:5, MAT 21:26, MAT 21:46

title: 5820: criticism
content: The judgment or evaluation of others. The word often has negative associations, implying a harsh or disapproving estimate of people or their actions.

title: 5821: criticism, amongst believers
content:
Harsh criticism is out of place among believers, who are urged to see each other in the best possible light. Criticism of God arises from a failure to understand his actions and purposes.

Criticism forbidden among believers

JAS 5:9 See also MAT 7:1–7:5 parallel LUK 6:37–6:42; ROM 14:1–14:4, ROM 14:10–14:13; 1CO 10:10; GAL 5:15; PHP 2:14–2:16; JAS 4:11–4:12

Reacting to criticism

Some criticism can be disregarded

ECC 7:21–7:22 See also 1CO 4:2–4:5; COL 2:16–2:18

Criticism can be dealt with by settling the dispute

MAT 18:15 See also PRO 15:1

Integrity is a defence against criticism

DAN 6:4 See also 2CO 8:20–8:21; TIT 2:7–2:8

Criticism can be constructive

PSA 141:5 See also PRO 10:17, PRO 15:5, PRO 27:6, PRO 27:9, PRO 28:23

content: Behaviour in which pain or suffering is deliberately inflicted on others, especially the weak and defenceless.

content:
Scripture condemns cruelty, and gives examples of situations in which it was practised.

Cruelty is an expression of wickedness

PSA 71:4; ROM 1:28–1:31 See also PSA 35:16, PSA 86:14; PRO 17:5; ECC 4:1; AMO 5:12

The cruel nature of war

content:
An expression of contempt or malediction for someone. To be cursed is to suffer various kinds of misfortune, sometimes to the extent of being cut off from one's family or community, or of suffering death itself.

Divine curses came into effect after the fall

GEN 3:14–3:19 See also GEN 5:29, GEN 8:21 This curse refers to the flood; the curse of Ge 3:17 is not revoked here.

content:
A deep sense of despondency, discouragement and sadness, often linked with a sense of personal powerlessness and a loss of meaning in and enthusiasm for life. Many biblical characters show evidence of such behaviour which originates in a number of different ways.

Some causes of depression

External circumstances

2CO 1:8 See also 1KI 19:3–19:4; JOB 9:23; PSA 42:1–42:11, PSA 88:1–88:18; JOL 1:11

Physical illness or exhaustion

1KI 19:5–19:8 See also GEN 21:15–21:16; PSA 6:1–6:7, PSA 22:14–22:17, PSA 31:9–31:12; ISA 38:1–38:2; JON 1:5

Fear of others

1KI 19:1–19:3

Serious sin

content:

content:

title: 5848: exaggeration
content:
An overstatement of something, usually relating to its importance or value. People exaggerate because of fear, envy, pride or self-pity. Exaggeration can also be used positively to good effect, for example, in the teaching of Jesus Christ.

Exaggeration of difficulties through fear

NUM 13:32–13:33 See also DEU 1:28, DEU 9:1

Exaggeration of the lifestyle of others through envy

title: 5849: exaltation
content:
The lifting up or raising on high of a person, in words or actions. The exaltation of Jesus Christ, first on the cross and then in his resurrection, provides a model of how God exalts the humble and obedient. God also humbles those who exalt themselves. Believers are called upon to exalt God in their praise of him.

True exaltation comes from God

PSA 75:6–75:7 See also GEN 39:1–39:6; 1SA 2:1–2:10; 2SA 7:18–7:29

God exalts those who are humble

JAS 4:10 See also MAT 5:3–5:5; LUK 1:46–1:55; 1PE 5:5–5:6; PRO 3:34

God's exaltation of Joshua

JOS 3:7

God's exaltation of David

The Israelites in idolatry

NUM 11:32

AMO 6:4–6:6

content:

By Moses: EXO 3:11, EXO 4:10; JDG 6:15 by Gideon; PRO 22:13, PRO 26:13; JER 1:6 by Jeremiah; MAT 25:14–25:30; ; LUK 19:12–19:27; MAT 25:41–25:45 by the ignorant

title: 5852: experience
content: The direct personal knowledge of people and situations which comes from a firsthand encounter with life. To experience God is to encounter and know him directly, rather than merely to know facts about him.

title: 5854: experience, of God
content:
Scripture stresses the importance and also the possibility of a true experience of the living God. This is contrasted with the more academic knowledge about him. Experiential knowledge of God comes through personal encounter, through the witness of the Holy Spirit, through reflection on his past goodness and through the shared experiences of others.

title: 5856: extravagance
content:
Exaggerated, excessive or immoderate behaviour often linked with wastefulness which may result in personal harm. God's people are called to be wise stewards of what has been entrusted to them. However, Scripture also points to a right kind of open-handedness and generosity of spirit which reflects love and worship towards God and concern for others.

Examples of sinful extravagance

content:
The reputation gained by individuals or groups of people as a result of their achievements. Scripture shows how God's fame among the nations rested upon his saving actions and, in the NT, how the miracles of Jesus Christ brought him widespread fame. God's people are to rejoice in his fame, without lapsing into arrogance.

content: Looking kindly upon someone or treating someone with special regard. Scripture stresses the kindness and graciousness of God and Jesus Christ, which is not the result of human merit or achievement.

title: 5875: hatred
content:
Hatred for others or God is associated with human sin. Scripture also emphasises God's hatred of sin and evil. Believers are commanded to love those who hate them.

title: 5877: hesitation
content:
A delay in reaching a decision, or a reluctance to reach a decision, on account of uncertainty, caution or rebellion. Scripture provides examples of individuals who hesitate in the face of divine commands or promises, and indicates its dangers.

Examples of people who hesitated

Lot

GEN 19:16

Lot's wife

GEN 19:26 See also GEN 19:17; LUK 17:32

Moses

EXO 3:11, EXO 3:13, EXO 4:1, EXO 4:10, EXO 4:13, EXO 6:12

Peter in obeying the Lord

ACT 11:12 See also ACT 10:14–10:20

Other examples

Israel on approaching the promised land: NUM 13:31–13:33, NUM 14:1–14:4; JDG 6:36–6:40 Gideon; ; 1KI 18:21 Israel in the time of Elijah; ; JER 1:6 Jeremiah

Examples of people who did not hesitate

Caleb

NUM 13:30

Simon and Andrew

Paul

ACT 20:27 See also ACT 20:20

They should not hesitate to speak

ISA 58:1

Jesus Christ commands immediate obedience

LUK 9:62 See also LUK 9:57–9:60 parallel MAT 8:19–8:22

God does not hesitate

To bring judgment

EZK 24:14 See also EZK 12:25; DAN 9:14

The delay in Jesus Christ's return is not due to hesitation

2PE 3:9

title: 5878: honour
content:
Great respect; the creation is called upon to respect and revere God as its Creator. Since human beings are made in the image of God, they should respect one another.

The creation honours its Creator

All creatures honour God

ISA 43:20 See also REV 5:13

The people of God honour God

EXO 12:40–12:42; PSA 22:23 See also PSA 50:14–50:15; ISA 25:1–25:3; JER 3:17, JER 33:7–33:9; 2TH 3:1

How God wishes to be honoured

Honouring God by worshipping him

REV 5:11–5:12 See also PSA 50:23; REV 4:9–4:11

Honouring God by obeying him

EZK 33:31 These people honoured God with their words only, but this was not true honour for they failed to obey his commands. See also NUM 25:10–25:13; ISA 29:13

Honouring God with one's body

1CO 6:19–6:20 See also ROM 12:1; 2CO 4:10–4:11

Honouring God with one's possessions

PRO 3:9 See also ISA 60:9; 2CO 8:19

Honouring God by caring for others

PRO 14:31 See also MAT 25:31–25:40; JAS 1:27

The consequences of not honouring God

MAL 2:2 See also NUM 20:12; DAN 5:22–5:31

Jesus Christ and honour

Honour given to Jesus Christ

HEB 2:9 See also ACT 19:17; 2PE 1:17; MAT 17:5; MRK 9:7; LUK 9:35

The relationship of honour between the Father and the Son

JHN 5:23 See also JHN 8:49–8:50

God brings honour to people

1SA 2:30 See also PSA 62:7; ZEP 3:19–3:20; JHN 12:26; ROM 2:9–2:11

Honouring others as a duty to God

Honouring one's parents

EXO 20:12; EPH 6:2–6:3 See also MAL 1:6; MAT 15:1–15:6; LUK 18:20

Honouring fellow believers

ROM 12:10 See also PHP 2:29; 1TI 5:17

title: 5879: humiliation
content:
The act of being put to shame, often in a public manner. Jesus Christ was humiliated through his suffering, degradation and execution. Believers may expect to suffer humiliation on account of their faith.

Examples of humiliation

David's men at the hands of Hanun

2SA 10:4–10:5 parallel 1CH 19:4–19:5

Michal, by David's dancing

2SA 6:14, 2SA 6:20–6:22

Joab and his men, by David's seemingly inappropriate mourning

2SA 19:5–19:6

Haman, by his death on the gallows prepared for Mordecai

EST 6:11–6:12, EST 7:10

Job

JOB 19:5

Peter, by his denial of Jesus Christ

MAT 26:69–26:75 parallels MRK 14:66–14:72, LUK 22:55–22:62, JHN 18:16–18:18, JHN 18:25–18:27

Warnings against presumption

PRO 25:7; ; LUK 14:7–14:11; ; 1CO 10:12

OBA 1:8–1:10 See also 2KI 19:28; EZR 9:7; PSA 35:26; ISA 13:11, ISA 22:19, ISA 25:11, ISA 26:5; JER 15:9, JER 23:40, JER 31:19, JER 49:16; EZK 28:8; MAL 2:9

Jesus Christ suffered humiliation

Jesus Christ's humiliation in his incarnation

Jesus Christ's humilation in his humble birth

LUK 2:7

Jesus Christ's humiliation through the words of others

MAT 9:34, MAT 11:19 parallel LUK 7:34; ; MRK 3:21; ; JHN 7:20, JHN 9:16

Jesus Christ's humiliation through the actions of others

LUK 4:28–4:29, LUK 7:44–7:46

Jesus Christ's humiliation at his trials

MRK 14:55–14:65; MAT 27:27–27:31 See also MAT 26:59–26:68 parallel JHN 18:19–18:24; MAT 27:26 parallels MRK 15:15, LUK 23:25, JHN 19:16, MRK 15:16–15:20, JHN 19:1–19:3; LUK 23:9–23:11

Jesus Christ's humiliation at his crucifixion

LUK 23:33–23:43 See also GAL 3:13; DEU 21:23; LUK 22:37; ISA 53:12; MAT 27:33–27:44 parallels MRK 15:22–15:32, JHN 19:17–19:24

Believers should be prepared to suffer humiliation from unbelievers

2TI 3:12 See also MAT 5:11, MAT 10:17–10:18; JHN 15:20, JHN 16:2; PHP 1:28–1:30; 1TH 1:6; HEB 10:33–10:34; 1PE 2:19–2:21; REV 2:10

JAS 2:2–2:4 See also MAT 5:22, MAT 7:4–7:5; 1CO 11:20–11:22

title: 5881: immaturity
content:
The result of insufficient growth, or a failure to develop to one's full potential.

Pride

2SA 15:1–15:4

Rejection of wise counsel

DEU 21:18; ; 1KI 12:8

Tactlessness

1KI 12:13–12:14

Lack of respect

2KI 2:23; ; JOB 19:18

Weakness of character

2CH 13:7

Foolishness

PRO 22:15

Lack of understanding

DEU 1:39; ; PRO 1:4; ; JON 4:11; ; 1CO 13:11

Lack of self-control

TIT 2:6

Disgrace

PRO 29:15

Waste

LUK 15:13

1CO 14:20; HEB 6:1 See also 2CO 13:9, 2CO 13:11 The word “perfection” may be understood in terms of maturity; EPH 4:13, EPH 4:15; COL 1:28, COL 4:12; JAS 1:4; 2PE 3:18

Discipline

title: 5882: impartiality
content:
The ability to be unbiased towards any one race, class or person. This attitude is demonstrated by God and is to be emulated by the human race.

God is impartial

DEU 10:17 See also 2CH 19:7

God treats people impartially

MAT 5:45 See also JOB 25:3, JOB 34:19; PRO 22:2; ROM 2:11; EPH 6:9

God judges impartially

COL 3:25 See also JOB 34:11–34:12; PSA 62:12; JER 17:10; ROM 2:9–2:11; 2CO 5:10; 1PE 1:17; REV 22:12

God does not distinguish between people on the basis of external appearance

1SA 16:7 See also PSA 147:10–147:11; JER 9:25; LUK 16:15; GAL 2:6; REV 2:23

God does not discriminate against different races or classes

ACT 10:34–10:35; GAL 3:28 See also DEU 10:18; JOB 34:19; ACT 10:28, ACT 15:7–15:9

The impartiality of Jesus Christ

Jesus Christ's teaching was impartial

LUK 20:21 parallels MAT 22:16, MRK 12:14 See also MAT 20:1–20:16 a parable of Jesus Christ about divine impartiality

Jesus Christ showed impartiality in his dealings with people

JHN 4:9 Jesus Christ contravened accepted boundaries of partiality in this encounter. See also MAT 9:10–9:12 parallels MRK 2:15–2:17, LUK 5:29–5:31; MAT 15:22–15:28 parallel MRK 7:26–7:29; MAT 20:20–20:23 parallel MRK 10:35–10:40

Impartiality commended

JAS 2:1 See also PRO 28:21; 1CO 3:3–3:4, 1CO 4:6–4:7; 1TI 5:21; JAS 2:9

Humanity should judge impartially

PRO 24:23–24:25 See also EXO 18:16; DEU 1:17, DEU 16:19, DEU 24:17; PRO 17:15, PRO 18:5; MAL 2:9

Impartiality to foreigners

EXO 22:21 See also EXO 23:9; LEV 19:33–19:34; NUM 15:15–15:16; ROM 10:12

Impartiality to children

DEU 21:15–21:17

Impartiality to the poor

EXO 23:6 See also EXO 23:3; LEV 19:15; PRO 29:7; JAS 2:2–2:7

By not accepting bribes

EXO 23:8 See also JOB 36:18; PRO 15:27; ISA 1:23

EXO 23:2; ; MRK 15:15

GEN 25:27–25:28 Isaac and Rebekah to Jacob and Esau; ; GEN 29:30–29:32 Jacob to Leah and Rachel; ; GEN 37:3–37:4 Jacob to Joseph and his brothers; ; 1SA 1:4–1:6 Elkanah to Hannah and Peninnah

title: 5883: impatience
content:
A refusal to wait for people or developments, frequently displaying a lack of faith.

Examples of impatience

GEN 16:1–16:2 Abraham and Sarah who did not wait for God to give them the son he had promised; ; GEN 25:30 Esau's impatience cost him his birthright; ; NUM 20:9–20:11 Moses; NUM 21:4; ; PSA 106:13; ; ISA 59:7; 1SA 13:6–13:12 Saul made the offering without waiting for Samuel; ; 2SA 13:2 Amnon with his half-sister, Tamar; ; 2SA 14:29 Absalom with Joab; ; 2SA 18:14 Joab with Absalom; ; 2KI 5:11–5:12 Naaman; ; 2KI 6:33 King Joram; JOB 6:11, JOB 21:4; JOB 32:16 Elihu; ; MAT 18:29–18:30 the unforgiving debtor; ; LUK 15:2 The younger son could not wait for his inheritance; ; JHN 21:3 Peter; ; ACT 20:16 Paul; ; 1CO 11:20–11:21 the Corinthian Christians at their communal meal; ; REV 6:10–6:11 the martyrs waiting for the Lord to avenge their deaths

Warnings against impatience

PSA 37:7; PRO 19:2; GAL 6:9; JAS 1:19–1:20 See also PRO 6:18, PRO 12:16, PRO 14:29, PRO 15:18, PRO 16:32, PRO 20:3PRO 21:5, PRO 28:22 PRO 25:8 the need to exercise caution in disputesPRO 29:20; ECC 5:2 ECC 7:9, ECC 8:3; HAB 2:3

title: 5884: indecision
content:
Uncertainty, hesitation and doubt reflect a failure of the basic human ability to choose. They reveal an internal debate and lack of conviction.

Indecision arising from doubt and hesitation

JAS 1:6–1:8 See also 1KI 18:21; MAT 14:31, MAT 21:21; MRK 11:23; ROM 14:23

Examples of indecisive behaviour

EXO 3:11 See also EXO 4:13, EXO 14:10–14:15; JOS 7:10; EST 5:8; MAT 27:21–27:26 parallels MRK 15:9–15:15, LUK 23:13–23:25, JHN 18:38–18:40; MRK 16:11–16:14; JHN 20:25; ACT 24:25

Indecision may be indicative of divided loyalty

MAT 6:24 parallel LUK 16:13 See also MAT 19:22 parallels MRK 10:22, LUK 18:23

Indecision or uncertainty may be prompted by Satan

GEN 3:1 See also GEN 3:4; JHN 8:44; 2CO 11:3; REV 12:9

title: 5885: indifference
content:
A neutral attitude to God that is as dangerous as hostility. It is condemned as a rejection of God's love and of the needs of others.

Indifference towards God

No desire to seek God

ROM 3:11 See also ISA 42:20; JER 5:21; ZEP 1:6; MAT 13:15, MAT 24:12; ACT 28:27; REV 3:15–3:22

Refusal to heed God's word

JER 37:2 See also PSA 81:11; JER 6:10, JER 7:13, JER 25:3–25:7, JER 35:15; EZK 3:7; ZEC 1:4, ZEC 7:11–7:13

Refusal to respond to God's discipline

JER 5:3 See also JER 2:30, JER 7:27–7:28, JER 17:23, JER 32:33

Ignoring God is rebellion against him

EZK 12:2 See also JER 2:19, JER 7:26, JER 36:24; EZK 20:8

People ignore God and his warnings at their peril

JER 12:11 See also EXO 9:21, EXO 9:25; 2CH 33:10–33:11; NEH 9:30; PRO 1:24–1:27, PRO 13:18; JER 11:8, JER 36:31, JER 44:5–44:6; MAT 22:5–22:7

For those who ignore God's salvation, there is no hope

HEB 2:3 See also JER 7:24; MAT 12:30 parallel LUK 11:23

Indifference to God's declared intentions

EZK 22:30 See also NUM 32:6–32:7; JDG 5:15–5:17, JDG 5:23; 2CH 24:5; PSA 22:11; ISA 64:7; JER 48:10

Indifference of religious leaders condemned

EZK 34:2–34:4; ; ZEC 11:16–11:17; ; JHN 10:12–10:13

Indifference towards the needs of others

Indifference arises from sin

PRO 29:7 See also JOB 21:21; ISA 32:6; JAS 2:15–2:16, JAS 5:1–5:6

Examples of indifference towards others

GEN 40:23 towards Joseph; ; 1SA 25:10–25:11 towards David; MAT 26:40 parallels MRK 14:37, LUK 22:45; 2TI 4:10, 2TI 4:16

Jesus Christ condemns indifference

MAT 25:41–25:45 See also LUK 10:30–10:32, LUK 16:19–16:21

Jesus Christ's apparent indifference

MRK 4:38 parallels MAT 8:24–8:25, LUK 8:23–8:24 Jesus Christ sometimes delayed responding to cries for help in order to draw out faith. See also MAT 15:26 parallel MRK 7:27; LUK 10:40; JHN 11:6

title: 5886: individualism
content:
The recognition of individuality, of the differences between particular people, and of their special gifts, needs and character. In a negative sense, the term can mean placing the needs of individuals above those of the church as a whole, which is contrary to the biblical emphasis on all believers sharing in the common ministry of the body of Christ.

Individualism stresses the differences between people

Recognising people's special gifts

1CO 12:4–12:6 See also ROM 12:6–12:8; 1CO 12:8–12:11, 1CO 12:28–12:30; EPH 4:11; HEB 2:4; 1PE 4:10

Recognising people's abilities and opportunities

MAT 25:14–25:15 See also LUK 19:12–19:13; 1CO 4:7

Individualism and the church

Recognising the parts people play in the church, the body of Christ

1CO 12:12 See also ROM 12:4–12:5; 1CO 12:14, 1CO 12:17–12:20, 1CO 12:27

Individualism must not emphasise the individual at the expense of the church as a whole

1CO 12:21–12:26 See also ROM 12:3, ROM 12:10, ROM 12:16; PHP 2:3

Contrary to self-seeking individualism, believers should share in the common ministry of the body of Christ

ACT 2:42 See also ACT 2:44, ACT 4:34–4:35; 2CO 8:13–8:14, 2CO 9:13; HEB 13:16

title: 5887: inexperience
content:
Lack of experience of life or a particular aspect of life. Inexperience is often associated with the young who are thus vulnerable and who should be taught by those older and wiser. God sometimes calls the inexperienced to leadership but usually also provides encouragement and support from more experienced leaders.

The inexperience of youth

1SA 3:4–3:7; JER 1:6 See also DEU 1:39; 1KI 3:7; 1CH 29:1; 2CH 10:8–10:11 parallel 1KI 12:8–12:11; 2CH 13:7; ISA 7:15–7:16

The inexperienced may be led astray

2KI 17:41 Children often follow in the ways of their parents; MAT 18:6 See also 1KI 22:53; 2KI 24:9; MRK 9:42; LUK 17:2

God's call to the inexperienced

JER 1:7–1:8 See also 1SA 16:11–16:13 David, Jesse's youngest son, is chosen by God; 1SA 17:33 David's inexperience in the face of Goliath; 1TI 4:12 Timothy was called to pastor a church despite his youth. In general, however, church leaders should be people of experience (see 1Ti 3:6).

Support for the inexperienced

Teaching the inexperienced

DEU 4:9–4:10; JOB 8:8–8:9 Each generation learns from the wisdom and experience of those going before. See also DEU 11:2–11:7, DEU 31:13; JOB 32:6–32:7; PSA 71:18, PSA 78:3–78:5; PRO 5:1–5:2; EPH 6:4

Examples of help given to the inexperienced

1CH 22:5 See also DEU 1:38 Moses is to encourage his young successor, Joshua; JDG 3:1–3:2 teaching warfare to those who have no experience of it; 1SA 3:8–3:10 Eli instructs the inexperienced Samuel; 1KI 19:19–19:21 Elisha becomes Elijah's attendant; 1CH 28:20 David encourages Solomon to build the temple; PRO 4:3–4:4 Solomon recalls the instruction given by his father; ACT 15:39 Barnabas takes John Mark with him; 2TI 3:14–3:15 Paul reminds Timothy of the example he has been given.

title: 5888: inferiority
content:
A discouraging sense of being of less importance or value in comparison with others.

Inferiority as a depressing lack of self-worth

JDG 6:15; PSA 22:6; 1CO 2:3 See also 1SA 18:23; NEH 4:4, NEH 6:9; PSA 31:9–31:10, PSA 70:5, PSA 74:21, PSA 86:1, PSA 109:22, PSA 119:25, PSA 119:141; ECC 9:16; ISA 33:8; JER 22:28; LAM 1:11; MAL 2:9

Inferiority as a healthy sense of unworthiness

ISA 6:5; MAT 5:3; LUK 5:8 See also 2SA 12:13; JOB 42:6; PSA 38:1–38:22, PSA 51:3–51:5; REV 1:17, REV 3:17

God's judgment will bring inferiority on on proud nations

OBA 1:2 See also ISA 16:14; JER 49:15; EZK 29:15

Refusing to be intimidated by a sense of inferiority

JOB 12:3; 1TI 4:12 See also JOB 13:2; 2CO 11:5, 2CO 12:11; TIT 2:15

God values those regarded as inferior and uses them

DEU 7:7–7:8; 1CO 1:27–1:28 See also 1SA 2:8; PSA 12:5, PSA 34:6, PSA 35:10, PSA 36:7, PSA 40:17, PSA 72:13, PSA 136:23, PSA 140:12; ISA 11:4, ISA 25:4, ISA 29:19, ISA 41:14, ISA 49:7, ISA 61:1–61:3; HOS 11:1–11:4

Jesus Christ valued those traditionally regarded as inferior

MAT 8:2–8:4 the diseased and ritually unclean; ; MAT 9:10–9:13 the morally unacceptable; ; MAT 15:21–15:29 non-Jews; ; MAT 19:13–19:14 children; ; LUK 18:13 those who are ashamed of their sins; ; JHN 4:9 women

LUK 14:13; ROM 12:16 See also PSA 82:3–82:4; 1TH 5:14; HEB 12:12–12:13

title: 5889: ingratitude
content:
The absence of due thankfulness. Scripture gives examples of human ingratitude to God for all the blessings and gifts which he provides for them. It is especially important for Christians to give thanks to God.

The ingratitude of human beings to one another

Examples of ingratitude

GEN 40:23 the chief butler towards Joseph; ; NUM 16:13–16:14 Dathan and Abiram to Moses; JDG 8:35, JDG 9:18; 1SA 25:21 Nabal to David; ; 2CH 24:22 King Joash to Jehoiada; ; ECC 9:15 the citizens to the wise man who delivered a city

Returning evil for good

content:

title: 5894: intelligence
content:
The natural ability to acquire knowledge and to learn skills. It is not emphasised in Scripture because wisdom is viewed primarily in spiritual and moral terms. Human cleverness proves ultimately futile; nevertheless, believers are called to develop and use their minds to the full in God's service and to dedicate gifts and abilities to him.

Wisdom is primarily spiritual and moral

PRO 9:10 See also JOB 28:28; PSA 111:10; JAS 3:13

The spiritual and moral inadequacy of unaided human intelligence

Unaided human intelligence proves futile

PSA 94:11 See also ECC 9:11, ECC 12:12; DAN 12:4; ACT 17:21; 1CO 3:20

Human intelligence does not bring knowledge of God

1CO 1:20–1:21 See also JHN 5:39–5:40; ROM 1:22–1:23; COL 2:8

COL 2:23 See also 1CO 8:1–8:2; JAS 3:14–3:16

MRK 12:30 parallels MAT 22:37, LUK 10:27 See also 1CO 7:37 The mind is to be used in seeking to discern God's will; 1CO 14:15–14:18 The mind is to be used in worship.

content:
Close relationships are part of God's will for human life. Scripture speaks of intimate relationships between Jesus Christ and the Father, between God and his people, and between various individuals.

God as a father

JER 31:9 See also PSA 103:13; JER 31:20; HOS 11:1–11:4; ROM 8:15; 1JN 3:1

God as a husband

ISA 62:5 See also ISA 54:4–54:8; JER 3:14; HOS 2:19; EPH 5:25–5:27; REV 19:7, REV 21:2

title: 5896: irreverence
content:
A complete absence of the proper sense of awe, respect and wonder that is inspired and demanded by the character and activity of the living God. Irreverence involves disrespect for the character, deeds, words, law and ministers of God. As such, it brings judgment upon those who behave in this way.

Irreverence as the root of sin

ROM 3:10, ROM 3:18 See also PSA 36:1, PSA 10:4–10:5, PSA 55:19; ROM 1:21

Arrogance

PSA 36:1–36:2

Prosperity

content:

Remorse

title: 5902: maturity
content: The full development at the end of a process of growth, by means of which a human being reaches adulthood.

content:

title: 5909: motives, importance of
content:
God acts from the highest, purest motives and expects his people to do the same.

God's supreme motive is the honour of his name

PSA 106:8 See also EXO 9:16; PSA 23:3; ISA 43:7; EZK 36:20–36:23; EPH 1:11–1:14

God's glory is to be the highest motive of his people

1CO 10:31 See also NUM 25:7–25:13; ISA 26:8; COL 3:17; 1PE 4:11

Purity of motive is essential for acceptable worship

MAT 6:1–6:18 See also PSA 51:6, PSA 51:10, PSA 86:11; MAT 5:8

Wrong motives hinder effective prayer

JAS 4:3 See also PSA 66:18; 1JN 3:21–3:22

Motives for good moral behaviour

Wanting to please God

COL 3:22–3:25 See also EPH 6:5–6:8

Compassion for others

DEU 24:17–24:22 The experience of slavery and the exodus were to promote compassion for the poor and the alien. See also EXO 22:21–22:27; LEV 25:35–25:42, LEV 25:54–25:55

Fear of punishment for sin

HEB 13:4 See also COL 3:5–3:6; 1TH 4:3–4:6

God judges the motives of the heart

PRO 16:2 See also 1CH 28:9; PRO 20:27

title: 5910: motives, examples of
content:
Scripture reflects the wide range of motives which influence human behaviour.

Right actions can result from wrong motives

PHP 1:15–1:18 See also 1SA 18:20–18:23

Right motives do not always produce right actions

1KI 8:17–8:19 parallel 2CH 6:7–6:9 See also MAT 1:18–1:20

Examples of wrong motives

Malice and envy

GEN 37:11 See also GEN 37:18–37:28; EST 3:1–3:9; EZK 25:15–25:16, EZK 36:5; MAT 2:7–2:13

Greed

JHN 12:4–12:6 See also 2KI 5:19–5:27; TIT 1:10–1:11

Motives are sometimes misjudged

JOS 22:9–22:34 See also NUM 32:1–32:33; 2SA 10:1–10:4 parallel 1CH 19:1–19:4; 2KI 5:5–5:7

Jesus Christ's actions motivated by a desire to do God's will

JHN 8:29 See also JHN 4:34, JHN 6:38; HEB 10:5–10:7; PSA 40:6–40:8

Paul's motives

Paul rejected all base motives in ministry

1TH 2:3–2:6 See also 2CO 2:17

Paul was motivated by his knowledge of God

2CO 5:9–5:12

Paul was concerned for the spiritual growth of others

PHP 4:14–4:18 Paul's motive in rejoicing in the gift from the Philippians was the spiritual benefit which they would gain as a result of it. See also PHP 1:22–1:26; PHM 1:8–1:14

title: 5913: negotiation
content:
Negotiation between peoples

GEN 21:23; LUK 14:31–14:32 See also JOS 9:6, JOS 10:4; 1SA 11:2; 2SA 3:12–3:13; 1KI 15:19; 2KI 18:23 parallel ISA 36:8

Negotiation in the buying of land

GEN 23:8–23:9 See also RUT 4:4; 2SA 24:24; JER 32:8

Negotiation in the setting of wages

GEN 29:15 See also GEN 29:27, GEN 30:32; JDG 17:10–17:11; 1KI 5:6; MAT 20:2, MAT 26:14–26:15 parallels MRK 14:10, LUK 22:4

Negotiation for personal safety

JOS 2:12–2:13 See also JDG 15:12–15:13; 1SA 20:8, 1SA 30:15

title: 5914: optimism
content:
The ability to face the future with confidence. For believers this is possible because of their knowledge of God.

Optimism resulting from faith

Confidence in God

PSA 52:8, PSA 125:1 See also PSA 25:4–25:5, PSA 56:4, PSA 71:5, PSA 91:2; NAM 1:7

Confidence in what God can do

2CO 1:10–1:11 See also PSA 27:1–27:3; JER 17:7; MIC 7:7; HEB 13:6; 1JN 5:14

Confidence in what God will do in the future

2CO 5:5–5:8 See also ACT 24:14–24:15; GAL 5:5; PHP 1:3–1:6

Confidence founded on God's grace

ISA 12:1–12:2 See also EZR 10:2; 2CO 3:4–3:5; EPH 3:12; 2TH 2:16–2:17; 1JN 3:21–3:22

Encouragements to be optimistic

JHN 14:1; ROM 15:13 See also PSA 9:10, PSA 37:3–37:5, PSA 42:5, PSA 115:9–115:11; JHN 14:27, JHN 16:33; ROM 12:12; 1TI 6:17; HEB 4:15, HEB 10:19–10:23; 1PE 1:13; 1JN 2:28

Examples of optimism

In the OT

2CH 32:8; ; PRO 12:25, PRO 31:11

The apostle Peter

1PE 5:10

The apostle Paul

2CO 7:4 See also 1CO 1:8–1:9, 1CO 4:17; 2CO 1:7, 2CO 2:3, 2CO 8:22; PHP 2:22; COL 4:9, COL 4:12–4:13; 2TI 1:12; PHM 1:21

The apostle John

3JN 1:3–1:5

Misplaced optimism

Trusting in anyone or anything other than God

PSA 146:3 See also JDG 9:26; 1SA 15:32; JOB 6:20, JOB 8:12–8:13; PRO 11:7; JER 7:4, JER 9:4, JER 12:6, JER 49:4, JER 49:31; EZK 29:16; MIC 7:5; 2CO 9:4

Presumption

EZK 13:6 See also ISA 58:4; JER 7:9–7:10; LUK 18:9

title: 5915: ornaments
content:
The use of jewellery and other adornments is not forbidden in Scripture, but excessive use can indicate worldliness. Inner spiritual adornment is of greater value.

Possession and use of various ornaments show wealth

Ornaments used to beautify

SNG 1:10–1:11 See also GEN 37:3, GEN 37:23, GEN 37:32; 2SA 1:24; JER 2:32

Rings, ear-rings and nose rings

GEN 35:4; ; EXO 32:2–32:3; ; JDG 8:24; ; EST 8:8; ; PRO 25:12; ; ISA 3:19, ISA 3:21; ; EZK 16:12; ; LUK 15:22; ; JAS 2:2

Bracelets and gold chains

GEN 24:22, GEN 41:42; ; PRO 1:9; ; EZK 16:11; ; DAN 5:29

Bells

EXO 28:33–28:35

Ornaments plundered from Egypt

EXO 3:22

The misuse of ornaments for pride and seduction

ISA 3:16 See also EZK 23:40, EZK 23:42; HOS 2:13

Ornaments as gifts

GEN 24:53 See also GEN 24:22; JOB 42:11

Adornment as a picture of God's love

EZK 16:11–16:13 See also ISA 61:10; LUK 15:22

Ornaments as symbols of authority

GEN 41:42 See also 2SA 1:10; EST 3:10; DAN 5:29

Ornaments discarded

In mourning

EXO 33:4–33:6 See also EZK 26:16

To make idols

EXO 32:2–32:4 See also JDG 8:24–8:27

As offerings to God

EXO 35:22 See also NUM 31:50

Inner, not outer, adornment encouraged

1PE 3:3–3:4

title: 5916: pessimism
content:
A negative and hopeless attitude, resulting either from viewing the world as being without God or from loss of faith in God.

The world may appear to be meaningless

ECC 1:14 See also ECC 1:1–1:11

Wisdom may be pointless

ECC 1:17–1:18 See also ECC 2:12–2:16

Pleasures may be empty

ECC 2:1

Work may be in vain

ECC 2:17 See also ECC 2:18–2:23, ECC 4:4

The world may seem corrupt and oppressive

ECC 4:1 See also ECC 4:2–4:3, ECC 5:8–5:9

Loneliness can be depressing

ECC 4:8

Wealth is no answer

ECC 5:10 See also ECC 5:11–5:15, ECC 6:1–6:6; LUK 12:18–12:20

Life is short and often miserable

ECC 6:12 In the OT, before the resurrection hope was fully developed, this life seemed to be all that there was. See also 1CH 29:15; JOB 7:6, JOB 14:7–14:12, JOB 14:18–14:22, JOB 17:13–17:16

Suffering may lead to pessimism

JOB 6:11 See also JOB 30:26; LAM 3:16–3:18; EZK 37:11

Suffering may cause a sense of God's rejection

JOB 14:18–14:19 See also JOB 19:5–19:13

The godless have no grounds for optimism

EPH 2:12 See also JOB 8:13–8:15; PRO 10:24, PRO 11:7, PRO 24:19–24:20; ISA 19:3; JER 4:9; MAT 7:26–7:27; 1TH 4:13

Examples of pessimism

The Israelites on hearing about the strength of the Canaanites

NUM 13:31–13:33; ; DEU 1:28

Israel's enemies

DEU 2:25; ; JOS 2:9

Naomi on her return to Israel

RUT 1:21

The Israelites threatened by the Philistines

1SA 17:11, 1SA 13:6–13:7

Elijah at Mount Horeb

1KI 19:9–19:10

The men with leprosy at the gate of Samaria

2KI 7:4

Judah facing the threat from Aram and Israel

ISA 7:2

The Philistine cities on seeing Tyre's destruction

ZEC 9:5

Thomas after the resurrection

JHN 20:24–20:25

Paul's shipboard companions during the storm

ACT 27:20

The antidote to pessimism is faith in God

PSA 42:5; 2CO 4:13–4:16 See also ISA 41:10; LAM 3:21–3:24; 2CO 4:7–4:9

title: 5917: plans
content:
Designs or schemes, prepared in advance of doing something. Scripture indicates the sovereign plans of God and the varied plans of men and women.

God's plans

For judgment

JER 18:11 See also NUM 33:55–33:56; 2KI 19:25–19:26; JOB 23:14–23:16; ISA 25:1–25:2, ISA 37:26–37:27; JER 26:3; LAM 2:17; MIC 2:3ISA 14:24–14:27, ISA 19:12, ISA 19:17, ISA 23:8–23:9; JER 49:20, JER 50:45; MIC 4:11–4:13

For salvation

EPH 1:11 See also PSA 40:5; HEB 11:40

For the tabernacle and the temple

EXO 26:30–26:37 See also 1CH 28:11–28:12, 1CH 28:18–28:19; EZK 43:10–43:11

God's plans are revealed to his people

AMO 3:7 See also EXO 26:30; JER 49:20–49:21

God's plans are always fulfilled

JOB 42:2 See also PSA 33:11; ISA 5:18–5:19, ISA 14:24–14:27, ISA 46:11

God may sometimes reverse his plans

JER 36:3 See also JER 18:5–18:10, JER 26:3; JON 3:10

Plans of the wicked

PSA 64:5–64:6 See also 2SA 17:1–17:4; 2KI 16:10–16:11; PSA 140:2; PRO 14:22, PRO 30:32; ISA 30:1; JER 18:12; MIC 2:1; MAT 28:12–28:13

Plans of the righteous

PRO 12:5 See also 1CH 28:2; PSA 14:6; PRO 14:22, PRO 21:5; ISA 32:8; ROM 1:13, ROM 15:24; 2CO 1:15–1:17

Plans and the role of counsellors

PRO 15:22 See also EZR 4:4–4:5; PRO 20:18

Malicious plans

Against other people

1SA 18:25 See also 1SA 23:10; EST 8:3; PSA 140:4; JER 49:30

Against God's servants

JER 18:18 See also MAT 22:15; JHN 12:10–12:11; ACT 9:23–9:24, ACT 27:42–27:43

Human plans are subject to God's will

JAS 4:13–4:15; PSA 33:10 See also PSA 20:4, PSA 140:8, PSA 146:4; PRO 16:1–16:3, PRO 16:9, PRO 19:21, PRO 21:30; ECC 9:10; ISA 8:10, ISA 19:3; JER 19:7

title: 5918: pleasure
content:
A gratifying emotion, used in Scripture to refer to both human and divine emotions. Believers are invited to take pleasure in every aspect of God's creation, while not allowing pleasure in the creation to overshadow pleasure in the Creator himself.

Divine pleasure

That which gives God pleasure

PSA 147:11; JER 9:24 See also PSA 37:23, PSA 149:4; PRO 11:20, PRO 12:22; MAT 11:25–11:26 parallel LUK 10:21; MAT 12:18; ISA 42:1; EPH 1:5, EPH 1:9

That which does not give God pleasure

PSA 5:4; EZK 18:23 See also PSA 51:16, PSA 147:10; ISA 1:11; EZK 18:32, EZK 33:11

Human pleasure

God provides everything for the enjoyment of life

ECC 8:15; 1TI 6:17

Pleasure in human physical relationships

SNG 4:10 See also SNG 1:2, SNG 2:3, SNG 7:6

Such pleasures are not satisfying in themselves

ECC 2:10–2:11 See also ECC 2:1–2:2, ECC 2:24–2:25

True pleasure is found in the things of God

PSA 16:11, PSA 37:4; ROM 7:22 See also PSA 1:2, PSA 35:9, PSA 43:4, PSA 111:2, PSA 112:1, PSA 119:16; PRO 10:23, PRO 16:13, PRO 18:2; ISA 55:2; JER 6:10, JER 15:16

Pleasures may also be misleading or positively sinful

LUK 8:14; TIT 3:3 See also PRO 1:22, PRO 2:14; ECC 7:4; ISA 66:3; 2TH 2:12; 1TI 5:6; 2TI 3:4; HEB 11:25; JAS 4:3; 2PE 2:13–2:14

title: 5919: popularity
content:
The state of being liked and admired. Scripture notes how the faithful preaching of the gospel will lead to hostility and unpopularity, not least on account of its demands on people and its proclamation of judgment.

The popularity of Jesus Christ during his early ministry

Crowds gathered round him

MRK 2:2 See also MRK 3:10, MRK 5:24; LUK 5:1, LUK 8:19, LUK 8:45

Many people followed him

MAT 4:25, MAT 13:2, MAT 15:30; ; MRK 1:33, MRK 2:13; ; LUK 12:1

The popularity of David

1SA 18:7, 1SA 21:11, 1SA 29:5; ; 2SA 3:36

Popularity can result from seeking approval from human beings, rather than from God

JHN 12:43 See also LUK 6:26; COL 3:22

Actions carried out to gain popularity

2SA 15:1–15:6 Absalom's attempt to curry favour; ; ACT 12:1–12:3 Herod's arrest of Christians; ; ACT 24:27 Felix' imprisonment of Paul; ; ACT 25:9 Festus' prosecution of Paul

Causes of unpopularity for the gospel

Its appeal to those whom the world regards as weak and foolish

1CO 1:26–1:29, 1CO 2:6–2:7

Its insistence that people are sinful

ROM 7:7; ; 1TI 5:20; ; 1JN 1:8

Its challenge to vested interests

JHN 11:45–11:48 the Pharisees' privileged position; ; ACT 19:23–19:40 the silversmith's trade; ; ACT 5:17–5:41, ACT 21:27–21:36

The high demands that the gospel makes of people

MRK 10:17–10:23

The difficulty of some of Jesus Christ's sayings

JHN 6:60–6:66

title: 5920: pretence
content:
The deception of others by individuals, usually for the sake of their own interest, safety or pride. Scripture condemns such pretence and demands honesty from believers at every point.

Pretence practised by people for their own interests

The wearing of a disguise

1KI 14:1–14:6 See also GEN 27:5–27:19, GEN 27:35–27:36, GEN 29:16–29:25, GEN 38:13–38:16; 2SA 14:1–14:3

Other pretences

GEN 42:7 See also GEN 34:13–34:15, GEN 34:25; 2SA 13:1–13:11; 2KI 10:18–10:19; PRO 13:7; JER 9:6–9:9; MAT 22:15–22:22 parallels MRK 12:13–12:17, LUK 20:20–20:26

Pretence practised by people for their own safety

The wearing of a disguise

JOS 9:3–9:22 See also 1SA 28:7–28:12; 1KI 22:29–22:32 parallel 2CH 18:28–18:32

Other pretences

1SA 21:10–21:13 See also 1SA 19:11–19:17; PSA 34:0; ACT 27:29–27:30

Examples of pretence

That practised by people because of their pride

PRO 12:9 See also 2CH 35:20–35:22; PRO 13:7; MAT 6:2, MAT 6:5, MAT 6:16, MAT 23:27–23:28, MAT 24:4–24:5 parallels MRK 13:5–13:6, LUK 21:8

That practised by people in their approach to God

JER 3:10 See also MAT 15:7–15:8 parallel MRK 7:6; ISA 29:13

That commanded by the LORD for his own purpose

1KI 20:37–20:43

God's people must rid themselves of pretence

1PE 2:1 See also PSA 119:29; LUK 12:1; 1PE 2:21–2:22; ISA 53:9

The gospel demolishes pretence

2CO 10:5

title: 5921: privacy
content:
Privacy to conduct conversations

JER 37:17 See also 1SA 18:22; 2SA 3:27; JER 40:15

Privacy to express emotions

GEN 43:30 See also MAT 14:9–14:13

Privacy to teach and to learn

MAT 17:19 parallel MRK 9:28 See also MAT 24:3 parallel MRK 13:3; LUK 10:23; GAL 2:2

Privacy to pray

LUK 9:18 See also MAT 6:5–6:6, MAT 14:22–14:23 parallel MRK 6:45–6:46; MAT 26:36 parallels MRK 14:32, LUK 22:39–22:42; LUK 6:12

title: 5922: prudence
content:
Careful, wise discernment; the avoidance of rash behaviour or speech; the good management of talents and resources and the showing of tact and wisdom in relationships with other people.

The link between prudence and wisdom

PRO 8:12 See also PRO 1:1–1:6

Characteristics of prudence

Discernment

PRO 14:15 See also PRO 12:16, PRO 14:8; LUK 14:28–14:32

Foresight and caution

PRO 22:3 See also PRO 23:1–23:3; AMO 5:13

Wise use of knowledge

PRO 12:23 See also PRO 14:18; MAT 7:6

Wise speech

PRO 21:23 See also PSA 39:1; JAS 3:5–3:8

A teachable spirit

PRO 15:5

Prudence involves good management of talents and resources

Good management commended

PRO 6:6–6:11 See also GEN 41:33–41:40; PRO 24:27; MAT 25:14–25:30

Warnings against unwise financial dealings

PRO 22:26–22:27 See also PRO 6:1–6:5; MAT 5:25–5:26

Examples of prudent behaviour

In averting disaster

1SA 25:14–25:35 See also GEN 32:3–32:21

In avoiding persecution

ACT 14:5–14:7 See also MAT 12:14–12:16 parallel MRK 3:6–3:7 Jesus ChristACT 9:23–9:25, ACT 9:29–9:30 ACT 12:17 Peter

Prudence in dealing with other people

GEN 26:26–26:31 Abimelech makes a treaty with Isaac; ; GEN 32:3–32:21 Jacob prepares to meet Esau; ; NEH 2:1–2:6 Nehemiah petitions Artaxerxes; ; DAN 1:8–1:14 Daniel's diplomacy in avoiding Nebuchanezzar's food; ; DAN 2:10–2:16 Daniel's wisdom and tact in the face of death; ; MAT 22:15–22:22 Jesus Christ's wisdom on the question of paying taxes to Caesar; ; ACT 5:33–5:40 Gamaliel's speech to the Sanhedrin

title: 5923: public opinion
content:
The concepts and views held by the majority of the population. Scripture urges personal, independent thinking, based on God's word, rather than adherence to popular beliefs.

God's people should not be concerned about public opinion

EXO 23:2 See also JOB 31:33–31:34; ECC 7:21–7:22

Examples of the impact of public opinion

1SA 14:45 Public opinion saved Jonathan's life; ; 1SA 15:24 Public opinion led to Saul losing his kingdom; ; MAT 27:15–27:26 Public opinion led to Jesus Christ being crucified; ; ACT 12:3 Public opinion led to Peter being imprisoned.

Public opinion is often contrary to divine standards

HAG 1:2–1:11 See also NUM 13:21–14:10; DEU 1:19–1:40; 1SA 8:4–8:9; 1KI 18:21; JER 2:31–2:35, JER 26:7–26:16

Public opinion is sometimes in accord with divine standards

DEU 5:28–5:29 See also JOS 24:19–24:24

Public opinion of Jesus Christ was divided

Concerning his identity

MAT 16:13–16:17 parallels MRK 8:27–8:29, LUK 9:18–9:20 See also JHN 7:40–7:43

Concerning his teaching and ministry

LUK 12:51; ; JHN 7:12, JHN 7:43, JHN 9:16, JHN 10:19

title: 5924: quarrelsomeness
content:
The evil of quarrelling

JAS 4:1–4:2 See also EXO 21:18–21:19; PRO 10:12, PRO 13:10, PRO 15:18, PRO 20:3, PRO 21:9, PRO 22:10, PRO 26:20–26:21, PRO 27:15–27:16, PRO 30:33; 2TI 2:23

Quarrelsomeness is unfitting for God's people

1CO 3:3; 1TI 3:2–3:3 See also PRO 17:19; ISA 58:4; ROM 13:12–13:14; 2CO 12:20; 1TI 6:3–6:5; 2TI 2:14, 2TI 2:23–2:24

Examples of quarrelsomeness

1CO 1:10–1:12 See also GEN 13:7–13:8, GEN 26:20–26:22; EXO 17:1–17:7 NIV footnote at verse 7; NUM 20:1–20:13 NIV footnote at verse 13; DEU 33:8; PSA 95:8, PSA 106:32; MRK 9:33–9:34 parallel LUK 9:46; LUK 22:24; PHP 4:2–4:3

title: 5925: rashness
content:
Acting without careful consideration of the possible consequences or risks.

Examples of rashness

GEN 34:25–34:31 Jacob's sons; EXO 2:11–2:12; ; ACT 7:24–7:25; ; NUM 20:8–20:12; ; PSA 106:32; JOS 8:14–8:17 the king of Ai; ; JDG 11:30–11:31 Jephthah; ; 1SA 14:24 King Saul; ; 2SA 6:6 Uzzah; ; 2SA 12:18 fear for King David; ; 1KI 1:5 King Adonijah; ; 2KI 5:20–5:21 Gehazi; ; 2KI 10:16 Jehu; ; 2CH 26:16–26:20 King Uzziah; ; 2CH 35:21–35:22 King Josiah; ; HAB 1:6 the Babylonians; ; MAT 8:19–8:20 a would-be disciple; ; MAT 14:6–14:10 parallel MRK 6:26 King Herod; MAT 26:33–26:34; ; JHN 18:10; ACT 19:36 the Ephesian crowd; ; GAL 1:6 the Galatian Christians; ; 2TI 3:2–3:4 a characteristic of the last days

Warnings against rashness

PRO 14:16; ECC 5:2 See also PRO 6:16–6:18, PRO 12:18, PRO 13:3, PRO 19:2, PRO 20:3, PRO 20:25, PRO 21:5, PRO 25:8, PRO 29:20; ECC 7:9, ECC 8:3; ISA 52:12; ZEP 3:7; ACT 19:35–19:36; 1TI 5:22; 2TI 3:1–3:5

Antidotes to rashness

Trust in the guiding presence of the Lord

ISA 52:12

Appreciating the importance of considered actions

JAS 1:19 See also LUK 14:28–14:33

title: 5926: rebuke
content:
A verbal expression of blame. Scripture gives examples of both divine and human rebuke. Sometimes God issues rebukes directly but more commonly he did so through the OT prophets. In the NT Jesus Christ and the apostles issue rebukes and teach the church how to address those who sin.

God has an absolute right to rebuke those who depart from his ways

He sometimes exercises this right directly

LEV 26:23–26:24 See also DEU 28:20; NEH 9:30; JOB 5:17; PSA 39:11, PSA 50:21, PSA 94:12, PSA 105:14, PSA 119:21; JER 2:19, JER 2:30; HEB 8:8

His rebuke is powerful

JOB 26:11; ; PSA 80:16, PSA 104:7; ; ISA 50:2

In the OT much rebuke came indirectly

Balaam's ass rebukes Balaam: NUM 22:28; ; 2PE 2:16; 1SA 2:25 Eli rebukes his sons; ; 1SA 15:12–15:26 Samuel rebukes Saul; ; 1SA 24:5–24:7 David rebukes his men; ; 2SA 12:1–12:12 Nathan rebukes David; ; 1KI 18:18 Elijah rebukes Ahab; ; EZR 10:9–10:11 Ezra rebukes the men of Judah and Benjamin; ; ISA 1:10–1:17 Isaiah rebukes Judah and Jerusalem; ; HOS 4:1–4:3 Hosea rebukes the Israelites.

Examples of Jesus Christ issuing rebukes

To evil spirits

MAT 17:18 parallels MRK 9:25, LUK 9:42 See also LUK 4:41

To his disciples

MRK 8:33 parallel MAT 16:23; ; MRK 16:14

Other examples of rebuke being administered in the NT

Inappropriate rebukes by Jesus Christ's disciples: MAT 16:22 parallel MRK 8:32; ; MAT 19:13 parallels MRK 10:13, LUK 18:15; LUK 3:19 John the Baptist rebukes Herod; ; LUK 23:40–23:41 The repentant thief on the cross rebukes the other crucified criminal.

Proverbs on the subject of rebuke

The importance of responding correctly to a rebuke

PRO 1:23–1:26 See also PRO 6:23, PRO 10:17, PRO 12:1, PRO 15:10, PRO 15:31–15:32, PRO 17:10, PRO 19:25; ECC 7:5

Different responses to a rebuke

PRO 9:7–9:8

Instructions to believers on giving and receiving rebuke

On giving a rebuke

LEV 19:17 See also MAT 18:15; LUK 17:3; GAL 6:1; COL 1:28, COL 3:16; 1TI 5:1 advice on rebuking those who are older; 1TI 5:20 disciplining elders; 2TI 3:16 the usefulness of Scripture for rebuking; 2TI 4:2; TIT 1:9, TIT 1:13, TIT 2:15; JAS 5:19–5:20

On receiving a rebuke

HEB 12:5 See also 1CO 16:14

Believers thus follow the example of the Lord himself

HEB 12:6 See also PRO 3:12; REV 3:19

title: 5927: resentment
content: A feeling of bitterness towards someone, usually as a result of their actions or words. Resentment is possible against God or against other people.

title: 5928: resentment, against God
content:
Resentment against God or Jesus Christ is usually the consequence of a lack of faith or unbelief or as a response to adverse circumstances.

Israel's resentment against God expressed in constant grumbling

Resentment at hardships and lack of provisions

EXO 15:24, EXO 16:2–16:3, EXO 17:3; ; NUM 20:2–20:5, NUM 21:4–21:5

Resentment due to faithless fear

EXO 14:10–14:11; ; NUM 14:2–14:3, NUM 14:36; ; DEU 1:27; ; PSA 106:25

God's response to Israel's resentment

Punishment

NUM 11:1, NUM 14:27–14:30, NUM 14:37; ; PSA 106:26–106:27; ; 1CO 10:10

Merciful provision

EXO 16:4, EXO 16:8–16:9, EXO 16:11–16:12; ; NUM 17:5, NUM 17:10

Expressions of resentment

At suffering

JOB 10:1 See also JOB 3:20–3:26, JOB 7:11; 1SA 1:10; PSA 77:1–77:3, PSA 142:2; JER 15:18

At apparently unjust treatment by God

title: 5945: self-pity
content:
Sorrow or despondency aroused by one's own suffering or misfortune. It can result from personal loss or suffering, hardship in God's service or the judgment of God. Its cure is to remember the goodness of God.

Examples of self-pity as a result of personal loss or suffering

The Israelites in the wilderness

EXO 16:3 See also EXO 14:10–14:12, EXO 17:3; NUM 11:4–11:6, NUM 14:1–14:4; DEU 1:26–1:28; 1CO 10:10–10:11

Job

JOB 6:1–6:13, JOB 10:1 See also JOB 3:1–3:26, JOB 12:1–12:6, JOB 16:6–17:2, JOB 30:9–30:31

Other examples

GEN 27:34, GEN 27:38; ; 2SA 15:30; ; 2KI 20:2–20:3 parallel ISA 38:2–38:3; ; PSA 10:1, PSA 73:2–73:3, PSA 73:13–73:14, PSA 74:1

Examples of self-pity as a result of hardship in the service of God

Moses

NUM 11:11–11:15 See also EXO 5:22–5:23, EXO 17:4

Elijah

1KI 19:4 See also 1KI 19:10, 1KI 19:14

Jeremiah

JER 15:10 See also JER 15:18, JER 20:7–20:10, JER 20:14–20:18

Other examples

JER 45:3 See also JON 4:1–4:5

Examples of self-pity as a result of God's judgment

PSA 137:1–137:9; ; LAM 3:1–3:18; ; REV 18:9–18:19 The kings, merchants and sailors will be full of self-pity when they see the destruction of Babylon, because their opportunities for making wealth will be gone.

People calling upon others to pity them

JOB 19:21 See also MRK 9:22; LUK 17:13

Turning to God puts self-pity in its true perspective

PSA 43:5, PSA 73:16–73:17 See also PSA 3:1–3:4, PSA 13:1–13:6, PSA 37:1–37:7, PSA 73:23–73:28, PSA 106:7; LAM 3:19–3:26, LAM 3:31–3:33; 2CO 1:5, 2CO 6:3–6:10; JAS 1:2–1:3; 1PE 4:13

title: 5946: sensitivity
content:
Deep feelings for others and sympathy for their needs, leading to appropriate action on their behalf. Spiritual sensitivity is the ability to perceive and respond to the call of God or the spiritual demands of the moment. Oversensitivity and lack of sensitivity are extremes to be avoided.

God's sensitivity to his people

EXO 3:7 See also JDG 2:18; ISA 40:2; LAM 3:22; HOS 2:14; LUK 1:78

Sensitivity shown by Jesus Christ

MAT 12:20 See also ISA 42:3MAT 23:37 parallel LUK 13:34 See also LUK 7:12–7:13, LUK 19:41; JHN 9:34–9:35, JHN 11:33–11:35

Jesus Christ's own experience of temptation

HEB 4:14–4:15 See also HEB 2:18

Sensitivity to others

Arises from an experience of God's compassion

2CO 1:3–1:4 See also PHP 2:1

Believers urged to show sensitivity

ROM 12:15 See also ISA 40:2; EPH 4:32; COL 3:12–3:13; 1PE 3:8; HEB 13:3

Sensitivity to foreigners in Israel

EXO 23:9 parallel EXO 22:21 See also LEV 19:33–19:34

Sensitivity to those in distress

JOB 2:11–2:13 See also MAT 26:38–26:40 parallel MRK 14:34–14:37; 2CO 7:5–7:7; HEB 10:33–10:34; JAS 1:27

Sensitivity to those weak in faith

ROM 15:1 See also ROM 14:1–14:3, ROM 14:15; 1CO 8:9–8:12; 1TH 2:7

Sensitivity in speech

PRO 15:23, PRO 16:24, PRO 25:11, PRO 25:15; ; 1PE 3:15

Insensitivity to others

Examples of insensitivity to others

DEU 28:53–28:57 As a result of God's judgment, the most sensitive person will become insensitive even to the needs of family; ; 1SA 1:13–1:14 Eli's insensitivity to Hannah; ; JOB 16:2 the insensitivity of Job's “comforters”; ; JON 4:9–4:11 Jonah's insensitivity to the people of Nineveh; ; MAT 19:13 parallels MRK 10:13, LUK 18:15 the disciples' insensitivity towards children brought to Jesus Christ; ; 1CO 11:20–11:21 insensitivity to the needs of others; ; JAS 2:2–2:4 insensitivity towards poorer visitors to church

The results of insensitivity

PSA 69:20; ; PRO 25:17, PRO 25:20

Oversensitivity

Oversensitivity in the face of rejection

1SA 25:11–25:13 David's hasty reaction towards Nabal; ; LUK 9:53–9:54 James' and John's hasty reaction

Oversensitivity of conscience

ROM 14:2; ; 1CO 8:6–8:8

Spiritual sensitivity

Spiritual awareness

1SA 3:8 See also MAT 24:32–24:34 parallels MRK 13:28–13:29, LUK 21:29–21:30; ACT 16:9–16:10

Lack of spiritual sensitivity

EPH 4:18–4:19 See also PRO 23:31–23:35; ROM 1:28–1:29; 1TI 4:1–4:4ISA 42:25; JER 5:3EZK 12:2; ZEC 7:11–7:14

God hardens human hearts

EXO 7:3; ; ROM 1:24–1:25

title: 5947: shame
content:
An uncomfortable feeling of guilt and humiliation, usually arising from sin or failure.

Shame is to be avoided

PSA 25:2 See also PSA 25:20, PSA 31:1, PSA 31:17, PSA 44:15, PSA 119:31, PSA 119:80

Causes of shame

Military defeat

2KI 19:26

Natural afflictions

LUK 1:25 See also GEN 30:23; ISA 4:1, ISA 54:4 not only childlessness but widowhood

Humiliation by an enemy

PSA 69:19 See also PSA 69:6–69:7; 1SA 11:2; 2SA 10:4–10:5; ISA 3:17; MRK 12:4

Nakedness

REV 3:18 See also GEN 2:25, GEN 3:10, GEN 9:22–9:23; ISA 47:3; EZK 16:37; REV 16:15

The sin of relations or associates

PRO 14:34

Heathen gods as a source of shame

2SA 2:10 “Bosheth” means “shame”. According to 1Ch 8:33 he was originally Ish-Baal, but the name “Baal”, subsequently associated with a heathen god, was changed by later writers to “Bosheth”. See also JER 3:24, JER 11:13; HOS 9:10

Shame as a divine judgment

JER 23:40 See also PSA 44:9; JER 46:24

Shame brought upon God's enemies

PSA 6:10, PSA 31:17, PSA 35:26, PSA 70:2, PSA 71:13, PSA 109:29, PSA 129:5

Shame as guilt for sin

EZR 9:6 See also PRO 6:32; DAN 9:5–9:7; ROM 6:20–6:21

Shame may lead to repentance

1CO 6:5; ; 2CO 7:9–7:11; ; 2TH 3:14

Some people are without shame

JER 3:3, JER 6:15; ; ZEP 3:5

Jesus Christ bore shame

HEB 12:2 See also DEU 21:23; MAT 27:39–27:44; HEB 6:6

The temptation of being ashamed of Jesus Christ and the cross

MRK 8:38 parallel LUK 9:26 See also ROM 1:16; GAL 6:14

Those who trust in God will not be put to shame

PSA 25:3 See also PSA 119:5–119:6; ISA 28:16; ROM 9:33, ROM 10:11; 1PE 2:6, 1PE 4:16

title: 5948: shrewdness
content:
Astuteness or craftiness in dealings with others, especially in using one's understanding and judgment to one's own advantage. Scripture commends it when it is seen in wise words and actions directed towards a worthy goal, but condemns it when it takes the form of cunning and deceitful scheming for sinful and selfish ends.

Shrewdness as astuteness

It is encouraged in believers

MAT 10:16; LUK 16:8–16:9 Jesus Christ explains the parable of the dishonest manager (Lk 16:1–7) and urges his disciples to be shrewd in their use of worldly wealth.

Practical demonstrations of astuteness

MAT 7:24–7:25 parallel LUK 6:47–6:48 See also PRO 12:23, PRO 14:15, PRO 15:5, PRO 18:15; MAT 24:45–24:47 parallel LUK 12:42–12:44

Jesus Christ's wisdom in answering his enemies

MAT 22:18–22:22 parallels MRK 12:15–12:17, LUK 20:23–20:26 on the matter of paying taxes to Caesar; ; MAT 22:31–22:32 parallels MRK 12:26–12:27, LUK 20:37–20:38 on the question of the resurrection; ; JHN 8:7 regarding the woman caught in adultery

Further examples of astuteness

1SA 23:22–23:23 David's shrewdness in fleeing from Saul; ; 2SA 14:1–14:3 Joab's ruse to persuade David to call Absalom back from exile; ; 1KI 3:28 Solomon's wise judgment; ; 2CH 11:23 Rehoboam acts wisely to secure his kingdom; ; DAN 1:11–1:13 Daniel avoids eating royal food and wine; ; MAT 2:16 Herod is outwitted by the Magi; ; MRK 7:27–7:29 parallel MAT 15:26–15:28 the Syro-Phoenician woman's wise response

Shrewdness as crafty and deceitful scheming

It demonstrates human sinfulness

PSA 64:6 See also JOB 15:5; PSA 83:3, PSA 140:1–140:3; PRO 7:10; ACT 13:10; EPH 4:14

It is condemned by God

2SA 22:26–22:27 parallel PSA 18:25–18:26 God is shrewd in dealing with those who cleverly deceive others; JOB 5:12–5:13 See also PSA 94:11; PRO 6:12–6:15, PRO 12:2; ISA 5:21, ISA 44:24–44:25; 1CO 1:19; ISA 29:14; 1CO 3:19–3:20

Others dislike it

PRO 14:17, PRO 25:23

It is a characteristic of Satan

2CO 11:3 See also GEN 3:1; 2CO 2:11, 2CO 11:13–11:15

The craftiness of Jesus Christ's enemies

MAT 22:15–22:17 parallels MRK 12:13–12:15, LUK 20:20–20:22 The Pharisees try to trap Jesus Christ over paying taxes; ; MAT 26:3–26:4 parallels MRK 14:1–14:2, LUK 22:1–22:2 The religious leaders plot Jesus Christ's death.

Further examples of crafty scheming

GEN 25:31–25:33 Jacob buys Esau's birthright; ; GEN 27:15–27:16 Isaac is tricked into blessing Jacob; ; EXO 1:10 Pharaoh plans to reduce the number of Israelites; ; JOS 9:3–9:6 The Gibeonites deceive Joshua; ; 2SA 13:3 Jonadab plots for Amnon against Tamar; ; NEH 6:2–6:13 schemes against Nehemiah; ; 2CO 12:16 Paul sarcastically echoes the slander against him that he tricked people into giving him money.

title: 5949: shyness
content:
Moses was shy of public speaking

EXO 4:10–4:15, EXO 6:12, EXO 6:30

Shyness caused by youth and inexperience

Jeremiah

JER 1:6

Timothy

1CO 16:10–16:11; ; 1TI 4:12; ; 2TI 1:7
