MRK 5:25–5:28, MRK 5:33

Jesus Christ taught his disciples not to be shy of bearing witness to him

MAT 5:14–5:16

title: 5950: silence
content:
A stillness or absence of noise, often associated with the absence of life or people, but also associated with a sense of expectancy or reverence, especially in the presence of God. Scripture stresses that God is not silent, but has spoken his word to his creation. The silence of Jesus Christ before his accusers is seen as the fulfilment of OT prophecy.

The silence of God

His apparent silence in the face of sin

PSA 50:21 See also JOB 34:29; ISA 42:14, ISA 57:11

God will not remain silent in the face of sin

PSA 50:3 See also ISA 62:1, ISA 65:6–65:7

Prayers that God will not be silent

PSA 28:1 See also PSA 35:22, PSA 39:12, PSA 83:1, PSA 109:1; ISA 64:12; HAB 1:13

God silences those who oppose him

1SA 2:9 See also PSA 8:2, PSA 63:11, PSA 107:42; ISA 25:5, ISA 47:5; JER 47:5, JER 48:2, JER 51:55MAT 22:34; MRK 3:4; LUK 20:26 ACT 4:14; ROM 3:19

The silence of Jesus Christ

It was foretold in the OT

ISA 53:7 See also ACT 8:32

Its fulfilment in the NT

MAT 26:63 parallel MRK 14:61 before the Sanhedrin; ; MAT 27:14 parallels MRK 15:4–15:5, JHN 19:9 before Pilate; ; LUK 23:9 before Herod

Jesus Christ commands silence as a sign of his authority

MRK 1:25–1:26 parallel LUK 4:35 Jesus Christ silenced evil spirits; ; MRK 4:39 Jesus Christ silenced the storm.

There are times when it is appropriate for God's people to be silent

The silence of expecting God to act

JOS 6:10 See also GEN 24:21; EXO 14:14–14:15; 2KI 2:3, 2KI 2:5; REV 8:1

The silence anticipating the wisdom of another person

JOB 29:7–29:10, JOB 29:21

The silence of prudence

PRO 10:19; ECC 3:7 See also 1SA 10:27; JOB 13:5, JOB 33:31–33:33; PRO 11:12, PRO 17:28

The silence of suffering

LAM 3:28 See also PSA 39:9

The silence of shame

EZK 16:63

The silence of anger

PSA 4:4 The psalmist is warning against hasty action when angry.

The silence of amazement at God's actions

See also LUK 9:36; ACT 15:12

A tongues-speaker should be silent if no interpreter is present

1CO 14:28 silence in the church; ; 1CO 14:30 A prophet should be silent if another receives a revelation.

Christian women are sometimes exorted to be silent

1TI 2:11–2:12 See also 1CO 14:34–14:35; 1PE 3:1–3:4

There are times when it is inappropriate for God's people to be silent

When there is good news to tell

2KI 7:9; ; PSA 40:9

When much depends upon a person's words

EST 4:14 See also JER 4:19, JER 20:9; ACT 18:9–18:10

When God should be praised

PSA 30:11–30:12 See also LUK 19:37–19:40

When sin is unconfessed

PSA 32:3

When God's people feel they have a genuine complaint

PSA 39:1–39:2 See also JOB 7:11, JOB 23:16–23:17

When prayer is urgently required

ISA 62:6–62:7

God's people are sometimes brought to silence

JOB 31:34 Job fearing the crowd; ; EZK 3:26 Ezekiel as a judgment on Israel; ; MRK 9:34 the disciples when their pride was exposed; ; LUK 1:20 Zechariah because of his unbelief

Silencing the wicked

Believers pray that the wicked will be silenced

PSA 31:17–31:18; 1PE 2:23 See also PSA 143:12

Believers so live that the wicked may be silenced

TIT 2:8; ; 1PE 2:15

False teachers must be silenced

TIT 1:10–1:11 “the circumcision group” believed that in order to be saved it was necessary to be circumcised and keep the Jewish ceremonial law.

Death is compared to silence

See also PSA 94:17, PSA 115:17

title: 5951: slander
content:
False and malicious talk about others. It not only harms those against whom it is directed, but also brings ruin to those who propagate it.

Slander condemned

Slander is sinful

MRK 7:21–7:23 parallel MAT 15:19–15:20 See also JER 9:4–9:6; EZK 22:9; ROM 1:29–1:31; 2CO 12:20; 2TI 3:2–3:4

Slander is forbidden

LEV 19:16 See also EXO 23:1; PRO 3:30, PRO 10:18, PRO 12:22; EPH 4:31; COL 3:8; TIT 2:3, TIT 3:1–3:2; JAS 4:11; 1PE 2:1

Slander is destructive

PRO 16:27 See also PRO 11:9, PRO 26:28, PRO 30:10

Dealing with slander

Committing one's cause to God

PSA 120:1–120:2 See also PSA 12:1–12:7, PSA 31:14–31:20, PSA 64:1–64:4, PSA 69:6–69:21, PSA 109:1–109:5

Maintaining one's integrity

1PE 2:12 See also PSA 119:23; 1PE 2:15, 1PE 3:9, 1PE 3:15–3:17

Rejoicing in the Lord

MAT 5:11–5:12 See also ACT 5:41

Not listening to slander

1SA 24:9 See also PRO 17:4

Judgment upon slanderers

PRO 21:28 See also DEU 22:13–22:19; PRO 19:5, PRO 19:9, PRO 21:28; ISA 29:20–29:21, ISA 51:7–51:8; 1CO 6:9–6:10

Examples of slander

JER 18:18 See also GEN 39:7–39:20; 1KI 21:1–21:14 Naboth's vineyard; NEH 6:5–6:7; PSA 31:13, PSA 35:15–35:16, PSA 38:19–38:20, PSA 41:5–41:9; LUK 23:2; ACT 6:13–6:14, ACT 24:5–24:9; ROM 3:8; 3JN 1:9–1:10

The human reponse to painful and distressing life situations, especially those involving loss.

Sorrow caused by the trials of life

PSA 90:10 See also PSA 13:1–13:2, PSA 31:9; ECC 1:18, ECC 2:23; JER 20:18

Sorrow caused by fulfilling God's will

1PE 1:6 See also MAT 26:38; PHP 2:27

Sorrow caused by illness

ISA 38:2–38:3 See also PSA 6:1–6:7

Sorrow caused by childlessness

1SA 1:16

Sorrow caused by parting

ACT 20:37 See also MAT 17:23 the disciples' reaction to Jesus Christ predicting his death; LUK 22:45; JHN 16:6

Sorrow caused by bereavement

GEN 23:2; JHN 20:11 See also GEN 50:1; DEU 34:8; 2SA 19:2; LUK 7:12–7:14, LUK 8:52; JHN 11:33–11:35; ACT 8:2

Sorrow caused by national calamities

PSA 137:1 See also ISA 15:3, ISA 22:4; JER 22:10, JER 48:17; EZK 21:6, EZK 27:30

God and sorrow

God is close to those who grieve

PSA 34:18 See also PSA 10:14; ISA 53:4; JHN 11:35

God comforts the sorrowing

JER 31:13 See also ISA 35:10; LAM 3:32–3:33; JHN 16:20; 1TH 4:13–4:14; REV 21:4

Sorrow in response to human sin

The result of sinning

PSA 16:4 See also 1SA 2:33

Grief over the failure of others

2CO 2:4–2:5 See also GEN 34:7; 1SA 20:34; EZR 10:6; EZK 9:4; ROM 9:2; 1CO 5:2

Grief over one's own shortcomings

MAT 5:4 See also MAT 26:75; 2CO 7:9–7:11; JAS 4:9

Sorrow in response to God's judgment on human sin

LAM 1:5 See also NEH 1:4; JER 8:21, JER 10:19, JER 13:17, JER 14:2; EZK 21:6, EZK 21:12; AMO 5:16–5:17, AMO 8:10; MIC 1:8; ZEP 1:15; ZEC 12:10; MAT 8:12, MAT 24:30; REV 1:7

Jesus Christ's sorrow in response to human sin

LUK 19:41–19:42

The promise of final deliverance from sorrow

See also ISA 35:10; REV 21:4

title: 5953: stability
content:
The state of being in a firm or unwavering situation, whether emotional, political or personal. Stability is an important element of a settled life before God.

Stability in the life of faith

Stability for the believer is based on God's unchanging nature

DEU 32:4; PSA 103:19 See also 1SA 2:2; 2SA 22:32; JOB 25:2; PSA 62:2, PSA 89:2, PSA 93:2; ISA 26:4; MAT 7:24–7:27

Stability gives resistance to spiritual assault

1CO 16:13; COL 1:22–1:23 See also PSA 20:7–20:8, PSA 40:2; PRO 10:25; MAT 10:22; ROM 16:25; 1CO 15:58; 2CO 1:24; GAL 5:1; PHP 1:27, PHP 1:27; COL 4:12; 1TH 3:8; 2TH 2:15; HEB 6:19, HEB 10:23; JAS 1:23–1:25, JAS 5:8; 2PE 1:12

Stability depends upon firmness of faith

COL 2:5–2:7 See also PSA 57:7, PSA 119:5; ISA 26:3; EPH 3:17; HEB 3:14; 1PE 5:9–5:10

EPH 4:14 See also COL 1:28

Political stability

2SA 7:16; PRO 29:4 See also 1SA 13:13; 2SA 5:12; 1KI 2:12; PRO 16:12; ISA 16:5

title: 5954: strength
content: The quality of power and might which characterises God and his relationship to his creation. Human strength can lead to rebellion against God on account of a belief in human self-sufficiency.

title: 5955: strength, divine
content:
The strength of God is made known in creation and redemption and in his empowering of believers to live faithfully.

The revelation of the strength of God

In creation

ROM 1:20 See also JOB 38:4, JOB 38:8, JOB 38:12, JOB 38:31–38:33; PSA 68:34, PSA 104:1–104:3, PSA 104:32; ISA 40:12, ISA 40:25–40:26; JER 32:17; HEB 1:2–1:3

In providence

PSA 135:6 See also PSA 46:8–46:10, PSA 115:3; ISA 14:24, ISA 40:23; JER 27:5; DAN 4:35; ACT 17:26; EPH 1:11

In redemption

EXO 6:6; EPH 1:19–1:20 EXO 3:19–3:20; ; DEU 4:34, DEU 4:37; ; PSA 77:13–77:15; ; ISA 51:10; ; JER 32:21; DEU 3:24; ; 2SA 22:2–22:3 parallel PSA 18:1–18:2 David's song of praise for deliverance; ; PSA 98:1; ; ISA 59:1, ISA 59:16

In human weakness

2CO 12:9–12:10, 2CO 13:4 See also JDG 7:4–7:7; 1CO 1:25–1:27; HEB 11:34

In judgment

REV 6:15–6:17 See also PSA 89:10; ISA 63:5–63:6; EZK 20:33–20:35; HAB 3:12; 2TH 1:8–1:9; 2PE 3:7; REV 6:12–6:14, REV 18:8

PSA 27:1 See also PSA 27:3; JHN 10:28–10:29; ROM 8:28, ROM 8:31

title: 5956: strength, human
content:
All human strength derives from God. Among non-believers, strength may become a source of arrogant self-confidence, the oppression of others or rebellion against God.

The strength of the ungodly

Physical prowess

1SA 17:4–17:10 See also NUM 13:31–13:33

Intelligence

1CO 1:22 The Gentile world relies on fallen reason rather than revelation. See also ACT 17:19–17:21, ACT 17:32; COL 2:8

Political and military might

PSA 20:7 See also GEN 10:8–10:12; PSA 33:16; ISA 31:1, ISA 36:18–36:20

Prosperity

PSA 49:6 See also JER 49:4; LUK 12:18–12:19; 1TI 6:17

The ultimate futility of human strength

1CO 1:25 See also 2CH 32:7–32:8; PSA 49:17, PSA 146:3; ECC 5:15; ISA 30:1–30:3; LUK 12:20; 1CO 1:19–1:20, 1CO 2:6; 1TI 6:7; JAS 1:11

Negative consequences of human strength

Arrogant self-confidence

GEN 11:4 See also 1SA 17:41–17:44; PSA 52:1 Boasting betrays the source of people's confidence; ISA 36:8–36:9; DAN 4:30; LUK 18:9–18:12; GAL 6:13; PHP 3:3

Violence and oppression

PSA 52:7 See also GEN 4:23–4:24; EXO 1:11–1:14, EXO 5:10–5:14; JDG 6:2, JDG 6:6; PSA 37:14, PSA 73:3–73:8; ISA 5:8; JAS 5:4–5:6

The physical strength of some godly men

2SA 23:20 parallel 1CH 11:22 Benaiah; ; 1CH 11:20–11:21 Abishai; ; HEB 11:32–11:34

title: 5957: strength, spiritual
content:
In contrast to human strength, God is the source and supplier of all spiritual strength through which believers can do all that God asks.

God is the source of spiritual strength

God gives strength

EPH 6:10 See also JDG 16:3, JDG 16:6, JDG 16:18–16:20; PSA 68:35; ISA 40:29–40:31; LUK 24:49; ACT 1:8; EPH 3:16, EPH 3:20; 2TH 2:16–2:17; 1TI 1:12; 2TI 1:7

JOS 1:9 See also DEU 31:7–31:8; PSA 119:28; ISA 41:10; JER 1:8; HAG 2:4; 2TI 4:17

Strength comes from the realisation of his grace

2TI 2:1 See also ACT 20:32; 1CO 15:10; HEB 13:9

Strength comes through the Holy Spirit

ZEC 4:6–4:7 See also JDG 14:6; LUK 4:14; EPH 3:7, EPH 3:16

2CO 12:7–12:10 See also PSA 8:2; ACT 14:19–14:20; 2CO 4:8–4:12; COL 2:15; HEB 11:32–11:38

Profound dependence upon God

1SA 17:45 See also PSA 27:1, PSA 44:4–44:8, PSA 118:6; ISA 40:29–40:31; DAN 3:16–3:18; MAT 26:42; 1CO 1:31; GAL 6:14; HEB 13:6

Humility and gentleness

MAT 11:29 See also NUM 12:3; 1TH 2:6–2:8, 1TH 2:11–2:12

title: 5959: submission

A humble attitude where obedience is rendered within a relationship; whether it be to God, authorities or other people at work, in the church, in marriage or in the family.

God requires submission

From all people

PSA 2:9–2:11 See also JOB 22:21; 1PE 5:6

From Christians especially

MAT 6:9–6:10 See also HEB 12:9; JAS 4:7

The submission of Jesus Christ to his Father

The submissive spirit required in the church

In believers' relationships with one another

EPH 5:21 See also PHP 2:5–2:7

To Jesus Christ

EPH 5:24 See also EPH 1:22–1:23; COL 1:18 As the body is subject to the head, so the church is subject to Christ.

To the Scriptures

JOS 1:7–1:8 See also PSA 119:133; COL 3:15; JAS 1:22–1:25; REV 22:18–22:19

To church leaders

HEB 13:17 See also ROM 13:1; 1CO 16:15–16:16; 1TH 5:12–5:13

In prophecy

1CO 14:32 The implication is that individual prophecies must be submitted to the overall judgment of the church.

ROM 13:1 See also MAT 22:21 parallels MRK 12:17, LUK 20:25; ROM 13:2–13:7; TIT 3:1; 1PE 2:13–2:14

Of wives to husbands

EPH 5:22–5:24 See also COL 3:18; TIT 2:4–2:5; 1PE 3:1, 1PE 3:5–3:6

Of children to parents

title: 5976: visiting
content:
Calling to see a person or place. Examples include pilgrims to Jerusalem and those visiting family and friends. Visiting those in need, especially the sick and bereaved, is particularly important. Individuals and churches are encouraged and strengthened by visits from other believers.

Visiting particular people or places

Pilgrims visit Jerusalem

LUK 24:18 See also LUK 2:41; JHN 5:1, JHN 12:12; ACT 2:9–2:11, ACT 8:27–8:28

Visiting family, friends, etc

LUK 11:6 EXO 2:11; ; ACT 7:23; JDG 15:1; MAT 21:17; ; MRK 11:11; ; LUK 10:38–10:42; ; JHN 11:20; JHN 4:43–4:46 Jesus Christ visits his home region of Galilee.

Visits from foreign dignitaries

2CH 9:1 parallel 1KI 10:1–10:2 See also 2CH 18:2 parallel 1KI 22:2; 2KI 20:12–20:13 parallel ISA 39:1–39:2; JER 27:3

title: 5977: waiting
content:
Being in readiness for service or for some future appointment or event. Wild animals and the wicked lie in wait to ambush the unsuspecting; servants wait on their masters; believers and the whole creation wait for their renewal by God. God, too, waits for sinners to repent.

Waiting for future events

Waiting to see what happens

RUT 3:18; ; JON 4:5; ; ACT 28:6

Waiting for a period of time

GEN 8:10–8:12; ; LEV 12:4–12:5; ; EZK 44:26

Waiting for people

Waiting to meet others

EXO 5:20, EXO 7:15; ; 2SA 16:1; ; 1KI 20:38

Waiting to be joined by others

1CO 11:33 See also EXO 24:14; ACT 17:16, ACT 20:5–20:6; 1CO 11:21

Waiting for word from others

JOB 29:21–29:23 See also 1SA 10:8, 1SA 20:19; 2SA 15:28; LUK 3:15

title: 5978: warning
content:
Telling someone of coming disaster or danger or of the consequences of their action or attitude. Scripture gives strong warnings against idolatry, sin and false teaching.

title: 5979: waste
content:
The misuse and squandering of resources. God condemns the waste of resources which he provides, especially spiritual provisions such as grace and opportunity. Sometimes extravagance in God's service is mistaken for waste.

Waste of material resources

Squandering is folly

LUK 15:13–15:16 See also PRO 21:20, PRO 29:3; LUK 16:1; JAS 5:1–5:6; 1PE 4:3–4:5

As a consequence of yielding to temptation

PRO 29:3 See also PRO 5:7–5:14

Jesus Christ avoids waste

JHN 6:12–6:13

Spiritual resources should not be wasted

God's grace

JON 2:8 See also JHN 12:35–12:36; 2CO 6:1; GAL 4:9–4:11; HEB 10:26–10:29, HEB 10:35; 2PE 2:21

God-given abilities

MAT 25:14–25:30; ; LUK 19:12–19:27

Opportunities for service

EPH 5:16 See also JHN 9:4; GAL 6:10; COL 4:5

Spiritual teaching

MAT 7:6 Spiritual teaching is wasted if inappropriate to the spiritual capacity of the hearers. See also PRO 9:7, PRO 23:9; 1CO 2:14

Examples of wasted lives

Esau

Esau lived for the pleasures of the moment and threw away his spiritual inheritance: GEN 25:29–25:34; ; HEB 12:16

Samson

JDG 16:18–16:21 Though Samson did retrieve something at the end of his life, his spiritual gift of supernatural strength was largely wasted through his indulgence in sexual immorality.

King Saul

1SA 16:21; ; 2SA 1:17–1:27 Through natural strength and spiritual gifts Saul had the prospect of establishing a successful royal dynasty. The future was lost through disobedience and the end of his reign was wasted through jealousy.

Judas Iscariot

MAT 27:3–27:5 Judas had the best of opportunities--three years with Jesus Christ. This was thrown away in a moment of personal ambition.

Devotion to God is not waste

MAT 26:6–26:13 parallel MRK 14:3–14:9 See also JHN 12:1–12:8

Waste as the destruction of life and land

The frailty of human beings

JOB 13:28 See also JOB 33:21; PSA 32:3; LAM 4:9; 2CO 4:16

Waste as a result of the judgment of God

JER 34:22 See also LEV 26:31–26:33, LEV 26:39; NUM 5:21; DEU 28:22, DEU 29:23, DEU 32:24; PSA 106:43; ISA 24:1, ISA 24:3; EZK 4:17; HOS 5:9
